# Update log

## 2026-11-26
* **Fix**: **An area's name that begins with a space is listed first, as in Aurora** ([#54](https://github.com/jadzziaa/moonglow-toolset/issues/54); [Main Window](manual/02-main-window.md)). With List areas and blueprints by name, the Module panel and Edit Areas Together sorted by the name with its spaces trimmed, so the areas a builder names " Arrival" to have them at the top were listed among the rest. The space at a name's start is now kept for the order (the end's still trimmed); Setup Area Transition's Target Area list already kept it. Tests: `tree::an_area_named_with_a_leading_space_is_listed_first` and `areas::areas_together_keeps_a_leading_space_in_its_order` (both seen to fail first), and `transition_setup::the_target_areas_keep_a_leading_space`.
* **Fix**: **The sun's shadow plan takes the receivers' box as it goes, and the box around points is a plain loop** (mg-render; [deferred](deferred.md): the grass field's window frame entry given its bisect). A bisect of the grass field close up without grass (load 2.5 to 4) put +0.2 to 0.3 ms of the window's frame on b4da2984, the review's R20, beside a small step between 992ed8d2 and 27a4050c (+0.06) and 89e62b7f, the redesign's M3 shell (+0.11, Interface's). Temporary timers found it in the shadow plan, which runs on a thread beside the meshes' draws: it put `box_of` around the receivers' box so far and each receiving mesh's box, about 10,000 times a frame in the 32 by 32 field, and took 0.31 ms against the draws' 0.18, so the frame waited 0.18 ms at the join. The receivers' boxes are already known to be somewhere (a mesh that is nowhere is skipped before), so their box is now taken as it goes, as is the box of a light's shadow parts; `box_of` itself is a loop with a branch to each point, not a filtered fold, and still leaves out what is not finite. The plan's instance loop went from 0.29 ms to 0.20 with the loop and to 0.065 with both, the wait at the join from 0.18 ms to none (load 15 to 22, three rounds alternated); the idle line, develop and the fix alternated four rounds at load 15 to 16, 1.37 to 1.65 ms against 1.16 to 1.33. To be confirmed on a quiet machine. Tests: `the_box_around_points_leaves_out_what_is_nowhere` and `an_instance_that_is_nowhere_changes_no_shadow`, unchanged, pass. Confirmed on a quiet machine (load 2.8 to 4.8, six rounds alternated): the idle line 1.21 ms on develop, 1.04 to 1.06 with the fix, 0.84 before b4da2984.

The turning rings' lines are kept on screen while the view and the rings stand, the pointer's test rejects rings far from it by their squares' corners, and the pivots' dots are kept once by cells of half a point (not each against every other); these three are untimed quietly. **Select Texture's opening** 11.7 to 12.6 ms (from 27): the 135,094 names are sorted as 128-bit numbers (ResRef's order folds both names at every comparison); **a letter typed in its Find** 6.0 to 6.3 ms (from 6.4 to 9.6): Find looks among what the last filter found (`narrowing::Narrowing`, shared with Choose Image). **Select Portrait's opening** 4.8 ms with the install's table (from 9.9), 8.1 to 8.6 with 32,000 rows (from 18.8): the portraits' names are gathered in one walk of the layers (`images::Portraits`), not each row's five sizes looked up in every layer. **The Appearance page of 999 icons** stands each icon in a cell of the largest drawn yet, by the owner's ruling of 26 November ([manual](manual/05-blueprints.md) "Items"): the grid is in even lines and columns, which no longer change as it scrolls (icons in sight had their own sizes and those out of sight the first one's), and its lines out of sight are skipped whole, not each icon given its room (+145 µs at rest over the same with 142; not timed again, no quiet slot). * **New**: **An include's own `main` warned of, Moonglow's entry point kept** (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-26, "Compile: 1 (keep, warn)"; [deferred](deferred.md): the "41 changed" question settled; [Scripts](manual/07-scripts.md), [Command-line tools](manual/11-command-line.md), [findings](findings.md)). Aurora 8193.37's Build compiles a script whose include has a `void main()` of its own as that `main`: an `int StartingConditional()` script (which in the game then always fails as a condition) and a script that is only the `#include` (an include's `StartingConditional` too, for a script with none). Moonglow keeps compiling what was written, and now says so for each such script, in Compile All's log and `mg compile` (`warnings` in the JSON), and in the Compiler pane for a script compiled there: `lib.nss(3): WARNING: lib has a main of its own, which Aurora compiles as cond in place of its StartingConditional…`, or `…only has no main or StartingConditional of its own, so Moonglow compiles nothing for it. Aurora compiles lib's main as only`. The include-only script, passed over as an include, is read again for it (`Compiler::passed_over`). Tests: `return_types::tests::an_includes_entry_point_that_aurora_compiles`, `build::tests::an_includes_main_that_aurora_compiles_is_warned_of`, `compile::an_includes_main_is_warned_of` (mg), and `aurora_scripts::codegen_compiles_as_aurora_builds_it`, which holds the warned scripts to the three Aurora builds otherwise; the 992 base-game scripts of `aurora_scripts` warn of nothing new. * **Fix**: **Shiny water keeps its picture, and the water's copy holds the see-through meshes behind it** (mg-render; [deferred](deferred.md): "The Domains of Dread's fountain is 10.6 of 255 from the client" and "The framebuffer's copies" closed, one narrower entry and one Settled added, the shadows entry updated; [findings](findings.md), [the framebuffer proposal](framebuffer-proposal.md), [the shaders notes](research/notes_shaders.md), [Areas](manual/04-areas.md)). Read in the client with patched `fswater` programs: the fountain's basin floor and ttr01's shallow pool show through the client's water because it draws their DDS whole, where Moonglow's rippling procedure (2026-11-02) made a shiny water's DDS a flat opaque gray, which `fswater` takes as water nobody sees into. Shiny water (`bumpmaptexture shinywater`) now keeps its picture: the shallow pool darkens by 0.264 under a wall's shadow (the client's 0.26, 0.002 before), its region 3.2 of 255 from the client's (5.8 before); the fountain's basin shows its floor's pattern (4.25 against the client's 4.97, 1.19 before); a rural lake's far water 11.1 (17.5 before). The whole fountain's figure stays at about 9.7 of 255 (9.9 before): the rest of it lies outside the basin and was not broken down. Moonglow's own water (the Shaders switch off, or the game's water off) keeps drawing such a texture in the procedure's gray (`TextureEntry`'s `lost`): the shallow pool's pictures with the switch off are the same as before pixel for pixel. `copies::reading_copy_order` read what the client's copies hold: one copy a frame after the see-through meshes, read by shiny water and `sample_framebuffer` meshes; a solid or `transparency 1` mesh reading it gets the frame before's picture; particles a depth copy without the water. Moonglow now makes the copy after the see-through meshes' solid parts and draws its readers after it; the frame before's picture is not kept (no program the game or TDoD draws reads it so; 40 MB more at 3440×1440 a view). A soft see-through mesh in front of the water hides it in the client, as though it wrote its depth, where Moonglow lays its soft part over the water; drawing the soft parts before the copy was tried and laid the water over them, so it is filed in the deferred list. Frame cost: within the runs' spread but for one row left unresolved (three alternated `frame_perf` runs each, load 28 to 54: the water area's overview at 4x 2.24 / 2.28 ms lowest / median before, 2.26 / 2.36 after; TDoD's woods turned 9.66 / 9.93, 9.43 / 9.80; their overview at 4x 6.35 / 6.37 before, 6.51 / 6.87 after, at spreads of 0.6 and 0.45, not settled on a machine this loaded), and no memory more. Tests: `the_water_s_copy_holds_the_see_through_meshes_behind_it`, `moonglow_s_own_water_draws_a_lost_ripple_in_its_gray`, the shiny-water case of `the_rippling_procedure_s_picture_is_the_client_s`. Open entries 61 to 60 (two closed, one added).
* **Fix**: **A plugin's time budget counts only its own code, and only a job it stopped ran out of time** (mg-plugin; [Plugin API](manual/17-plugin-api.md) "Limits"). Windows CI (run 45754933913) reported a panel's "a panel only reads" as "it ran out of time" (250 ms). The deadline was set when the job's state was made, so Moonglow's own setup (the Lua machine, the sandbox, reading `main.luau`) counted; and a failure reported after the deadline was called a time-out though the code had raised it in time, the thread held up between. `start` now sets the deadline as the code starts to load, and the reports read what `out_of_time` recorded when it stopped the job, not the clock. The plugins tests on one CPU with 16 threads: the old code failed 1 run of 30 (another panel, the same relabeling), the fixed one 0 of 130. Tests: `runtime::tests::the_hosts_setup_is_not_the_jobs_time` and `an_error_reported_after_the_deadline_is_the_codes_own`.

## 2026-11-25
* **Fix**: **The game's draws set their zeros and group 1 only where another is bound** (mg-render; [deferred](deferred.md): the Shaders switch's water entry and "Small slowdowns the timing run of 10 November did not trace" narrowed to the grass field's window frame, the dense-area entry updated; [the frames note](research/notes_frames.md)). With the Shaders on, each of the game's draws set group 1 (bones, framebuffer copies, the mask) and the zero vertex buffer again: 5,514 binds of each a frame in TDoD's woods seen whole. Group 1 is now one bind group per kind, set where another is bound, and the zeros are bound once a slot until a skin takes it: about 11,000 commands and 1.0 ms of encoding less (both paths on alternate frames, three runs), the pictures identical pixel for pixel. `m_texture` and `skinmesh` are written as a draw's other values. What is left of the switch's cost in the woods is the game's programs themselves (a pipeline per material kind, two groups each, see-through runs by material across chunks); a chunk in their state and runs split by chunk were tried and dropped. The water's gap is about 0.3 ms now, not 0.9, inside the budget. Against 3.18.1 (the review's build), area092 turned is quicker; the woods turned with Moonglow's shader take about 1 ms more of the GPU, which is 6b26e702 (see-through runs by chunk), kept for the 1.5 to 2.4 ms of encoding it saves; the grass field close up takes 0.15 to 0.2 ms more of the GPU since dd8d0bc1 (grass taking the shadows through a mask, kept), and its window frame is slower too but did not bisect under the machine's load, left in the deferred list for a calm machine. `render_area` takes `MG_USER_DIR` for a module's haks and prints the encoding's time on the processor. Tests: `the_zeros_are_bound_again_after_a_skin_took_their_slot`, `a_draw_s_own_members_are_written_as_any_member_is` extended.
* **Fix**: **The editors' costs at the review's sizes, timed and five of them cut** ([deferred](deferred.md): the timing-view entry's editors line and its item 17 line closed, what is left named there). A new timing view, `frame_perf::editors_at_scale` (`FRAME_VIEW` picks its groups), builds the persistent world grown to 1,400 areas (3,000 placeables in one, a conversation of 20,000 lines, a creature, a 50,000-line talk table with a 20,000-line map, a claims table, a variables.toml) beside a small module of 4 areas, and times each view against its own rest in the same run. The line set beforehand: 70 µs of UI over the rest, or a frame past the 6.9 ms budget, is a cost to find. The figures after are three runs at a load of 11 to 17 (another program kept twelve cores busy all evening: the spreads are wide), lowest, then the spread, of the tree before the hak's Save job was given nothing (which changes only that view); the hak's are three runs of the final tree at a load of 21 to 23. Three runs of the final commit at a load of 30 to 39 settle nothing (its controls 1.5 to 2.4 times the quieter runs', every view's spread hundreds of µs, the typed line's text kept in the field as slow as its commit): its timing at a quiet load is filed as waiting on one ([deferred](deferred.md)):

TGAs stay compressed. The cost, in the campaign's areas with the most creatures: moonseabattle 156.7 MiB of textures (45.2 with PLTs compressed, 160.1 uncompressed), zhentkeepwar 35.2 (29.0), area092 21.2 (17.9). `frame_perf` gains `FRAME_AREAS`. Tests: the PLT row of `only_pictures_drawn_over_what_is_behind_are_compressed` and a colored copy in `a_texture_compressed_as_it_is_read_keeps_what_is_known_of_it`. * **Fix**: **Particles' pictures and additive textures are no longer compressed as they are read** (mg-render; [manual](manual/10-options.md), [the frames note](research/notes_frames.md)). Area026's floor showed green and magenta blotches around a placeable's glow with compression on: the glow is a Lighten emitter whose picture, `fxpa_lensflare`, is a white flare in pure grays, and BC1's 565 colors tint dark grays by a few levels, which many added particles sum into blotches; the best effort and BC3 kept them, leaving the picture uncompressed took them away. A particle's picture and a texture whose TXI says `blending additive` are now kept as stored: the crop matches the uncompressed build's in two runs, for 0.2 to 0.3 MiB more textures (area092 17.9 MiB of 31.2) and no longer opening (median 121 ms). Tests `only_pictures_drawn_over_what_is_behind_are_compressed` and two more kinds in `a_texture_compressed_as_it_is_read_keeps_what_is_known_of_it`.

* **Fix**: **An area is drawn again as soon as its last texture is read** (mg-render, mg-ui; closes the audit's "area's opening" item in [deferred](deferred.md); [the frames note](research/notes_frames.md)). Since 3.0.0 the picture waited for the animation's next 40 ms step after its textures were read: area092 was whole after 174 to 177 ms against v2.13.3's 102 to 110 (both tags built beside develop). It is now drawn at once: whole after 105 to 119 ms with RGBA8 textures and 112 to 160 compressed (medians 111 and 122, five runs each in turn). The model viewer reads its textures in the frame and never waited. Test `an_area_is_drawn_again_as_soon_as_its_textures_are_read`, seen failing without it.
* **Feature**: **TGA and PLT textures are compressed as they are read** (mg-image, mg-render; closes the audit's uncompressed textures item in [deferred](deferred.md); [manual](manual/10-options.md), [the frames note](research/notes_frames.md)). A picture read as RGBA8 (a TGA, a PLT's colored copy, a cutout or see-through texture) of 64 pixels or more becomes BC1, or BC3 where it has alpha, on the renderer's reader threads; maps, procedural textures and the UI's pictures stay as stored, and a GPU without BC keeps RGBA8. The encoder gained a quick effort and threads (4 to 6 ms a megapixel, from 72 to 192). Area092's textures went from 31.2 to 17.9 MiB, for about 10 ms more of its opening (no frame longer); TDoD's woods, all DDS, are unchanged. Shots with and without differ less than two runs do. Tests `a_texture_compressed_as_it_is_read_keeps_what_is_known_of_it`, `a_texture_read_as_rgba_is_compressed_by_its_alpha`, `the_quick_effort_stays_near_the_best`.

Grass receives the sun's, moon's and lights' shadows, and a see-through mesh of a tile or static placeable has its solid part drawn before they are laid; every darkening pass (Fast's and High's) also darkens a mask of the shadows beside the picture, which the soft parts, drawn after, multiply themselves by (Moonglow's shader by a flag of the draw; the game's programs through `Program::darken_by_mask` in their soft-part pipelines). Water takes none, as the client's; a shallow pool's floor, which the client shows darkened through the water, stays the fountain entry's ([deferred](deferred.md)). The mask is an R8 target of the view's size and samples (about 25 MB at 3440×1440 with four samples), kept while its frames have shadows; the GPU's frame takes 0.3 to 0.6 ms more in area084 seen close with Fast (1.03 to 1.41 ms before, 1.65 to 1.72 after) and no more with High (2.09 to 2.25, 2.02 to 2.33), and 0.1 to 0.45 ms more over the grass field (across it with Fast 2.09 to 2.38 before, 2.53 to 2.55 after), its views without grass 0.1 to 0.3 ms more (`frame_perf`, sun and creature shadows, three runs of each build in turn): within the budget. * **New**: **Custom Light flickers** ([deferred](deferred.md): "Lights placed on the fly, the flicker" closed; [proposal](lights-proposal.md) marked built; [manual](manual/04-areas.md#lights-of-any-color-and-reach)). The Custom Light section has **Flicker**: None, Candle, Torch, Fire or Pulse. A flickering light's model keys its light node's `color` over a short cycle (the brightness at even steps, the first again at the end) in its `default` animation, which the compiler carries into the binary model; its placeables.2da row is `Static` 0 and every placing of it (Custom Light, the palette's Lights, Add Light Here, a gallery drop) is dynamic and Plot (a dynamic placeable can be destroyed, a fireball takes placeables), as the client plays a dynamic placeable's `default` and holds a static one's still (2026-10-30). The section says the light is placed dynamic and that a dynamic placeable costs the game more. **Change Light…** sets the instance's Static (and Plot) with its row in one command. **Make Placeables Static** (and `mg areas --static-placeables`) leaves flickering lights dynamic, and says why. A steady light writes the same model, label and row as before, byte for byte (pinned in `lights::tests`). The area view plays the flicker (`a_flickering_custom_light_is_placed_dynamic_and_flickers_in_the_view`), and the server reads and places a flickering light from its hak (`engine_custom_light`). Not yet watched in the client.

A placeable's contents and a store's page select several (Ctrl, Shift) as a creature's inventory does. Onto a list all go in at their free places; onto a row of their own list they move before it; onto a creature's own backpack its slots' items come off into it. Onto a slot, the one the drag began on goes in it where it fits, else the first that does (Aurora's slot rules, the free primary and the feat question kept); the rest from another object go to the backpack after what the slot held, the creature's own stay; none fitting, nothing changes and the Log says so. Aurora selects one item, so there was nothing of its to match. Edit Together's Paste adds every item copied ("Paste 2 items"). The one difference is a script that includes a file with its own `void main()`: Aurora compiles a `StartingConditional` script as the include's `main`, which in the game always fails (`engine_include_entry`); Moonglow compiles the condition. Recorded in [findings](findings.md) and, waiting on the builder and the owner's ruling, [deferred](deferred.md). Tests `aurora_scripts` (three new) and `engine_include_entry`.
* **Update**: **The UI's per-frame costs, measured, one fixed** ([deferred](deferred.md): the Right Dock's entry and the placed sounds' item closed, the NUI Creator's narrowed to its two walks, the timing-view entry one view shorter; 80 entries and 117 items to 79 and 116). Timed in release with timers around each suspect, not left in; 70 µs a frame (1% of the 144 fps budget) set beforehand as the line between "fix" and "left as is".
  - **The NUI chart:** a series of a million samples was kept by a SipHash of every value: 3.7 ms of each frame (`nui_perf`'s idle frame 4.4 ms, not the 28.5 the entry still gave). A multiply and rotate a value takes 1.3 ms (the idle frame 2.0 ms) and still changes with any one value changed. A new test changes one value in place, in the window and in a bind, and sees the line drawn anew. The walk itself (1.3 ms, for columns too) stays in the narrowed entry: the window is edited in place, with no cheaper sign of a change.
  - **An area's placed sounds read from its GIT each frame:** 58 µs a frame for the campaign's area with the most placed sounds (317); it grows with their count. Left as is.
  - **The area's Right Dock layout and tab lists:** about 6 µs a frame together with the default layout, 9 µs with a builder's own (`frame_perf`'s Sound Ranges views). Left as is.
  - **The NUI Creator's lesser copies:**
    - `check` costs 0.3 µs on an idle frame: it copies only when the bytes change.
    - Interact's two comparisons cost 13 µs at 96 controls and 47 µs at 304.
    - The variant's context document costs 277 µs a frame at 304 controls. A cache would compare (about 95 µs) and clone its output for the canvas (168 µs), so it saves nothing unless the canvas borrows it. It stays in the narrowed entry, with the figures.
  - **A new view, the Design page of 304 controls and a list bound to 1,000 rows** (`nui_perf`'s `three_hundred_controls_and_a_bound_list`, the review's N13): 0.98 ms an idle frame.

* **Fix**: **A change to the game data asked for while something still reads it is made once it is free, and said** (issues #49 and #50, reported on 4.2.1). Close, open, the module layer after edits, before jobs and on Save, Module Properties' haks, the bake's rows, the custom talk table, Reload Resources and the game data's tables did nothing, silently, when something still held the game data after `release_game_data`'s ten-second wait (#50: the closed module's haks stayed layered and the next one's were never added; `use_module` alone said so). Each now asks `Moonglow::game_free_for`: still held, or with a change waiting already (so a stuck holder is waited for once, not by every change after it: New Module had waited 30 s for one), what it would have done is marked in `GameWaits`, the log says once what waits, the Status Bar says *Waiting for the game data to be free…*, and `make_waiting_game_changes` (each frame, after `poll_job`, never waiting) makes it from what the window has once the data is free: the open module's haks and resources layered in their order, the last module's gone, the talk table read again, and what was drawn or read from the old layers forgotten (the area views read again). `use_module` forgets the drawn textures after `stack_onto` too. `release_haks`, needed before its project command runs, is not kept for later: it says that the haks stay open. #49's 10-second Save fits 4.2.1's Placeable Wizard keeping the game data's `Arc` in egui's memory (`kept_for`, replaced by `kept_for_key` in 5.2.0): `game_data_holders::only_the_window_holds_the_game_data_once_it_lets_go` walks the surfaces a builder uses with an area open (palette, Placeable and Creature Wizards, Appearance Gallery, a script, a creature's and an item's Properties, Save, New Module) and finds no holder on 5.3.0 without a GPU; with that holder put back it fails as the issue reads (Save 10 s, "shared by 1 other"). `a_module_opened_while_the_game_data_is_held_has_its_haks_once_it_is_free` (a job holding the data). GPU tests written, run by the session that may use the GPU: `game_data_holders::gpu::` (Save during texture reading and the first area reading, a gallery making pictures, and module A's red hak textures then B's blue drawn blue, also opened while held). `RELEASE_WAIT` is unchanged ([Modules](manual/03-modules.md)).
* **Fix**: **`mg serve` reports `ready` from every read of the server's console.** The `ready` event was raised only inside the serving loop; the two last reads (after the server exited, and after it was stopped) passed its lines on as `console` alone, so a module that loaded after `--timeout` (a loaded machine) was never reported as ready, and `serve::a_module_is_served_until_a_line_of_its_log` once failed for it. One helper (`console_events`) now turns a console line into its events in all three places, and `drain_console` does the last reads (`a_load_said_after_the_loop_is_still_ready`); that test's `--until "never said"` step waits 10 s, not 2 ([Command Line](manual/11-command-line.md)).
* **Fix**: **Text typed as a job began was lost to the job's write.** A job (a plugin's command or event) reads the module as it was when it began; text typed in a field and not yet set (held until the field is left) was not in it. The job's window then took the field's keyboard, the typing was set as a step of its own, and the job's write (the journal written whole, in CI's flaky `journal_factions::typed_text_follows_its_entry_through_a_whole_write`) replaced it from the module before. A job that reads the module now sets what is typed first (`Moonglow::set_held_text`, shared with Pop In Properties); the test's plugin takes long enough for its window to take the keyboard, and fails without the fix.

Down from the hak editor's, the tileset editor's and the Appearance Gallery's Find gives their list the keys at its first row (scrolled into sight; from the hak's More popover too, which closes); the hak and tile tables are outlined while they have them. The tileset palette and the Prefabs list have a cursor and the outline: Up, Down, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End over the rows as drawn (a closed heading's rows are not among them), Left and Right close and open a heading or go out and in, Enter does what a click does (a brush chosen, a heading opened or closed, a prefab placed); a click or F6 gives them the keys, and none act behind a dialog, menu or popover. The Status Bar says the keys after the area's own hints. One cursor for both lists, `palette_view::FlatList`. [Scripts](manual/07-scripts.md); [the main window](manual/02-main-window.md): floating windows' Maximize, pane sizes, renamed menu items and groups; [Journal](manual/08-journal-and-factions.md); [Modules](manual/03-modules.md): recovery's Confirm Discard, Check All and Choose N Areas…; [Options](manual/10-options.md); [Conversations](manual/06-conversations.md); [Blueprints](manual/05-blueprints.md); [NUI Creator](manual/18-nui-creator.md); [Getting started](manual/01-getting-started.md)), and "tick" made "check" throughout, as the interface now says. * **Fix**: [The UI redesign](ui-redesign-proposal.md)'s M5, **W6, second fix round** (reviewer D, item 5): the picture decode pool.
  * **A thread that died no longer stays counted.** `catch_unwind` is gone. A decode that panics ends its thread, and the thread's `Worker` guard gives up its place in its drop, however the thread ends. If jobs are still waiting, a new thread takes its place (`viewers::staff`). Before, a dead thread would never have been taken off the count, and after four panics every later picture would have waited for ever.
  * **The picture in sight goes first.** A picture drawn while its decode waits is moved to the front of the window's queue (`DecodesShared::hurry`), ahead of the tabs restored behind it.
  * **Memory ordering of the decode count.** `pending` is taken down with `Release`, after the picture is stored and `stored` is set, and read with `Acquire`, before `stored` (`Decodes::busy`). So a frame that sees the count at 0 also sees `stored`, and runs one more frame to make the texture. With relaxed ordering on both, the two could be seen in either order, and `settle` could stop a frame early. `stored` itself stays relaxed: the `Release`/`Acquire` pair on `pending` orders it.
  * **Test hooks:** `viewers::fail` now adds keys and `viewers::heal` removes them. **New tests:** `read_only::the_window_decodes_on_after_decodes_that_panic` (five panicking decodes, then a good picture is decoded), `read_only::a_picture_let_go_of_before_its_turn_is_not_decoded` (the skip of a picture let go of before its turn, which no test covered before) and `read_only::the_picture_in_sight_is_decoded_before_hidden_ones`. Breaks B19 to B21 in `target/m5/W6/breaks.txt`.
* **Fix**: [The UI redesign](ui-redesign-proposal.md)'s M5, **W8, second fix round** (review D) and the owner's ruling "fit: b" (2026-11-22). This corrects the first round's W8 entry above (2026-11-21): its fit is not yaw-free at every tilt, and "the long table about 15%" smaller is no longer true.
  * **Turning, and the owner's ruling.** Review D found that the first round's fit, made for every yaw, held only at the pitch it was framed at: in a wide picture a vertical drag carried the 6 m plank out. A fit for every pitch too was built and measured. It made the commoner fill 0.64 of the tall Preview's height (the Creature board asks 0.8) and the long table 0.73 as big in a wide picture. The owner ruled "fit: b": every yaw at the pitch the view is framed at. Tilt is not fitted, so a steep tilt can carry a long model past a wide picture's edges. That is the ruling, so it has no deferred entry. `model_view::Fit` is the first round's fit, made once.
  * **Sizes** against the first round's: 1.00 for the wagon, long table, obelisk and commoner, tall and wide (the long table is no longer smaller at the first yaw; `target/ui-mock/impl/m5-w8/fit-b/`). The manual's two sentences now say the model stays whole as the view turns about it.
  * **The refit's cost.** A picture of another shape (a dock dragged wider) is framed anew from what Frame kept (`ModelView::refit`), not from the model's points read and skinned again (review D: about 1.7 ms for 50,000 points, every frame of a drag). A model's file read again drops what was kept. The two timings (making the kept fit, and fitting a shape from it) are owed at the release gates (the machine's load allowed none).

  * **The read-only tab**: a row's menu copies the value itself (Copy Value), a localized string's text or StrRef by name, all its languages, the meaning beside a number; Shift+F10 opens it from the keyboard and Ctrl+C copies a focused row's value. A value that means none has nothing beside it, as `mg gff --names`; a string of the module's talk table says it was not read, or shows its text. The Status Bar says a floating read-only tab's resource and size, and the lock's tip does where the header shows the lock alone. Copy to Module takes the copy shown (a hak's), and is off for a kind a module kept as files cannot hold.
  * **Options**: Enter while Keyboard waits for a key is that key, Escape gives up the waiting alone; Questions stand beside their dropdowns at the board's width, the minutes field without arrows; OK applies and writes once, Cancel, Escape and × set every page back.
* **Feature**: OpenGL (Moonglow Client's asks A9 to A11; the note is `.agdb/knowledge/renderer-on-wgpus-opengl-back-end-three-causes-and-their-gua.md`). The renderer draws on wgpu's OpenGL back end as on the others, its three causes found and guarded. The depth buffer is read as a float texture where a program reads it by the texel. The values of a draw and of a light are laid out as std430 in mg-shader's `layout` module, and `split_uniforms` refuses a program OpenGL would read otherwise (7 of the 65 stock programs had differed). One sample a pixel on OpenGL (`Gpu::samples`; no anti-aliasing there). The render tests pass 93 of 93 on OpenGL on Mesa radeonsi, from 53. The causes are guarded without OpenGL too: Moonglow's own shaders and every game program as the renderer splits it are written in GLSL as wgpu's OpenGL back end has naga write them. [The manual](manual/13-troubleshooting.md) says OpenGL is still not among the backends offered; [the deferred list](deferred.md) keeps what is open (other vendors, Windows, GLES, offering it, anti-aliasing).
* **Feature**: mg-area for a game client (A1, A2, A4). The editing half is the feature `edit` (default on; mg-edit and mg-module only with it), the items it needed moved to mg-rules and mg-tiles and re-exported. `mg_area::values` builds an area from values (tiles by id, turn and height, lights, flames and loops, the lighting, the grass, objects by kind with where they stand and their look) and `AreaModel::from_values` settles what is out of range; `AreaModel::read` goes through it, and every installed area reads the same as before. An area's scene follows a client's objects: a move needs no update (`AreaObject::move_to`), objects added at the end of the list are shown alone, `AreaScene::remove_object` takes one out, and the example `client_objects` shows it.
* **Feature**: mg-preview for a game client (A3): a creature's looks as values (`DressedLook`, `ItemLook`, `VisualTransform`), drawn by `dressed_look`, which a blueprint and a client's values both go through. `values::Look::creature` takes a `DressedLook` or a bare creature look and applies no wear check (that stays the reader's, `from_utc_as_the_game`); `Look::read` is unchanged.
* **Feature**: mg-render for a game client: `Camera::game` (A5) and `mg_render::present` (A6), a `Presenter` that puts the targets' picture into a window's surface texture and a `Screen` that does the surface's chores (format, present mode, configure on resize, outdated or lost), with the example `examples/window.rs`. The crate `mg-testkit-gpu` (A7) holds the GPU hold alone; mg-testkit re-exports it.
* **Update**: Moonglow Client's mc-scene was accepted on these APIs, ported in a scratch copy (it builds without mg-edit, mg-module and mg-script and draws the same pictures); the note says what its creatures lost to the wear check before and how the port was proved. The example count in CLAUDE.md is corrected, and [the plan](PLAN.md)'s crate table and [the deferred list](deferred.md) follow.
* **Update**: The fog at night (Moonglow Client's upstream ask A8). The client's fog start follows its camera's distance from the player: fogStart = min(30 − FogAmount − (20 − d), FogClipDist − 1), read back for cameras from 5.5 to 25 m (`night_fog.rs` `fog_start_follows_the_camera`). Earlier readings all had the 20 m entry camera. `mg_area::fog_from` and `View::camera` give it; the area view fogs nearer when zoomed in under 20 m. `night_fog_matches_the_client` draws night areas with clip 22 and 45 beside the client, the ground within 0.6 of 255 on both paths. Updated findings.md (Fog), research/notes_shaders.md (F), the manual's Areas chapter, and the Area Lighting and Render Distance wiki corrections.

## 2026-11-12
* **Fix**: [The UI redesign](ui-redesign-proposal.md)'s M3, T9's review: an area's (or another module resource's) modified dot shows at once as it changes and is checked against the saved module only once the change has rested, never during a drag, so an edit's frame no longer pays for it; the saved copies kept for that check are let go of when the module is saved, the resource deleted or its tab closed, and can no longer be mistaken for data saved later. A 2DA tab sent behind another while its description was being looked for no longer keeps the window busy for good (a test that failed now and then). Split Editor's tip says "Move the tab in front to another editor group". The drop targets of a tab being dragged are drawn light again, readable over a toolbar. The record of the editor groups is described as Moonglow 4.1.0 reads it: two groups come back as they were, three or more as groups split off the middle, every tab kept ([the main window](manual/02-main-window.md#tabs-and-windows)).
* **Feature**: [The UI redesign](ui-redesign-proposal.md)'s M3, T9, **document tabs and editor groups**: each tab of the editor area (and of a floating window) shows its kind's icon, its name and a dot where what it shows has unsaved changes (the " *" is gone from tabs; an area, conversation, blueprint or Module Properties changed since the module was saved has the dot too, and loses it when saved or undone back), and a close button on the tab in front and the one under the pointer, its room kept so the name does not move; a screen reader says the tab's name and "modified". **Split Editor** (the button at the right end of the focused group's tab bar, View › Split Editor, Ctrl+\\) moves the tab in front to an editor group of its own at the right; the docks and the tab keys (Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl and a digit, Ctrl+W) follow the focused group; a group whose last tab closes goes; the groups are kept with the module's open tabs (each as `split right 500`, as 4.1.0 reads it, and three or more in their order). A crowded tab bar cuts its titles alike (their whole names in their tips), then scrolls, keeping the tab in front in sight. The main pane's tab bars have no arrow and no close-all button any more (Close All is on the tab menu); a floating window's keep them (egui_dock patched, `vendor/egui_dock/MOONGLOW.md`). A tool left alone in the editor area takes it whole, as any group does ([the deferred list](deferred.md) entry of issues 11 and 20 loses that item) ([the main window](manual/02-main-window.md#tabs-and-windows), [where things moved](ui-redesign-moves.md), [the parity checklists](parity/checklists.md)).
* **Feature**: Setup Area Transition now leads to area transition triggers as Aurora's does ([the findings](findings.md), "Setup Area Transition with triggers"). It lists them and draws them on the map, offers Aurora's Connection Type (Both Ways, Current To Target, Target To Current), and makes the `WP_<tag>` waypoint at the middle of the trigger's box, with both ends and the waypoints written in one undoable step. What it writes matches Aurora's captures field by field (`aurora_transitions.rs`, eleven steps), and the deferred entry "Setup Area Transition's Connection Type" is closed. It differs from Aurora on purpose in four ways, listed in the [manual](manual/12-differences.md): it reuses a waypoint already inside the trigger's box, writes Target To Current's other end, writes everything on the window's OK, and shows lines instead of questions.
* **Fix**: Area transition triggers are now saved as Aurora saves them and kept where the game shows them ([the findings](findings.md), "When the client shows an area transition"): the game client shows a transition under the pointer, and takes a click on it, only when its corners run counterclockwise and lie on the ground. Outlines that are drawn, made as Alt rectangles or redrawn are saved counterclockwise from the westernmost corner, and Redraw Polygon puts the trigger at height 0. A trigger dragged, moved by the arrows or Adjust Location, or pasted has its corners put back on the ground, and choosing Trigger Type Area Transition also sets the transition cursor. Verify's new `transition-hidden` (a warning, with a fix that does what Redraw Polygon does) finds transitions saved clockwise, which the game never shows, and transitions left at another level, more than 1 m off the walkable ground, which it may not show: nearer than that the game's answer depends on the place, and the game's own transitions 0.23 to 0.31 m off are shown (`transition_outlines.rs`), so it finds nothing in the game's own modules.
* **Fix**: Q or E pressed while the selection was dragged (moved, raised with Alt or slid along an arrow) stopped the toolset once the drag went on more than 0.6 s after the key: 4.1.0's crash in a builder's two reports from Windows ("cannot convert float seconds to Duration: value is negative"), which had been put down to moving a placeable across raised tiles (63 drags across such edges did not reproduce it). The view asked for a frame when the keys would rest, 0.6 s after the key less the time since; while the drag held the turn back, that wait went negative. Now a drag asks for no such frame (the turn is part of the drag's command, made as the button is let go, with the pointer moved since or not: one step of Undo), and Escape with the pointer led off the view drops the turn with the drag (it had become a Rotate of its own). The waits worked out from the time (Ctrl + wheel scaling's rest, the area's animation steps, the open tabs' record) go through one helper that asks for no frame for an elapsed, odd or endless wait (`jobs::wait`, `jobs::repaint_in`); the other timers in the UI were read and are constants or saturate. [Areas](manual/04-areas.md) says what Q and E do during a drag. Tests: the crash reproduced in the UI test harness for a move, a lift and a slide (and on the `v4.1.0` tag), let go without moving, Escape over and off the view, E before the drag, the helper's negative, NaN and infinite waits; the existing drag-and-turn test had slept 0.7 s, which the harness's clock never saw, and now moves the clock on.

## 2026-11-11
* **Change**: With [Exact Tile](manual/04-areas.md) chosen, a press on an object (or a handle of the selection) picks the object: a click selects it and a drag moves it, the brush staying chosen; over an object no tile is previewed and the status line says the press goes to the object. A press on bare ground paints as before, and a stroke begun there paints over objects' tiles. An object hidden, locked or behind a raised tile doesn't take the press. The owner's ruling, after a builder's report showed a press-drag on a placeable painting the tile under it; the plain tile and the groups followed on 2026-11-12, the painting brushes unchanged. Beside a raised tile with no cliff face, an object let go over the open gap goes to what is seen through it, as before (ruled: kept).
* **Update**: [The UI redesign](ui-redesign-proposal.md)'s M3 (the shell) planned in detail: sixteen tasks (T0 to T15) in three merge points (M3a the frame, M3b editors in the shell, M3c widths, Outliner and hints), with how today's shell is built, the architecture decisions checked against the code, where the documents disagree, the decided choices and five rulings, which the owner ruled the same day as recommended (Escape cancels a docked tab that has OK and Cancel, the tree keeps its areas' objects beside the Outliner, plugin panels follow the Open editors switch, the Toolbar buttons setting stays until M4, and panels are fixed to their docks).
* **Update**: The size-up's classification difference between `mg model info` and `mgv decompile` is not one. On the 11 compiled models it named (`pnl_chr_deity`, `wswss_m_032` and nine others) the classification byte is 0, `mg model info` says `other`, and `mgv decompile` 0.3.0 writes no `classification` line, which the game reads as 0 too; the `character` came from the Python reader the size-up ran on the decompiled text, which took a model without the line as a character. The game's own text models that declare `classification gui` (323 of them) are `other` as the game compiles them (nwn-mdl-spec MDL-ASCII-021, `zspec_cls_gui`): of the game's 25,597 compiled models every byte is 0, 1, 2, 4 or 8. A test holds mg-mdl's names to that table, and the manual says what `other` is.
* **Fix**: `mg model info` says which of a text model's faces the game's compiler leaves out. A size-up found five models converted from another game where it counted 2 to 10 faces fewer than their text declares, and said nothing of it. Each face it left out has two corners at one place with one UV and one normal, so once the vertices are merged (as the game merges them) two corners are on one vertex, and the game deletes such a face (nwn-mdl-spec MDL-MESH-020, its `zspec_merge` golden): 19 faces in all, every one of the differences, and none of the rows had a repeated index, an index past the vertices or a missing value. The count was right; it is now said: `faces_left_out` (`--json`) and a `Left out` line, 0 for a compiled model, and the reader's own notes (faces past the vertices, rows missing) with their lines, which `mg model info` had not shown. Zero-area faces whose coincident corners keep apart (another normal or UV) stay, as in the game. nwnmdlcomp, which merges no vertices, keeps all 19.
* **Fix**: `mg ls --sha256` and `mg cat --to` run four to five times faster (the hash alone six): a 1.5 GB hak (21,028 entries) in 0.71 s, where 4.1.0 took 3.7 s, and 8,165 resources from the load order with three haks (1.4 GB) in 0.9 s against 3.7 s with `mg cat --to` writing them (0.7 s against 3.8 s with `--dry-run`, which hashes and writes nothing). The time was all in the hash, mg-core's own software SHA-256 (about 410 MB/s): listing the same hak without hashes takes 0.02 s, and the hash's rate was the same on one large entry as on many small ones. `mg_core::sha256` keeps its API and is now the `sha2` crate's (0.11, pure Rust, MIT or Apache-2.0), which uses the processor's SHA instructions where it finds them at run time (x86-64's SHA-NI, ARMv8's SHA2, which every Apple silicon Mac has) and its own software rounds elsewhere (about 2.5 s for that hak, measured here with them forced). Nothing is chosen at build time: one binary runs on every processor of its platform. The output is the same bytes: `mg ls --sha256` (text and `--json`) on four haks and ERFs of a builder's module (49,759 entries), and `mg cat --to --dry-run --json` on the 8,165, compared with 4.1.0's. Plugins' and updates' hashes are the same function.
* **Update**: [The UI redesign](ui-redesign-proposal.md)'s M2, its frame times measured against `develop` on a quiet machine (the median view 0.04 ms more, no view across the budget either way), and the hand-run timing tests' clicks fail where a control is not found (one had stopped at the tree's Clear Filter, renamed in M2).

* **Fix**: The hak editor closes after a file was added to its hak (a builder's report on 4.0: "the editor refuses to close. Every attempt & method to close the editor results in either the 'you have unsaved files' prompt or nothing at all"). Closing Moonglow's window with only a hak, 2DA or tileset changed asked the module's question ("Save changes to the new module?" with none open, or a clean module's name, whose Save wrote the module); it now asks the editor's own question by its name, as File › Exit and File › Close do. Once those questions were answered, the Exit, Close or window's X they were asked for was dropped, with "then do that again" in the log: it now goes on (`Moonglow::side_then`, carried on by `side_doc::closing_window`; Cancel drops it). The module's **Don't Save** dropped a changed hak with it unasked: each changed document is now asked of by its name, in turn, then what was asked for is done. A save that failed (the added file gone from disk by the time of the save, as a file dragged out of an archive tool's temporary folder is, or a folder that can't be written to) said why only in the log, and its question came back for ever, or the editor's OK did nothing to be seen: why is now said in the question and under the editor (`Moonglow::side_failed`, for a hak, a 2DA, a tileset and the talk table), for as long as the document has unsaved changes (one made clean by Undo or Remove says nothing more, and the reason does not come back with a later change), and the OK asks the tab's question, with Save again, Don't Save and Cancel. The module's own question had the same fault: its Save failing (a place that can't be written) did nothing to be seen and dropped the Exit; it is now asked again, saying why under it (`Moonglow::module_failed`). A side editor's document no longer outlives its tab: File › Close lets the clean ones go with their tabs, a module opened (its kept tabs put back too) leaves the side editors that are open as they are, documents and tabs (a hak opened in the same frame as the module included: `run_actions` keeps the rest of its batch where that check sees it), and a changed one left by a way that does not ask (the second step of New Module or of a `.mod` with a folder beside it) gets its tab back (`Moonglow::side_docs_follow_tabs`); one left without a tab counted as unsaved work for ever, and the window would not quit. Pictures before and after with `screens.rs`' `hak_closing_questions`. The test `every_way_of_closing_a_hak_with_a_file_added` closes a hak by every route (the tab's ×, its window's ×, Close Tab, Ctrl+W, OK, Cancel, Escape, the window's X, File › Exit and File › Close) with every answer, over 559 cells, and holds each to the fixed behavior (238 deviated before the fix); with `quitting_asks_of_each_changed_document_in_turn`, `a_failed_save_says_why_and_the_exit_waits_for_it`, `the_editor_says_why_its_save_failed`, `a_reason_goes_once_the_hak_is_clean`, `the_talk_table_says_why_its_save_failed`, `the_module_s_question_says_why_its_save_failed`, `side_documents_follow_their_tabs`, `a_hak_opened_with_a_module_keeps_its_document` and `a_2da_and_a_tileset_ask_by_name_at_quit`; `a_game_table_is_edited_as_a_copy` now expects a 2DA of its own file to go with its tab once saved, and to stay with it while changed. Escape over the editor still does nothing (it cancels Properties windows), and Exit under the running Save Hak job is still refused. [The main window](manual/02-main-window.md) and [Modules](manual/03-modules.md) say it.
* **Fix**: A WAVE holding MP3, and other forms of music and sounds the game plays, now play (a builder's report, his file not yet seen: "Wav file format isn't accepted by Moonglow. This can cause issues when custom music files are used, as sometimes they're just .wav files that have had their filename changed to .bmu so NWN will read them (NWN is fine with .wav when renamed to .bmu)"). Moonglow already told a sound's format from its bytes and decoded every PCM, float and ADPCM WAVE. What it refused was a RIFF WAVE whose `fmt ` format tag is 0x55 (MPEG layer 3), which is what the builder's files must be if the game plays them, with "unsupported feature: wav: unsupported wave format" in the log (`Sound NAME: ...`) or in red in the hak editor's View; and three more forms the game plays: an MP3 behind an ID3v2 tag of a mebibyte or more ("no suitable format reader found"), an MP3 with zeros or junk before its first frame ("not a sound the game plays"), and a WAVE whose RIFF size is 0 or too small ("invalid riff length", "chunk length exceeds parent"). What the game plays was read in its client (Linux build 26c6e573) by the new hand-run test `client_audio` ([the findings](findings.md#what-the-game-plays-as-music-and-as-sounds)); `tools/nwclient/run-client.sh` has an opt-in, `MG_CLIENT_AUDIO_OUT`, which writes all the client plays to a WAV file (OpenAL Soft's `wave` backend, still no audio device). Music plays a `.bmu` holding MP3, with the `BMU V1.0` header or without, behind ID3v2 tags, zeros or junk, and an MP3 in a RIFF WAVE; it is silent on every PCM and ADPCM WAVE and finds no `.wav`. An ambient sound plays PCM and ADPCM WAVEs, also with a RIFF size of 0 or 36, and is silent on any MP3 under `.wav`. `PlaySound` plays `.wav` only. In `mg-audio` (so the area view's Music, Ambient and Sounds, the Play buttons of the sound editor, conversations and sound sets, and the hak editor's View have it): an MP3's first frame is found (`find_mp3`: ID3v2 tags skipped, then the first frame header that a second one confirms, up to a mebibyte on), a WAVE holding MP3 is read from its `data` chunk, a WAVE's RIFF size is not believed, and what is still refused says what it is (`an RF64 WAVE, which the game does not play`; `a WAVE of a format Moonglow does not play (format 0x0050, MPEG layer 1 or 2)`, Windows Media Audio, AAC and Ogg Vorbis named likewise); `mg_audio::container` now returns the range of bytes that are audio. Of 130 ffmpeg-made files of a scratch matrix, 15 changed from refused to decoded or to a clearer refusal, none the other way; the install's sounds still all decode and agree with ffmpeg. Moonglow still plays the forms the game is silent on and says so in the log, once per file and role, by the owner's ruling of 2026-11-11: a WAVE under `.bmu` as music, a music track that exists only as `.wav`, an MP3 under `.wav` as an ambient sound, a WAVE under `.bmu` as an ambient sound, and a sound that exists only as `.bmu` (a Play button, a placed sound); the hak editor's View marks a WAVE under `.bmu`, which the game plays in no role; music now looks for the `.bmu` first, as the game does, so with both files it plays the `.bmu`; a WAVE cut short in its data is played without a word; Verify reads no sound's bytes and checks no music row. Not determined: placed sound objects, stereo by `PlaySound`, the Windows and macOS clients. Tests: in `mg-audio` `mp3_in_the_forms_the_game_plays_decodes`, `mp3_inside_a_wave_decodes_from_its_data_chunk`, `mp3_in_a_wave_streams_what_decode_gives`, `a_wave_with_wrong_sizes_decodes`, `finds_where_the_mp3_starts`, `frame_lengths_follow_the_headers`, `what_moonglow_does_not_play_is_refused_by_name`, `cut_or_garbled_mp3_forms_are_answers_not_panics` and `noise_that_looks_like_frames_is_quick_to_refuse` (23 in all); `custom_music_kept_as_mp3_in_a_wave_named_bmu_plays` (the report's path: the area's Music plays it), `custom_music_kept_as_a_pcm_wave_named_bmu_plays_and_warns_once`, `custom_music_kept_as_a_wav_plays_and_warns`, `custom_music_with_a_bmu_and_a_wav_plays_the_bmu`, `a_pcm_wav_plays_as_an_ambient_sound_without_a_warning`, `an_mp3_under_wav_plays_as_an_ambient_sound_and_warns_once`, `a_wave_under_bmu_plays_as_an_ambient_sound_and_warns`, `a_preview_of_a_sound_that_is_only_a_bmu_plays_and_warns_once` and `custom_music_that_is_not_a_sound_does_not_play_and_the_log_says_why`; in `mg-ui` `audio` `the_game_is_silent_where_the_client_was`, `music_looks_for_the_bmu_first` and `the_messages_are_one_sentence_each`; `a_hak_editor_views_a_wave_named_bmu_and_marks_it`; `verify_says_nothing_of_pcm_music_and_sounds_kept_as_bmu_or_wav` and `ls_lists_a_pcm_wave_kept_as_bmu_in_a_hak`. [Area sounds](manual/04-areas.md#area-sounds) and [Troubleshooting](manual/13-troubleshooting.md) say it.

The rules are `mg_audio::role`'s, for the window's log and Verify alike (`Role`, `Silent`, `silent_in_game`, moved from mg-ui with their matrix, and `silent_positional`; `Role::looked_for` gives the missing references' sound types), judged by `mg_audio::Form` (a WAVE, MP3 behind the header, MP3 without it); the log also warns now of a Play button's or placed sound's MP3 under `.wav` without the header (`Sound mg_snd3 is MP3 under .wav without the BMU V1.0 header, which the game does not play`). A placed sound or sound blueprint kept only as `.bmu` is still a missing reference, now saying `missing (only mg_snd.bmu is there, which the game does not look for)` (`found_as` in the JSON). A file is read once a run (`mg_module::sounds::Judged`) and only its start: `mg_audio::form_by_start` asks 4 KiB, more only for a bare MP3 (its first frame, a mebibyte on) or a long chunk or tag, and tells what the whole file would (held by `a_start_tells_what_the_whole_file_holds` and `a_start_tells_the_form_and_channels_the_whole_file_has`); a folder's file is read only that far too (`DirContainer::read_start`). mg-audio's decoding is the feature `decode`, which mg-module leaves off: `mg` without its default `nui-preview` carries no Symphonia (with it, mg-ui brings it, as before; the binary 46,053,280 bytes before, 46,042,072 after). Measured: The Domains of Dread kept as a nasher project with its 145 haks (9 areas, all on row 0, no placed sounds or sound blueprints of its own), `mg --json verify --timings`, 2.8 to 3.9 s wall after against 3.2 to 5.0 s before (the machine loaded, 15 to 28), the check 14 to 55 ms of the workers' time, its findings none and the rest byte for byte the same; Wyvern Crown of Cormyr 0.10 s either way; a module made to load it (Neverwinter Chess with 40 copies of its area, 200 rows naming 122 files of a 1.9 GB hak on disk, tracks of 20 MiB, a quarter bare MP3), run before and after in turn: 0.27 to 0.40 s wall either way, the check 0.18 to 0.29 s of the workers' time, 68 findings, each the one made for it (no whole track read). The game's own content draws findings by these readings, none passed over: read in the client and silent in the game as the check says, `ambientsound.2da` row 200, `al_mus_throne2.wav`, BMU + stereo MP3 under `.wav` (`the_game_s_own_music_and_ambient_rows_are_heard` takes all 253 rows every day and holds that one to be the only finding), and Wyvern Crown of Cormyr's six areas on row 83 (known findings of `shipped_modules_have_only_known_findings`); and the positional blueprints `lavalakeloop.uts` and `sludgelake.uts`, of the stereo IMA ADPCM `al_na_lavalake1.wav` and `al_na_sludglake1.wav`, silent as shipped and heard made area-wide (read with `MG_AUDIO_FORMS=stereo`: stereo PCM and IMA ADPCM alike, at the stock distances and at 50 and 100), held to be the only two by `the_game_s_own_sound_blueprints_name_only_two_sounds_it_does_not_play` (all 301 blueprints, 876 sounds, 572 positional, every day: the test takes some 10 ms alone), with XP2_Chapter2's `q3_area_sanctum`, a positional LavaLakeLoop placed, a known finding of `shipped_modules_have_only_known_findings` (its blueprint's fields read; the area's own instance not loaded). ## 2026-11-10
* **Fix**: A DXT1's one-bit texels are drawn opaque black with Shaders on, as the game draws them. Read in the game client ([the findings](findings.md), "A DXT1's one-bit texels are opaque black"; `batch6_bioware_dxt1_one_bit`). An authored DXT1 in the one-bit mode was drawn black and opaque under BioWare's header and the standard one, with a TXI `alphamean 0.5` or `blending punchthrough`, on a mesh of `alpha 0.5` (evenly half there) and under an environment map. The game's `tdt01_wood04` was drawn as its texels made black. Moonglow's own shader already drew it so. The game's programs got alpha 0 from the GPU's BC1, so they cut those texels under a TXI `alphamean` or a mesh alpha and showed the reflection through them. A DXT1 with such texels now goes up decoded and opaque, a cube map's face too (`mg_render::texture`'s `one_bit_texels`): four of the game's DDS files (`tdt01_wood04` and `05`, a quarter of their texels; `tts02_gate03` and `tts02_tree01`, a few in smaller levels), and 38 of the 23,952 BioWare DXT1 entries in The Domains of Dread's haks (some names in two haks; `ttr01` fences, gates and trees and `dd_ce3` vampire and skeleton parts, a few scattered texels each). Read on lit meshes only: decals, additive meshes, an MTR's `transparency`, particles and icons were not. `mg texture convert` and `mg texture info` already took a BioWare DXT1 as opaque, its one-bit texels black, and are unchanged. Tests `a_dxt1_s_one_bit_texels_go_up_opaque`, and `dxt1_alpha_is_carried_as_the_header_says_and_ati_is_only_copied` now checks the texels and `info`. [The shader notes](research/notes_shaders.md) mark the BioWare half [CLIENT].

(1) `--hak`'s place in the load order for `mg cat`, `mg which` and `mg model-files` stays as built: over every hak of the module, the first given highest, under `development/`. The owner had no leaning and took the recommendation. (2) `mg cat --to` with a name found nowhere stays as built: the rest written, the missing one said, the run failing. The same. (3) A BioWare DXT1 is handled as the game handles it: its one-bit texels opaque black, as the client reading above shows, which is what `mg texture convert` and `info` do. A standard DXT1 keeps its bit in the converter (NWN2's cut-outs), though the game draws it black too: that choice was outside the ruling.

The list stands at 88 open entries, 125 items (`tools/deferred/count.py`).
* **Fix**: A creature's parts that are effects show their particles, as in the game (a builder's report on 4.0: "With CEP you can attach visual effects as tail to a creature. These seem to be not rendered in Moonglow"). CEP's `@VFX` tails and wings name the game's effect models (emitters and no mesh), and only a preview's base model's emitters were simulated. Read in the game client ([the findings](findings.md), "A creature's parts' emitters"; `part_emitters_look`): a tail's and wings' emitters are keyed by their own animation of the name the creature plays, else their own `default`, else as the model has them; a helmet's as the model has them; a held item's as its `equip` ends (a torch burns); a part's scale sizes its particles and not their speed, as any object's visual transform does. `Composed::emitting` gives each model that emits; the area view, the model view (with its parts' light nodes under **Lights**) and the pictures simulate them all; `mg_render::particles` sizes particles by the emitter's scale. The area view now draws chunk emitters' models too, at their own size as the client does ([the findings](findings.md), "A chunk emitter's models are drawn at their own size"; `reading_chunk_size`), which closes the deferred entry. Tests `a_part_s_emitters_hang_where_the_part_does`, `a_tail_s_emitters_play_its_own_animation_or_its_default`, `a_scaled_emitter_throws_bigger_particles_as_fast`, `an_effect_worn_as_a_tail_shows_its_particles`. [The deferred list](deferred.md): GitHub issue 8's wings are likely explained (CEP's "Balor: Flame" wings are a part full of emitters); a creature holding a torch, raised and lighting the area in the client, filed.
* **Fix**: A body part is drawn as the game draws it where its mesh names another texture than the part's own (a builder's report on 4.0: "Moonglow does render the texture instead of the given PLT of the body part"). Read in the game client ([the findings](findings.md), "A body part is drawn in its own PLT"; `part_textures_look`, 32 rows of authored parts): a part with a PLT of its own name, or of the first fallback that has one, is drawn with that name on every mesh, whatever each names (a texture of no part's name, a second mesh's hair or gem: the old rule kept those, which had never been read in the client); a DDS or TGA of its name alone replaces nothing; a head takes no other race's or gender's. Of a PLT and a DDS or true-color TGA of one name, the client draws the DDS or TGA wherever each is in the load order, on parts and items alike; Moonglow drew the PLT on anything in colors, and now draws it only over a gray TGA (the game's `pmd0_head001`). Hak usage counts a part's own PLT as used whatever its mesh names. `creature::plt_fallbacks`, `mg_render::Assets::texture_kept` and `takes_colors`, `mg_image::tga::is_gray`; tests `a_part_with_a_plt_of_its_name_is_drawn_in_it_whatever_its_meshes_name`, `a_part_s_own_plt_is_used_whatever_its_mesh_names`, `only_a_plt_takes_an_instance_s_colors`, `the_game_s_plts_with_a_plain_texture_of_their_name_have_a_gray_tga`. [The deferred list](deferred.md) files a missing texture drawn black where the client draws light gray, seen on the way, and the Vault and CEP entry loses its `bitmap NULL` item, read in the client the same way. Then (follow-up, the same day): a mesh whose `bitmap` names a material with a `texture0` keeps it, as the client draws it (Moonglow had given it the part's PLT); a DDS of one luminance channel loses to the PLT as a gray TGA does (`mg_image::dds::is_gray`), a DXT1 of gray texels wins; robes follow the rule as any part; all read in the client (rows G to V). Over the owner's module (The Domains of Dread's haks and the game, 56,664 part models) the rule draws 2,556 meshes of 2,520 parts otherwise, all the haks', most of them cloth parts naming TDoD's `cmh0_`/`qmh0_` textures; nine read in the client (`part_textures_tdod_look`): eight are drawn there as the rule draws them, where Moonglow drew them otherwise, and head 146 is drawn by neither. [The deferred list](deferred.md) files a part's own material drawn on a renamed mesh (row J, found on no content) and a luminance DDS drawn alone.
* **Feature**: `mg texture plt-split PLT… --to FOLDER` splits PLTs (files or by name from the load order) into a shade PNG and a layers PNG (grayscale, each texel's layer 0 to 9 as its value, the right way up), and `mg texture plt-join SHADES.png LAYERS.png -o OUT.plt` joins them back, byte for byte: all 500 of the game's `pmh0_` PLTs split and joined to the same bytes. `mg_image::plt::Plt` keeps the header's bytes 8 to 15, which nwn.wiki calls unused (10 in most of the game's files, another from 1 to 11 in 62 of its 500 `pmh0_` parts), and writes PLTs (`Plt::write`, `Plt::new`); `png::write_gray` and `png::text` write grayscale PNGs and read their text chunks, where the header word rides. For the two PLT readers and the writer of The Domains of Dread's and Neverblender's scripts ([Command-line tools](manual/11-command-line.md#archives-and-files)). Tests: `a_plt_split_into_pngs_joins_back_to_the_same_bytes`, `textures_are_converted_by_name_from_the_load_order`, `a_plt_written_reads_back`, `truncated_input_is_an_error_not_a_panic`, `gray_written_reads_back_with_its_text`.
* **Feature**: `mg texture info TEXTURE…` gives each texture's facts for as many as given, from files or by name from the load order (`--module`, `--hak`, `--list`): size, type (DDS, TGA, PNG, PLT), a DDS's header and BioWare's alpha mean, format, mip levels, whether the format holds alpha and how the largest level's texels use it (`opaque`, `binary`, `blended`; `--headers` leaves that out), a PLT's layers used; one that can't be read fails the run once the rest are said. 4,938 game textures (creatures' and trees') in 1.2 s. For the seven image-header readers of The Domains of Dread's and Neverblender's scripts ([Command-line tools](manual/11-command-line.md#archives-and-files)). `mg_image::png::info` reads a PNG's header without its pixels. Tests: `info_gives_each_texture_s_size_format_levels_and_alpha`, `textures_are_converted_by_name_from_the_load_order`, `a_png_s_header_is_read_without_its_pixels`.
* **Feature**: `mg texture convert TEXTURE… (-o FILE | --to FOLDER)` converts textures between TGA, PNG and DDS (BioWare's header by default, `--standard` for the other) from files or by name from the load order (`--module`, `--hak`; a bare name as the game finds it, a DDS over a TGA): DXT1 or DXT5 chosen by whether any texel is less than opaque (`--format` to choose), every mip level made (`--no-mipmaps` warns that the client reads past a single level), `--pow2` and `--max-size N` resizing (area averages shrinking, bilinear enlarging, color weighted by alpha: `mg_image::adjust::resize`), `--bleed[=ALPHA]` filling hidden texels' color from the visible ones by a pyramid pulled up and pushed down (`adjust::bleed`, as Neverblender's `bleed_colors`, without its wrap-around kin in The Domains of Dread's two), a DDS kept in its format and size copied rather than encoded again (its missing levels made), a BioWare DXT1 taken as opaque as its header says (two of the game's 6,737 DDS files, `tdt01_wood04` and `05`, hold one-bit texels it draws black; a standard DXT1 keeps its bit, as NWN2's cut-outs need), ATI1 and ATI2 only copied (encoding them as DXT would lose a normal map), and a JSON report per file (input, layer, output, container, format, size, mips, alpha). PNGs are turned over on the way in and out, so the game's row order holds. For the asset scripts' three alpha-bleed routines and five wrappers around Neverblender's encoder ([Command-line tools](manual/11-command-line.md#archives-and-files)). `mg_image::tga::write` writes 32-bit TGAs; `Texture::stored_rgba` gives the alpha a texture stores (DXT1's punch-through texels transparent) where `to_rgba` gives what the game draws. Tests: `textures_convert_between_png_tga_and_both_dds_headers`, `a_dds_kept_in_its_format_is_copied_and_its_missing_levels_made`, `textures_are_resized_bled_and_refused_before_anything_is_written`, `textures_are_converted_by_name_from_the_load_order`, `dxt1_alpha_is_carried_as_the_header_says_and_ati_is_only_copied`, `shrinking_averages_and_enlarging_blends`, `hidden_texels_do_not_tint_a_resized_picture`, `bleeding_fills_hidden_colors_from_the_visible_ones`, `powers_of_two_nearest_by_ratio`, `alpha_is_kept_where_it_is_stored`.
* **Feature**: An encoder for textures: `mg_image::encode::compress` encodes a picture as DXT1 (BC1) or DXT5 (BC3) with its mip chain down to 1×1 (each level halved by 2×2 means, color weighted by alpha), DXT1 with alpha in the punch-through mode when asked; `mg_image::dds::write_bioware` and `write_standard` write a texture in BioWare's header (the alpha mean the picture's mean alpha, as in the game's own files) or the standard one (DXT1 to ATI2 by FourCC, RGBA8 uncompressed), rows as stored in both. A color block's endpoints are refitted by least squares from its principal axis, a block of one color takes the endpoints whose blend comes nearest it, an alpha block is tried in both of DXT5's modes; every choice scored with the decoder's own palettes (`bc::color_palette`, `channel_palette`, now shared). On four pictures made in the test it beats Neverblender's numpy encoder, which the asset scripts of The Domains of Dread and Neverblender wrapped five times, on every one (flat colors 50.1 dB against 42.2, a soft-edged cut-out's alpha 40.8 against 38.9: [the measurement](research/notes_texture_encoder.md)). `textures_match_pillow` gives Pillow the game's textures as `write_standard` writes them. Tests: `encoded_pictures_keep_their_quality`, `written_textures_read_back_in_both_containers`, `opaque_bc1_never_uses_the_transparent_index`, `punch_through_keeps_the_cut`, `alpha_blocks_take_the_better_mode`, `mip_chains_go_down_to_one_texel`, `halving_weights_color_by_alpha`, `one_color_blocks_decode_to_their_color_or_next_to_it`.
* **Feature**: `mg 2da-set TABLE.2da COLUMN=VALUE…` sets cells of a 2DA file in a row by its number (`--row`), by a column's value (`--where Label=Sword`, one row matching) or in a row added at the end (`--append`), and writes the file as it is laid out (`TwoDa::to_bytes_like`: widths, row labels, tabs, line ends), its cells read and written by mg-2da (quoted values, `****`); `-o`, `--dry-run`, and refusals for a column, row or value the table can't take, with nothing written. For the scripts of The Domains of Dread and Neverblender that edited 2DAs with parsers of their own, which disagreed on quoted cells ([Command-line tools](manual/11-command-line.md#the-games-resources)). Tests: `cells_are_set_by_row_by_a_column_s_value_and_in_a_row_added`, `what_cannot_be_set_is_refused_and_nothing_written`.
* **Feature**: `mg model info MODEL` prints a model's facts, from its file or by its name from the load order (`--module`, `--hak`): nodes by kind, faces (every mesh's, and those of the meshes the game draws), vertices, the box the drawn meshes fill at rest in the model's space (nodes placed with their scales, skins at their bind pose, emitters, lights, walkmeshes and hidden meshes left out), skins with the bones their weights move and their triangles (and the bones of all of them), the textures and materials it names, its supermodel and its animations with their lengths, the same for a model's text and compiled. The facts are `mg_mdl::facts::Facts`, for Moonglow Viewer's `mgv info` to take up. For the four model-statistics readers of The Domains of Dread's and Neverblender's scripts, which parsed ASCII models for the box, the skins' bones and the drawn triangles that no command gave ([Command-line tools](manual/11-command-line.md#archives-and-files)). Tests: `a_model_s_facts_are_the_same_from_its_text_and_compiled`, `a_model_with_no_drawn_mesh_has_no_bounds` (mg-mdl), `model_info_gives_a_model_s_facts_from_its_text_and_compiled`, `model_info_finds_a_model_by_its_name`.
* **Feature**: `mg model-files WHAT FOLDER --hak PATH` stages a model, blueprint or area with every file it is drawn with (models and supermodels' animations, walkmeshes, textures, materials, TXI) from haks, ERFs and folders given, over the game, with no module needed, as `mg cat --hak` reads them; for the four staging scripts of The Domains of Dread and Neverblender, which copied a model's files themselves because the command read only a module's haks ([Command-line tools](manual/11-command-line.md#modules)). Test: `model_files_reads_the_haks_and_folders_given`.
* **Feature**: `mg ls ARCHIVE --sha256` gives each resource's SHA-256 beside its size (in `--json`, `sha256` beside `name` and `size`), for the hak inventories of The Domains of Dread's scripts, which hashed the entries with their own ERF reader; off by default, as it reads the archive whole (TDoD's 1.5 GB tile hak in 4.1 s) ([Command-line tools](manual/11-command-line.md#archives-and-files)). Test: `ls_gives_each_resource_s_size_and_its_hash_when_asked`.
* **Feature**: `mg cat NAME… --to FOLDER` writes many resources into a folder in one run (names also from `--list FILE` or standard input), each with the layer it came from, its size and its SHA-256, a name found nowhere said and failing the run once the rest are written, `--dry-run` writing nothing; and `--hak PATH` on `mg which` and `mg cat` reads haks, ERFs, modules and folders of your own over the game's load order, the first given highest, over every hak and under the portraits and the user folder's `development/` (`mg cat` takes `--module` too). For the asset scripts of The Domains of Dread and Neverblender, which kept their own ERF readers and game-plus-haks resolvers because reading many resources took one `mg cat` each (about 0.1 s) and haks came only from a module: 3,000 resources of a 1.5 GB hak (218 MB) are written in 1.3 s ([Command-line tools](manual/11-command-line.md#the-games-resources)). Tests: `many_resources_are_written_with_their_layers_sizes_and_hashes`, `which_and_cat_read_the_haks_given`.

Moonglow's own see-through draws now go in runs of one chunk too, where nothing they meet is between, so the picture is the same (the frame tests' views compared pixel by pixel with the build before): 2,159 chunk changes; draws encoded 12.6 ms where 14.8 seen whole and 17.9 where 19.7 turned, Shaders off (lowest of three; 10.2 and 15.6 for the build of 27 October with the same haks). The game's see-through draws keep their runs by pipeline and material: split by chunk they cost the GPU 2.6 ms more turned than they saved. `Drawn::chunks` counts the changes and `frame_perf` prints them; `see_through_draws_of_a_material_are_drawn_by_chunk_where_they_meet_nothing`. What is left against 27 October is no one thing in the profile ([the deferred list](deferred.md)).

The review's fail-before list was run: each listed test of X3 to X25 and of the blueprint fixer's (but B15 and B19) that can run at its fix's parent failed there for its finding's reason; those of X11, X18, X20, X22 and X23 call functions their fixes added and cannot run there.

## 2026-11-09
* **Update**: The fixes of the [review of November 2026](review-2026-11/overview.md), for 4.0.0, at the owner's word the same day ([the record of the fixes](review-2026-11/fixes.md)): twelve fixers took a page of the review each (one took two, the workspace's and the rules'), a thirteenth what the window's shell and the 2DA and hak editors left after the first round, a fourteenth what the fixers saw on the way; each read a finding's place again before changing it, wrote a test with each fix that could have one (named in the entries below), and made about a commit a finding (311 commits on fourteen branches, each merged into develop), after the reviewer's own 20 commits for the lost-work findings of the window. Of the 349 findings, 324 are fixed whole, 11 in part, 5 were found fixed by another finding's commit, 8 are left and 1 does not hold (S15, settled by the owner: the deferred list's account of it is right). What is left waits on the owner's word, a client run, an Aurora capture, Windows, macOS, Twine or the reviewer's timing run, each on [the deferred list](deferred.md) with its reason (28 entries added, none closed: more than the sprint's rule allows, said here plainly); tests not seen failing before their fix are listed there too.
* **Fix**: The review's last pass, items 1 to 8: what its fixers saw on the way, in the window's code ([the record](review-2026-11/fixes.md#the-last-pass-what-the-fixers-saw-on-the-way)). The creature page's sound-set play button reads a sound's name up to its first NUL, where a field with bytes after one played nothing (`a_sound_set_s_sample_is_its_field_up_to_the_first_nul`). An update is never downloaded into the system's temporary folder: without a cache folder the window says so and offers the release page (`an_update_is_not_downloaded_without_a_cache_folder`). Find References, the rename's count and warning, and what a delete says still names a resource find a name with a letter outside ASCII where a script spells it (`a_name_outside_ascii_is_found_spelled_in_a_script`). A module opened after the resources changed keeps its new pipelines for the next session (`a_module_s_own_pipelines_are_not_the_one_before_s`, `the_game_s_pipelines_made_before_are_made_before_the_first_frame`). Remove Unused Data stops at Cancel before the next data file, and the window and the log say how many files it had removed, where a canceled one removed everything and said "canceled" (`canceled_and_pruned`). A texture, MTR or TXI of the module replaced through Import is drawn as it is now, without a reload (`a_module_s_textures_changed_are_told_from_its_other_resources`). `mg rename MODULE NAME.jui NEW` fails, the rename saved, when a script that opens the window does not compile under the new name or the window can't be built under it (`a_rename_fails_when_a_script_that_opens_the_window_does_not_compile`). The unit tests' scratch folders are under `target/test-output`, not the system's temporary folder ([Main window](manual/02-main-window.md), [Build and test](manual/09-build-and-test.md), [Command-line tools](manual/11-command-line.md)).
* **Fix**: Areas, the review's A1 to A29 ([the page](review-2026-11/ui-area.md)): A2, A3 and A4 were fixed before. A group's brush kept across Reload Resources no longer panics the window once its group is gone, and the palette puts the tile brush down with the rest of the game data (`a_brush_of_a_group_the_tileset_lost_makes_no_stroke`). The view's selection, Adjust Location, Bake Walkmesh, Change Light, Redraw Polygon, the eraser's stroke and a Ctrl + wheel scaling or Q and E's turning under way follow their objects through Undo, Redo and edits made elsewhere, where the yellow box and the next Delete, drag or OK landed on the object that took the place (`the_selection_follows_its_objects_through_undo_and_redo`, `adjust_location_follows_its_object_when_one_before_it_is_deleted`, `a_wheel_scaling_under_way_is_not_given_to_the_next_object_by_a_cut`). An object moved, then set back behind another tab and saved, is read again in its view (`an_edit_undone_behind_another_tab_and_saved_is_undone_in_the_view`). Update Instances, Find and Replace Text and Find Instance act only on the module they searched: Update waits for a new **List Again**, Replace for Find, a double click searches again (`results_found_before_the_module_changed_are_not_acted_on`). Create Set writes its tags in the game's codepage (`create_set_writes_its_tags_in_the_game_s_codepage`). A pasted tile brings its Replacement Texture (`a_tile_keeps_the_replacement_texture_of_the_struct_kept_for_it`).
