A drag is dropped, not committed, when a key changes the mode (`a_drag_is_let_go_of_when_a_key_changes_the_mode`), and in Paint, Select Tiles and with a tile brush Alt + drag always moves the view (`alt_and_a_drag_moves_the_view_in_every_mode`). The tileset's grass on Area Properties is read again with the game data (`a_tileset_s_grass_is_forgotten_with_the_game_data`). The tileset editor's files, a bake's rows file and exported minimaps are written whole; Edit › Undo names fourteen of the area's steps in title case ([Modules](manual/03-modules.md), [Areas](manual/04-areas.md), [Blueprints](manual/05-blueprints.md)).
* **Fix**: Areas, the same pass's performance findings ([the page](review-2026-11/ui-area.md)). A large selection is looked up by a map kept as the model is shown, dragged over a posed copy kept from frame to frame, and boxed as one mesh past some eighty objects (`a_kept_copy_posed_again_is_as_a_fresh_copy_posed`, `lines_are_meshed_a_quad_each`, `a_large_selection_is_boxed_and_dragged_as_a_few_objects_are`). The scatter brush works its next dab out once, by squares, and draws the first four hundred (`the_places_taken_answer_by_squares_as_gone_through`, `the_next_dab_is_worked_out_once_and_drawn_in_part`). Find Instance, Update Instances, Find and Replace Text and Edit Areas Together lay out the rows in sight (`find_instance_lays_out_the_results_in_sight`); Update Instances asks which objects are ticked of sets (`the_ticked_objects_are_found_as_a_scan_of_the_list_finds_them`). Saved lighting, Save as Prefab and Custom Light read their folders as they open (`what_a_window_reads_from_disk_is_kept_while_it_is_shown`); Create Waypoint, Create Set and Find Instance keep no other area's document (`create_set_and_find_instance_keep_no_other_area_s_document`). The lights of placeables.2da are found once a reading of the table (`the_lights_of_a_placeables_table_are_found_in_one_pass`); the Position menu works out what it says as it opens; the tileset editor reads a section once a revision of the file, and its undo keeps the lines a step changed (`a_field_s_value_is_the_file_s_through_changes`, `undo_keeps_the_lines_a_step_changed`). A selected tile's outline is laid along the ground once: every tile of a 32 by 32 area selected cost 2.8 ms a frame over none, 1.0 ms after, on flat ground; a terrain drag's preview is handed out shared (a Shift rectangle's replay, 1.8 ms, stays). The other views are on the deferred list for the reviewer's timing run.

* **Fix**: The graphics checks, the same pass (R6 to R8, R24 to R27 and the page's three left out; [the page](review-2026-11/renderer.md)). A backend is recorded as failing only where the startup check compared a picture and found it wrong, or the GPU gave an error; no device, a panic, a timeout or a lost device takes the other backend for that run only. A record is one release's: another release tries the backend again. The watch's Restart with … records nothing where tiles failed or textures never came. Automatic takes OpenGL or a software adapter only where nothing else is there, and says so in the log and a notice with what to install. A lost device writes the recovery copy at once and tells the builder in a system dialog (a real driver reset on Windows not tried). `WGPU_BACKEND` set but empty or naming no backend is as unset, and said. A backend that ends Moonglow during the startup check is known at the next start and passed over. A check's panic is written up as `graphics-check-<time>.txt`, not a crash ([Options](manual/10-options.md), [Troubleshooting](manual/13-troubleshooting.md#the-window-stops-drawing-the-graphics-device-was-lost)). Settings that do not read are kept as `app.ron.unreadable-<time>` and read field by field, an enum name this version lacks is its default, and two windows no longer put each other's options back (`settings_are_read_field_by_field_where_the_whole_does_not_read`, `a_settings_file_that_does_not_read_is_kept_aside`, `a_name_this_version_does_not_know_is_the_default`, `a_window_saves_its_own_changes_over_another_window_s`) ([Command-line tools](manual/11-command-line.md), [Options](manual/10-options.md#where-the-settings-are-kept)).
* **Fix**: The plugin host's limits, the review's C2 to C4, C10 to C12 and C22 ([the page](review-2026-11/plugins-cli.md)). A ResRef set from text keeps letters outside ASCII; a new resource's name is one a file can have; numbers that are not finite are refused; `mg nui render` and `layout` read a window file's pictures from beside it only ([Plugin API](manual/17-plugin-api.md#limits), [Writing plugins](manual/16-writing-plugins.md), [Plugins](manual/15-plugins.md)). For P7, P16, P20 and P21 the test was seen failing before the fix; for the others the failure before is by reading.
* **Fix**: Models, shaders and previews, the review's M1 to M17 ([the page](review-2026-11/models-shaders-previews.md)): hostile models and the shaders. A compiled model could ask for gigabytes through its key records, a text model through one wide key row, and a chain of 20,000 nodes or 100,000 `aabb` entries ran the compiler out of stack; the decompiler indented a chained walkmesh tree by its depth. All are bounded now (a text row is cut at 16 values, 46 in a Bézier list). The compiler reads a node's keywords from a text that is not UTF-8 (one Latin-1 byte had every mesh compiled with shininess 1), a walkmesh with a null tree pointer reads as having no tree (none among 42,782 walkmesh nodes of the 147,175 compiled models swept; Moonglow's own compiler writes one), and the reader and linter share one table of list keywords. In the shaders, the compiled-shader cache drops entries unread for 30 days (by age, not release, as Moonglow Viewer shares the folder), includes are refused past 8 MB of assembled text and a file spliced twice is one, and a uniform's declared value is read from the branch the preprocessor keeps ([Areas](manual/04-areas.md), [Build and test](manual/09-build-and-test.md)). * **Fix**: What the Module Uses (`mg haks --usage`) and Export Model Files left out files the game reads, so a release cut by the report lost them (the review's M4 to M7, M10, M13, M15, M17; [the page](review-2026-11/models-shaders-previews.md)). * **Fix**: Formats and core, the review's F1 to F25 ([the page](review-2026-11/formats-core.md)): hostile files and the updater. A crafted tileset, `nwscript.nss`, compressed resource or NWNT file no longer asks for memory or stack its size doesn't warrant: a tileset's lists are bounded by its sections (`counts_that_are_no_counts_cost_nothing`), an engine structure past 255 is skipped (`engine_structure_numbers_size_nothing`), a zstd frame is read to at most 64 times its length and 64 MiB (`a_frame_that_expands_past_all_proportion_is_refused`), NWNT nesting stops at 128 (`deep_nesting_and_long_tables_are_bounded`). Rename Symbol on a struct member whose script changed under the window says so, where it panicked (`rename_refuses_a_declaration_that_changed`). An update is offered for an AppImage only where Moonglow runs from its mount (`another_program_s_appimage_is_not_this_one`); a second Moonglow leaves the first one's download and staged update alone (`another_run_s_staged_update_is_left_alone`); the unpacked zip and the copied-out app are checked again before the swap (`unpacked_files_changed_since_they_were_checked_are_refused`); `hdiutil`, `ditto` and `reg` run by full path with a time limit (`a_program_that_hangs_fails_its_step`; not run on macOS or Windows). A hak or talk table named with a folder in it opens nothing and is said not to be found (`a_name_with_a_folder_in_it_names_no_file`, `a_hak_named_with_a_folder_is_placed_nowhere`); `userpatch.ini`'s haks are named as a module's are; a resource name with a byte above 0x7F keeps its name through a folder (`a_name_past_ascii_survives_a_folder`). NWNT refuses text with a typed `\n` and labels it can't keep, so a nasher project fails to save such a file, naming the field (`what_nwnt_can_t_keep_is_found`). A 2DA cell takes no line break, and a character its codepage lacks is named with its cell; GFF JSON ids out of range are errors (`ids_out_of_range_are_errors`); a sound field's bytes after a NUL are kept (`a_sound_s_bytes_after_a_nul_are_kept`); the tileset editor reads `Count=250;` as 250 (`counts_are_read_as_the_reader_reads_them`). The sandboxed client's CD key copy is removed when its run ends ([The main window](manual/02-main-window.md), [Modules](manual/03-modules.md)).
* **Fix**: Formats and core, the same pass: one rule each and speed (the review's F9, F13 to F15, F18, F20 and Z1; [the page](review-2026-11/formats-core.md), [the finders' page](review-2026-11/mechanical.md)). One Nim float and one JSON escape in `mg_core::nim`, measured against `nwn_gff` and `nwn_tlk` (`floats_are_written_as_nim_writes_them`): a tie between two shortest forms goes to the even digit, as both tools write it. `mg tlk-export` of a talk table with an infinite sound length writes `"soundLen":"inf"`, as `nwn_tlk` does, where it panicked (`an_infinite_sound_length_is_written_and_read_back`; [Command-line tools](manual/11-command-line.md)). An update's checksum is taken with mg-core's SHA-256 and compressed resources are read with the zstd library that writes them: `sha2` and `ruzstd` are out of the workspace. A tileset's long value is read in one pass, by the reader 2DA cells have (`a_long_value_is_read_at_once`). Faster: `mg merge-gff` on long lists (`a_long_list_changed_throughout_merges_at_once`), script indexing (`a_script_of_many_functions_is_indexed_at_once`), `mg lsp` completions (`completions_are_the_unit_s_declarations_in_one_pass`), and finding the game on Windows, the usual folders tried before any drive letter (`the_usual_folders_are_tried_before_any_drive_letter`; read, not timed: that needs Windows with an unreachable mapped drive). The timed and hostile-file tests were not run against the old code, which would take gigabytes or minutes.
* **Fix**: Lost work, fixed by the reviewer before the fixers began (the review's E1, S1, S2, S4, S6, S7, P1; [the window's page](review-2026-11/ui-shell.md)). Save, Undo and a new edit left the module read as saved (no star, no question at closing, no recovery copy): whether it is saved is now a place in the history (`a_new_edit_after_an_undo_past_the_save_is_unsaved_work`). The module's Undo and Redo dropped a script editor's unsaved text (`the_module_s_undo_keeps_a_script_s_unsaved_text`), and text typed in script editors alone made no recovery copy, or one only (`a_copy_is_made_when_one_is_due`, extended). Recover, New Module's Create and Open Directory as a Module replaced unsaved work unasked (`recover_and_new_module_ask_before_they_replace_unsaved_work`). A pulled area made unsaved Module Properties count as read, and the next Save wrote nothing (`an_area_added_outside_leaves_unsaved_module_properties_to_be_saved`). Save As and a new module's first save left the old place's recovery copy, offered as unsaved work at the next start (`a_save_elsewhere_takes_the_old_place_s_copy_with_it`). A recovered module is opened where it lives, with the copy's resources: a module folder refused the save where the recovered work had deleted or renamed a resource (`a_recovered_folder_module_saves_into_its_folder`).
* **Fix**: The window's shell, fixed by the reviewer before the fixers began (the review's S3, S5, S8 to S13, S16 to S18, S22, S28, A2, A3, D4, D7, D13, B6 for two windows, B7, B8, B16, B17; [the window's page](review-2026-11/ui-shell.md)). Export Minimaps, the conversations' export and backups and Render Minimap Pictures wrote a resource named `../../x` outside the folder chosen (`a_resource_named_like_a_path_is_not_exported_out_of_the_folder`). The Variables window and String Edit wrote to whatever object took their object's place, and a Properties window of several moved only its first note (`the_variables_window_follows_its_object_through_the_list`). A closed module left its windows, Advanced Search's hits, the conversation clipboard and its pictures, palettes and model views to the next module opened (`closing_a_module_closes_the_windows_that_held_its_places`). Opening, closing and quitting wait for a running job (`nothing_replaces_the_module_or_closes_the_window_under_a_job`; [Build and test](manual/09-build-and-test.md)). Exit with only a hak or a table unsaved asks that editor's question (`quitting_with_an_unsaved_hak_asks_about_the_hak`). Options' OK writes what the tab changed and leaves the rest as it is now (`ok_writes_what_the_draft_changed_and_leaves_the_rest_as_it_is_now`). A Variables page forgets what was not set once it is left (`the_variables_page_forgets_what_was_not_set_once_it_is_left`). The debug log formats an action only as far as it is said, where an Import of 100 MB made hundreds of megabytes of digits (`a_long_value_is_cut_before_it_is_written_out`). A text field keeps Space, Delete, Backspace and the arrows from the window's commands (`letters_are_a_text_field_s_while_it_has_the_keyboard`, extended; Option with a key on a Mac from reading, not run there; [Options](manual/10-options.md)). Enter in a filtered list with nothing found leaves it open (`add_hak_filters_a_long_list`, extended). * **Update**: A review of the whole workspace for bugs found by reading, performance, logic written more than once and hygiene ([the record](review-2026-11/overview.md), a page a part beside it): fourteen readers over 305,000 lines of source (what changed since the review of 27 October read first), clippy's stricter lints and a clone finder as finders, the timing tests as the measure. 349 findings, 37 of them high: unsaved work lost without a word (the module read as saved after an Undo past the save and a new edit; a script editor's text dropped by the module's Undo, and never in a recovery copy), files written by a name that came from a file (ten places that join a folder with one, past `ResKey::path_in`), sizes, counts and depths taken from a file, objects held by their place in a list across edits that move it, and what outlives the module or the game data. Every high finding was read again at the lines it names, and a sample of the others: all hold; none was fixed here. Every timing test passes and no view is over its budget that [the deferred list](deferred.md) does not hold; a dense scene's draws take a fifth to a third longer to encode than on 27 October, in steps of 1 and 2 November (the audit's commits and the cap on the meshes' chunks; [the figures](review-2026-11/mechanical.md)).

The two switches are named in title case, **📌 Exact Tile** and **All Tiles (Ignore Fit)**, at the owner's word: a tool's name, as the manual calls it, is title case though the control is a switch ([Interface text](style-guide.md)). Tests: `a_group_placed_exactly_changes_its_cells_alone`, `an_exact_tile_changes_its_cell_alone` (a hut of two tiles for the lock), `an_exact_group_goes_in_as_it_is_and_replaces_a_staircase`.

* **Feature**: Plugin API 0.9: a panel's **fields**, for the owner's ask via the TDoD Module session (a tint picked in a window that stays open and follows the selection, not a form that closes on OK). A panel's element `{ type = "field", kind = …, id, label, value, … }` is a form's field (`kind` as a form's `type`; `value` what it shows, a form's `default` refused there); the window keeps each field's value by id across the panel's renders, taking the handler's `value` only when it differs from the one it gave last (`PanelState::took`). A color's `variable` draws the color on the objects selected while its picker is open, as the form's does; a field's `command` runs when it is set (a color's picker closed, text or a number let go, a check or a choice changed), on what was selected when the user began at it, one step of Undo. Every command a panel runs gets its fields' values as `ctx.values` (an empty table elsewhere; a plugin test's `values`). A choice's options, a form's and a panel's, may be `{ text, color }`, drawn with a swatch in the list and the box. The window of a plugin's job is headed by the command's title alone (`Tint`, the plugin's name on hover; the log keeps both) and no longer dims the window behind it. The workspace keeps what each change touched, by resource and place (`Workspace::touched_since`: commands, their amendments, undo and redo; unknown past a change made outside the edit history), and when each resource last changed (`Workspace::changed_at`). The area view reads again only the objects an edit changed (`AreaModel::touched_objects`, `read_objects`, and the scene's `update_objects`), and where only where they stand, their turn, tag or lock changed, those fields alone, their looks kept (`place_objects`: a creature's look took up to 2 ms to put together); an edit of another resource reads nothing; an object put in or taken out, the area's own properties or tiles, read it whole as before; where the workspace can't tell (a file changed outside), the GIT is compared with what was read (`changed_objects`). The module tree's lists of what is placed in an area follow that area's GIT, not every edit. `frame_perf`'s `refresh_parts`: a creature moved in an area of 1,063 objects 0.02 ms (8.7 ms read whole), its look changed 0.24 ms; a command every few frames costs what drawing the moved object costs. * **Fix**: Q and E turn the selection at once and make it one command when the keys rest (0.6 s), as the turning ring makes its drag one command when it is let go, for the owner's report (in a busy area Q and E lagged where the ring did not). Moonglow refused a drag whole when one tile on the way fitted nothing; Aurora, asked on the oracle with six drags whose ends or middles no tile fits (ttr01's road and stream, tic01's corridor and doorway, tdm01's tracks and corridor), lays it edge by edge, an edge no tile fits held and tried with the next (a stream across a road is a bridge only with both sides) and passed over if it fits neither with it nor alone, the rest laid. `mg_tiles::paint::Grid::lay_crosser` does so for the brush's drags and clicks; the quarters passed over are red while the drag lasts. A plugin's `area:cross` stays all or none ([the plugin API](manual/17-plugin-api.md)). [Areas](manual/04-areas.md), [the findings](findings.md) and [the parity checklist](parity/checklists.md) say so. Tests: the six drags in `terrain_scenarios.json` (ttr01, tic01 and tdm01 captured anew), held by `painting_matches_aurora` (73 steps); `a_crosser_is_laid_as_far_as_tiles_fit_it`; `a_crosser_drag_lays_what_fits_and_passes_over_the_rest`.
* **Fix**: A crosser is put on one edge with a click, as in Aurora, for a builder's report (a doorway in a wall took a drag, in the right direction, across two tiles, where Aurora takes a click on the wall). Aurora was asked first, on the oracle: a click without moving puts the crosser on the edge of the quarter of the tile clicked (the side it is nearest), refused where no tile fits it, its cursor (that quarter) red there; [the findings](findings.md) had said a click re-picks the tile, which was wrong. Moonglow's click chose the tile again; now it lays the crosser on that edge, the cursor red where nothing fits, and over a quarter the crosser already crosses still blue (the click chooses the tiles again, as Aurora's does). A drag is unchanged. The palette's crosser rows say so in their tip. [Areas](manual/04-areas.md) and [the parity checklist](parity/checklists.md) say so. Tests: five clicks in tic01's scenario (`terrain_scenarios.json`, captured anew by `capture_terrain.py`, which plays `click` steps now; two of them refused by both), held by `painting_matches_aurora` (67 steps), and `a_crosser_click_lays_it_on_the_edge_of_the_quarter_clicked`.

Off by default, today's × unchanged; on, a window with OK and Cancel closed any way but OK (its tab's ×, the tab's Close, Close Others, Close Tabs to the Right, Close All, Ctrl+W, a window's close button) does what its Cancel does, as Aurora's close button does (captured, `edit-copy-cancel/`): what was changed in it set back as one step that Undo takes back (a field typed in and not left with it), Edit Copy's and Add to Palette's new blueprint taken back, a NUI window's event script and the factions' numbers brought in line as by Cancel; a window with nothing changed just closes, and one whose window stays (its close button with a 2DA of unsaved changes among its tabs, which asks) is not set back. * **Creation**: [Sculpted terrain in Moonglow: a design](terrain-proposal.md), the deferred sprint's large entry 9 (a builder's terrain tool, NWN Mapper, as the measure), a draft for the owner, as the owner asked: design first, then build. It reads NWN Mapper's own repository (a Godot application with no license file: its behavior described, nothing taken) and the game's limits, and measures stock tiles with `mg cat` (binary tile models of 36 to 125 KB, ttr01's ground texture about 100 pixels a meter). It proposes a height field at 16 quads a tile with an 8-quad walkmesh painted with surface materials, a base and four texture layers blended in the game by a terrain shader Moonglow writes (baking them at the ground's sharpness would be about 700 MB for a 32 × 32 area), placeables kept as objects, the game's own lighting, a tileset of the area's own (the source tileset copied, then the sculpted tiles in a group; never a base tileset patched under its name), a model per tile holding only its own square with normals from the whole field, a mode of the area view rather than a plugin, and the source kept in the module. It sets out six milestones (the first a heightmap to the game, with no brush), the risks with numbers, fourteen readings to take in the engine, the client and Aurora before building, and eleven questions with recommendations. The [deferred list](deferred.md)'s entry says so and waits on the owner's verdict. The [shaders proposal](shaders-proposal.md)'s "NWN Mapper ships none of `mzlm`'s" is corrected: the tool's repository has the pair; the builder's export had not carried them.
* **Feature**: Updates install from the app (the deferred list's large entry 7, GitHub issue 28; the owner's decisions of the day; [the design](update-install-proposal.md)). The update notice and Help › Check for Updates… show the release's notes, with **Install Now** and **Later** beside Don't remind me about this version and ×, where Moonglow updates itself: the AppImage is replaced in place (the file at `$APPIMAGE`, its name and permissions kept, at once with Install Now), the Windows installer is run silently into the same folder as Moonglow closes (`/MOONGLOWRESTART=1` starting Moonglow again through `moonglow.iss`'s new `[Run]` entry), the Windows zip's files are moved in (the old ones aside, undone if a move fails), and the macOS app is swapped for the disk image's. Restart Now asks about unsaved work, installs, and starts the installed program again (the AppImage itself, not the program inside its mount, which the earlier Restart with … relaunch had used too). Flatpak, Scoop and Nix installs are left to their tools and never written. Every package is checked first: the release's `SHA256SUMS` signed with minisign by the owner's key (built in from `packaging/minisign.pub`, which the owner makes; until then a build installs nothing and links the page), its trusted comment naming the release's tag, and the download's SHA-256 the signed one; otherwise the window says why and links the page. Downloads are written to `.moonglow-update-*` files beside what they replace, renamed once checked; a folder that can't be written is said before anything is downloaded, and what a failed or interrupted download leaves is removed at the next start. Options › Updates: **Install updates automatically** and **Include pre-releases**, off (pre-releases compared by semver's precedence; the check asks the releases' list instead of the latest). The check's own request is unchanged. The new crate `mg-update` holds it, the app's ureq client behind its `http` feature and a release server on 127.0.0.1 for the tests; `packaging/sign-release.sh` signs a release ([packaging](../packaging/README.md), Signing a release). `a_signed_list_gives_the_package_s_hash_and_anything_else_is_refused`, `a_legacy_signature_is_refused`, `each_install_is_known_and_takes_its_package`, `an_appimage_is_downloaded_beside_the_image_checked_and_staged`, `a_package_that_doesn_t_verify_is_never_kept`, `a_folder_that_can_t_be_written_is_said_before_downloading`, `the_zip_is_unpacked_beside_the_program_and_its_files_swapped_in`, `a_zip_entry_outside_its_folder_is_refused`, `the_windows_installer_runs_silently_into_the_same_folder`, `the_macos_app_is_moved_aside_then_the_new_one_into_its_place`, `the_app_swap_is_undone_when_it_fails`, `the_app_s_client_asks_downloads_and_says_what_failed`, `the_signing_script_writes_the_sums_the_app_reads`; the UI tests `an_update_is_installed_from_the_notice_and_a_restart_asked`, `restart_now_asks_about_unsaved_work_first`, `an_update_with_a_bad_signature_is_refused`, `later_installs_the_update_as_moonglow_closes`, `the_download_runs_on_its_own_thread`, `a_pre_release_is_offered_only_with_the_option`; a failed install offers **Try Again** (a download from the start), in `an_update_with_a_bad_signature_is_refused`; `screens.rs`'s `update_install` pictures. [The main window](manual/02-main-window.md#installing-an-update) and [Options](manual/10-options.md#updates) say so. Running the installer and the swap on Windows and a Mac, and the first signed release, wait in the deferred list.
* **Feature**: Plugins add exporters, importers, wizards and panels: the plugin API is 0.6, as the [proposal](plugin-proposal.md#api-06-exporters-importers-wizards-and-panels-2026-11-02) designed it (the deferred list's large entry 8). An `[exporter]` (`mg.exporter`) is in **File › Export**, which becomes a submenu of Moonglow's own Export… and the plugins' exporters: the user chooses the file or the folder first, and the exporter, which only reads, writes it with `out:write` (with `for`, of what is selected, offered only then). An `[importer]` (`mg.importer`) is in **File › Import**, reading the file (of its kinds) or folder chosen into the module as one step of Undo. A `[wizard]` (`mg.wizard`) is in the Wizards menu: pages asked in the job's window with Back, Next and Finish, each a table or a function of the answers so far (nil skips it), a page's `check` keeping it; Finish's edits one step, Cancel making nothing. A `[panel]` (`mg.panel`) is a pane of Plugins › Panels showing the elements its code returns (headings, text, values, buttons running the plugin's commands, lists that open what they name), drawn by Moonglow, its code run on a thread of its own within 250 ms, redrawn on edits (once a run of them stops, `a_plugin_s_panel_is_drawn_once_after_edits_one_after_another`) and the selection as its `refresh` says and after the plugin's jobs, kept with the module's open windows. `mg plugin export`, `mg plugin import` and `mg plugin wizard` (`--answers FILE`, which `mg plugin run` takes too); a plugin's own tests run them (`export`, `import`, `wizard`, `panel`, with `to`, `content` and `shows`). Three examples, `creature-sheet`, `store-wizard` and `module-overview`, held by `the_examples_of_0_6_pass_their_own_tests`; the host's tests in `crates/mg-plugin/tests/kinds.rs`, the window's in `crates/mg-ui/tests/app/plugin_kinds.rs` (`a_plugin_s_exporter_writes_the_file_chosen_and_changes_nothing`, `a_plugin_s_wizard_asks_page_by_page_and_finishes_in_one_step`, `a_plugin_s_panel_shows_what_it_returns_and_follows_the_module`…), `mg`'s in `exporters_and_importers_run_from_the_command_line` and `a_wizard_is_answered_from_the_command_line`; pictures by `screens.rs`'s `plugin_kinds`. [Plugins](manual/15-plugins.md), [Writing plugins](manual/16-writing-plugins.md), the [reference](manual/17-plugin-api.md), [Command-line tools](manual/11-command-line.md) and the [API change list](plugins/CHANGES.md).
* **Update**: The [plugin proposal](plugin-proposal.md) designs API 0.6, the four kinds of thing a plugin adds that it had left for later (the deferred list's large entry 8): exporters (File › Export, to a file or folder the user chooses, of the module or of what is selected), importers (File › Import, into the module as one step of Undo), wizards (pages of a form with Back, Next and Finish, each page's answers given to the next, ending in edits) and panels (a pane that shows what a plugin returns as a small list of elements, drawn by Moonglow, redrawn when the plugin's manifest says, off the frame and within a budget); for each, the manifest, the Luau, the sandbox, `mg`, the tests, Undo, and what stays out and why.

* **Fix**: Typing in a very large script keeps to the 144 fps budget (the deferred list's large entry 5). Measured first, its stacks sampled (`eu-stack`): a key laid the whole text out again, highlighted whole, its layout job hashed, split at its lines by egui and put together again, the error's underline cut through every section; and at a typist's pace every key laid out each of the 14,000 lines anew, egui keeping a text's laid-out lines only while they are asked for at every frame, which the editor's frames between keys did not. The editor keeps egui's own `TextEdit` (its cursor, selections, IME, Undo and accessibility as they were) and gives it a layouter of its own, `script_layout::LaidOut`: each line is laid out by itself and kept while its text, its tokens' colors and its underline stay the same; a change lexes the lines from the first it touched, each from what the line before left open (a block comment, a raw string), until the tokens begin again as they did, and lays out only those whose fingerprint is new (a block comment opened: the lines down to its end; a Replace All: the lines it replaced); the editor's galley is the lines' put together (`Galley::concat`, as egui puts a text's lines together). The line numbers beside it are kept the same way, a number a line, laid out again where a mark changes. A view of its own over the text was not needed. Galleys are let go of when the colors, the font size or the scale change, or egui makes its fonts again (its font atlas full: `watch_fonts`). The frame after a key, which reads the side lists' symbols again, was slow besides: the symbols' duplicates were looked for through the whole list (a map now: nwscript.nss's 7,466 took 10 ms), the game's are sorted once, and the text's hash, taken every frame, is egui's (std's took a third of a millisecond); `word_at` no longer copies the script's characters. On the game's `nwscript.nss` (13,869 lines) at 3440×1400, the game loaded, medians before and after (`editor_perf`'s `editing_a_huge_script`, which now holds each to the budget as `frame_perf` does; another session's builds beside it move them by a tenth to a third): a key 11.5 to 12.1 ms, now 1.8; a key at a typist's pace (every eighth frame) 98, now 2.3, the frame after it 21, now 6.3; Backspace 11.4, now 1.6; a new line 15, now 2.6; text composed (IME) 31, now 2.0; 500 lines pasted 100, now 6.2; a bookmark set 3.6, now 1.6; idle 1.5, now 0.9; the cursor or the selection moved a line or a page over lines out of sight, and scrolling, 1.5 to 2.0, now 0.9 to 1.3. Still whole: taking back a change of the whole text (Select All, typed over, Undo) lays it out again as opening it does (110 ms), and the check as you type compiles once a pause (8 ms here). The editor looks as it did, pixel for pixel (`screens`' `script_editor_large`, before and after; the log's clock aside). `a_text_laid_out_line_by_line_is_laid_out_as_a_whole` and `nwscript_laid_out_line_by_line_is_laid_out_as_a_whole` (each row's place, size, characters and colors), `the_game_s_scripts_lexed_line_by_line_are_lexed_as_a_whole` (all 4,144 of the game's scripts, 213,606 lines, with `MOONGLOW_FULL_CORPUS`), `an_edit_lays_out_the_lines_it_changed`, `line_numbers_laid_out_one_at_a_time_are_as_all_together`, `fonts_made_again_lay_the_lines_out_again`, `a_long_script_s_lines_out_of_sight_are_edited_where_they_are` (the cursor moved down 120 lines, a selection over 200 typed over and taken back, Find going 2,750 lines down, 1,000 lines pasted, text composed, each drawn where the text has it); [the frames note](research/notes_frames.md) has the table.

## 2026-11-01
* **Update**: [The plugin proposal](plugin-proposal.md#external-programs-the-design-2026-11-01) has the design of external programs as plugins (JSON-RPC over standard input and output, the reference's names as its methods, marked as running with the user's rights and never allowed by a yes elsewhere), the last item of this round of the deferred list's "Plugins, beyond API 0.4", left to build in its own round (M). The entry is rewritten down to what is left: the terrain tool and more kinds of things to add (the owner's order), a list to install from, the 2DA editor's faults with fixes (that editor's own work), the type file with the Luau language server (a download), external programs, and what waits on a desktop, Windows or macOS (one item each).
* **Feature**: A plugin's own tests, the gaps of the deferred list's "Plugins, beyond API 0.4": a test holds what a job writes outside the module, `haks` (each hak's resources) and `written` (the files written into a chosen folder), writing none of it; `mg plugin test` takes a folder of plugins (each one's tests, its lines under its id); `mg plugin check` reads the test files without running them (`test_faults`: a file that doesn't read, a test of what the manifest lacks, a fixture not there); Manage Plugins' **Run Tests** runs them as a job, the log saying what each came to. How a test holds a command's edits, a finding's message and the game's data is settled, with the reasons. `a_plugin_s_test_holds_what_it_writes_outside_the_module`, `a_plugin_s_own_tests_run_as_in_a_pipeline` (a folder, check), `a_plugin_s_own_tests_run_in_the_window`; [Writing plugins](manual/16-writing-plugins.md#a-plugins-own-tests) and [Command-line tools](manual/11-command-line.md).
* **Feature**: A resource's own events, the gaps of the deferred list's "Plugins, beyond API 0.4": Save As (to another place) asks the plugins' `resource-saving` handlers as Save does (`Action::SaveAt`); `resource-created` fires for the Script Wizard, New Script (`by = "new-script"`), a new NUI window (`"new-nui"`) and an import (Import, a NUI window imported: `"import"`), and an event's `for` takes a resource's type (`nss`); `ctx.event.changed` gives a script's (a text's) lines that differ, each taken out and put in by its number; the time at-once handlers have is set in Manage Plugins (**Time within a save or a paste**, 5 s by default); `mg set` and `mg apply` take `--strict` (a warning stops the save too); and `mg rename`, `replace`, `areas`, `update-instances`, `import`, `verify --fix` and `mg plugin run`'s save ask the project's own plugins as `mg set` does. * **Feature**: Fixes for findings, the gaps of the deferred list's "Plugins, beyond API 0.4": a fix may ask (plugin API 0.5), `ctx.fix(label, { command = "retag", on = s? })`, its button running one of the plugin's commands on what the finding is about, which asks with its form (`mg_edit::fix::Asks`; `mg verify --fix` says it and leaves it); Undo of a fix offers its button again (its guard as before it, `Guard::unmade`; Redo makes it "Fixed" again), following its step of Undo (`Workspace::step_done`); **Fix All (N)** beside a check's first fix makes every one of them as one step of Undo (`Workspace::join_last`). `mg verify --fix` with a check there is none of (mistyped, or a plugin's not given) fails, where it only warned: a pipeline must not read a typo as "nothing to fix"; the doctor's checks and those the plugins given and the project's declare are known before any runs. * **Fix**: A game's or custom fragment program that works in the screen's pixels and reads no copy of the framebuffer counts `gl_FragCoord.y` from the bottom of the picture, as OpenGL does, where it saw the picture upside down (wgpu counts from the top): the height is the engine's `screenParams`, which `inc_common` declares for every stock program, read at the start of the program's `main` whether the program reads it or not (a program that reads the copies takes their height, as before). One that has neither height falls back to Moonglow's own shader and says why, where it drew upside down. `the_fragment_s_position_is_counted_from_the_bottom`, `a_program_in_the_screen_s_pixels_counts_from_the_bottom`; the corpus's `every_stock_program_compiles` and `every_program_in_the_installed_haks_compiles` count every fragment program so (TDoD's 102 with its haks). Closes the M1 entry's item in the [deferred list](deferred.md).
* **Fix**: Moonglow's own shader (the Shaders switch off, or a program that fails) turns a height map's parallax on a tile's `rotatetexture` meshes as the texture was turned, as the game's `inc_displacement` does (`mat2(m_texture)`): a turned tile's raised ground warped the other way. Beside the game's `fslit_nm` on a turned tile, normal- and height-mapped with tangents of its own, the picture differed by 17.84 of 255 on average (90 at the 99th percentile), now 0.33 (4; the parallax differs by 0.26 and 3 unturned); seen before and after. And the environment map's level under a normal map is taken from the normal it reflects by, as the game's is: the normal map's at the coordinates the parallax moved, a normal facing away bent towards the eye (`_nm` beside the game's: 0.08 and 2 before, 0.04 and 1), with one fewer normal-map read. `the_game_s_lit_shaders_match_moonglow_s` (its new `tile_turned_height_mapped` scene, the normal-mapped one held to 1 of 255 at the 99th percentile). Closes two of the M1 entry's items in the [deferred list](deferred.md).
* **Fix**: A custom shader with an array of samplers (`uniform sampler2D tex[2]`) is drawn with the Shaders switch on, where Moonglow's passes refused it and its own shader drew instead (Verify, which asks glslang alone, took it). Each array becomes its elements, split and paired as one sampler is and named as OpenGL names them (`tex[0]`, `tex[1]`); the engine binds no texture to such names, so they read white. Still refused, and said: such an array passed to a function (glslang reads an element of the parameter from a variable of its own, bound to nothing, so it would read white unsaid) or read whole. A uniform that is a struct, or an array of them, is described with its members (`ValueType::Struct`, `Member::members`) where it was `Other`, and is zero for every draw, as no MTR fills one. `an_array_of_samplers_is_split_into_its_elements`, `a_struct_uniform_is_described_with_its_members`, `a_check_keeps_what_glslang_takes`, `a_program_with_an_array_of_samplers_or_a_struct_draws`. * **Update**: Import Resources resizes, and chooses every overwrite at once (GitHub issue 40, ELadner: an ERF of hundreds of resources was hard to scroll through at the window's fixed size, and overwriting them meant ticking each box). Its edges and corners resize it, the list of what the module already has taking the room (it was 180 points tall), and **Select All** and **Select None** under the list tick and clear every one, as Aurora's Overwrite page has them, with a count beside. `import_resources_chooses_every_overwrite_at_once_and_resizes`; [Modules](manual/03-modules.md) says so.
* **Fix**: An area view's handles (the turning ring, and with Shift the tilt rings, the arrows and the scale handle) keep their size on screen with the camera close by (a builder's report on 3.1.4, placing fruit: the Shift handles ran out of the view). They were half a meter across at the least, which from a meter away filled the view and more; now they are the same share of the view at any distance (about a tenth of its height, or of its width in a view narrower than it is tall), as large as before from farther off. Seen before and after in pictures (`target/test-output/ui-area-handles-close/`). `the_handles_fit_the_view_when_the_camera_is_close`; [Areas](manual/04-areas.md) says so.
* **Feature**: The area view's **🌄 Tile Border** draws what the game client draws past an area's edge, where Aurora and Moonglow drew black (a builder's request on 3.1.4): the tileset's edge tiles (`<tileset>_edge.2da`), five deep beyond each edge tile and five by five beyond each corner, each carrying on its side's two corner terrains and its road, stream or wall, darkened as the client darkens them. Read in the client first ([the tile border](research/notes_tile_border.md), `reading_tile_border`): the row is looked up by the side's left corner, crosser and right corner, either way round (the other way round turned half a turn); the models are made for the east side; a raised corner is `Terrain+`; and the client sets the border meshes' material ambient and diffuse to half the sun's diffuse color in gamma space (read back from its uniforms through a patched `inc_standard`: 55, 30, 12 and 0 of 255 for a diffuse of FF, C0, 80 and 00, whatever the ambient). Beside the client's pictures from above, with an uneven side on each edge, Moonglow's border lines up to the pixel and measures within 0.2 of 255; a city's (tcn01) houses and a dungeon's (tdc01) floor and fences carry on as the client's, and an interior's walls keep their black cap. `mg_area::border` lays it out (`AreaModel::border`), `Instance::material` gives its meshes their color in both of the renderer's paths. Off by default, as Aurora draws nothing there and the edge shows plainest so; kept in the settings, in every area view. Under test (`mg_area::border`'s four tests: the depth, the corners' squares, a side listed the other way round, a crosser and a raised side, the material; `the_tile_border_is_drawn_past_the_edge_when_asked_for`: the scene's instances past the edge with it on, none off, on ttr01, tcn01 and tic01; `the_tile_border_is_off_by_default_and_kept`); seen in `look_tile_border`. [Areas](manual/04-areas.md#the-toolbar) and [Differences from Aurora](manual/12-differences.md) say so; [the tileset notes](research/notes_tilesets.md)' inference is replaced by what was read.
* **Fix**: With Shaders on, every Gallery picture draws shiny water as the area view does, by the game's `fswater` (a builder's report on 3.1.4: water in Gallery previews was the game's in some places and Moonglow's in others). The palette's Gallery, the Appearance Gallery, a tileset's tiles and groups and the placeables' pictures are all drawn by one function, which drew without the framebuffer copies `fswater` reads, so their water fell back to Moonglow's own pale, shiny water beside the area's dark see-through water; the area view, the model view and the minimap's tile pictures have had the copies since water became the game's on 2026-10-27 ([the framebuffer proposal](framebuffer-proposal.md)). A picture is now drawn with its targets' copies (`Renderer::render_with_copies`). Under test (`a_picture_s_water_is_drawn_as_the_area_view_draws_it`: a rural and a city water tile's pictures drawn by `fswater`, by `fslit` before); seen in `look_gallery_water_with_game_shaders` (the area's pond and the Tiles Gallery's water tiles side by side, before and after). A placeable's water, as the fountain's, is not shiny water and is drawn as before, as the area view draws it.
* **Creation**: [Audit: frames and GPU memory after 3.0.0, and on weaker hardware](performance-audit.md), after reports that performance fell and video memory rose since 3.0.0: v2.13.3, v3.0.0 and develop measured side by side (frames and wgpu's allocator report, `frame_perf`'s new `FRAME_MEMORY`), on the RX 9070 XT and the 9950X's integrated Radeon. Nothing got slower or larger since 2.13.3 (an area's opening to its last texture about 50 ms longer, grass 10 to 20% more GPU); what weighed was older: views, textures and wgpu's memory blocks held for good, an area drawn 25 times a second in the background, a fill-bound picture on an integrated GPU, a builder's 1024-pixel textures. The frame test's device had no BC textures (TDoD's woods 4.4 GB of textures where the app takes 870 MB): it now asks for what the app's does.
* **Fix**: The 3D views not drawn for two seconds (a tab closed or behind another, a window shut) let go of their targets and egui's binding of them, which held them on the GPU; an area whose tab is closed lets go of its scene too, read again where its camera was when reopened. Tyrants of the Moonsea's frame test ends at 267 MiB of the GPU's memory, from 611. `a_closed_area_lets_go_of_its_targets_and_scene`, `an_area_behind_another_tab_lets_go_of_its_targets_only`.
* **Fix**: Textures not drawn for 30 s of frames are let go of once there is more than a gigabyte of them (a quarter of one on an integrated GPU), the longest unused first; what a frame draws never is. `textures_not_drawn_lately_are_let_go_of_past_what_is_kept`.
* **Change**: The 3D views hold still while Moonglow's window has not the focus (an area drew 25 pictures a second behind another program's window; an integrated GPU's every moment), and go on as it comes back. `an_area_s_animations_wait_while_the_window_has_not_the_focus`; [Areas](manual/04-areas.md) says so.
* **Change**: The window's device takes the GPU's memory in blocks of 8 to 64 MB (wgpu's `MemoryUsage` hints), not 128 to 256: 524 MiB held after the frame test where 768 were, TDoD's woods 1552 where 1856; frames as long.
* **Feature**: Options › Area › **Largest textures** (as they are, 1024, 512 or 256 pixels) and **Area view resolution** (Full, 75%, 50%), for weaker GPUs, both as before by default: TDoD's woods take 244 MiB of textures at 512 where they take 868, and on the integrated GPU Tyrants of the Moonsea's largest area turning takes 20 ms a picture at 50% where it takes 80. [Options](manual/10-options.md) says what each costs.

## 2026-10-31
* **Update**: Update Instances for many blueprints is easier to find and to choose for (silentrocks' question after 3.1.3, who found no multi-selection in the palette and no command to update all): **Shift+click** in the palette chooses the custom blueprints from the one selected to the one clicked (Ctrl+Shift+click adds them), a single blueprint's Update Instances says so on its tip, and **Edit › Update All Instances…** opens Update Instances for every blueprint of the module, as `mg update-instances` with none named. `shift_click_chooses_a_range_of_custom_blueprints`, `palette_updates_the_instances_of_a_selection_and_a_category`; [Blueprints](manual/05-blueprints.md), [The main window](manual/02-main-window.md) and [The command line](manual/11-command-line.md) say so.
* **Fix**: Compile Models and `mg pack --compile-models` compile a mesh of more than 21,845 faces and a texture named longer than 16 characters, as the game draws them (dafena's report after 3.1.2: Blender's meshes of 24,005 faces and textures named `wm50b087bda5e788.014` left as text). Seen in the client (`placeables_look`): a wall of 29,768 faces in one mesh drawn whole, as text and as Moonglow compiled it, and a `bitmap` of 20 characters drawn with the TGA of its first 16. The linter's limits are the binary format's (`mg_mdl::lint`: 65,535 vertices, 32,767 faces a mesh, which the binary writer already held to), and a texture's long name is a warning naming what the game looks for; a model's (`refmodel`, `chunkname`, the supermodel) stays an error. A [wiki correction](wiki-corrections/38175602-models-triangle-limit.md) for the Models page, whose 65535 / 3 the limit was.
* **Fix**: A blueprint shown to look at (the game's, opened by View; an area another builder holds) has its fields' text chosen and copied again: they keep the keyboard, and what would change their text doesn't reach them (`blueprint::typing_kept_out`: typing, pasting, cutting, Backspace, Delete, Enter, their undo), where they gave the keyboard up and nothing of them could be copied (Troubletcat's report after 3.1.0: a base item's ResRef, copied for a script). And a blueprint's menu in the palette has **Copy ResRef** and **Copy Tag** (their ask). `a_viewed_blueprint_s_fields_take_no_typing` (now: and copies), `a_blueprint_s_resref_and_tag_are_copied_from_the_palette`; [Blueprints](manual/05-blueprints.md) says so.
* **Fix**: No tab's scroll bars come and go every frame any more (Troubletcat's report after 3.1.0: the jittering came back as a conversation's line went to Actions Taken). At 125% and some sizes, the area view beside the conversation, in the scroll area egui_dock puts round a tab, never settled: that scroll area stretches the tab's content to its room rounded to pixels, a sliver past itself (GitHub issue 38's cause, fixed then for the windows with OK and Cancel). egui_dock's scroll areas are off; a tab that doesn't fit its pane scrolls in Moonglow's own, its content held to the room in sight in whole pixels, so only what is truly wider or taller scrolls (`TabViewer::ui`). `a_line_s_actions_taken_page_holds_still` (six sizes never settled before); `screens.rs`'s `factions-narrow`, a tab that scrolls in a narrow window.
* **Fix**: An armor's or item's Metal 2 is drawn in, and chosen from, the game's metal palette, `pal_armor01`, as Metal 1 is (Troubletcat's report: Metal 2's picker showed other colors than Metal 1's, and the item was drawn in colors of neither). Moonglow read `pal_armor02` for it, a lighter palette the game has and never reads: seen in the client with `creatures_look`, `pal_armor01` green and `pal_armor02` red in the override, the armor's Metal 2 drawn green (Moonglow drew it red; now green). `mg_image::plt::PALETTES` and `ArmorChannel::palette`; a [wiki correction](wiki-corrections/14618045-plt-metal-palette.md) for the PLT page, which guesses otherwise.
* **Fix**: Options › Folders, and `mg` of its `--root`, say why a folder isn't the game where they said only "no data/nwn_base.key": the original game (1.69, as the Diamond Edition is: its `chitin.key`, GitHub issue 39), a folder inside the game's (`bin/win32`, `data`: choose the one above), or one above it (Steam's `common`: the game's folder in it named). `GameInstall::why_not`, under test (`a_folder_that_isn_t_the_game_says_why`); [troubleshooting](manual/13-troubleshooting.md) says so.

## 2026-10-30
* **Change**: The open tabs kept with each module (Moonglow's data folder, `open-tabs`) write a placed object's path as every path is written (`/Creature List[3]`), where they had a form of their own (`Creature List#3`), the owner's word on the GFF paths' leftovers. A file Moonglow 3.1.0 or before kept is read as it was written, its placed objects found again by what was kept of them, and written anew in the one form at the next close (`a_session_kept_as_3_1_0_kept_it_opens_and_is_written_anew`).
* **Change**: `mg vars --json`'s places say a variable on a resource's root (`module.ifo`, an area's GIT, a blueprint) at the path `/`, as every other path is written, where they said `""` (the owner's word on the GFF paths' leftovers). `var_desc::Found` carries its object's path as a `GffPath`, built as the walk goes, no text read back; Verify's fix that removes a variable takes it as it is.
* **Fix**: Check for updates automatically asks at each start (and as it is switched on), then once a day while Moonglow runs, where it asked once a day at most: a release out since that day's check was told only a day later, however often Moonglow was started again, and the notice wasn't kept from one run to the next (Carcerian's report on 3.1.0: the notice never came, Check for Updates… found the release). `the_update_check_asks_at_each_start`; [Options](manual/10-options.md) says when it asks and what is sent.
* **Fix**: The tileset editor fits its pane too, its page scrolling both ways over OK and Cancel (GitHub issue 38's foot going up and down: it held still in the first sweep, and moved at 746 by 613 points at 125% once its page held what it holds now). `a_properties_window_s_buttons_stay_put` holds it.
* **Fix**: With Shaders on, what is drawn see-through in the area view, a brush's tiles under the pointer and a blueprint about to be placed, is drawn by the game's shaders as the area is (the owner's report on 3.1.0: a brush's water was Moonglow's pale water beside the game's dark water). The renderer drew any instance below full opacity with Moonglow's own shader, as its solid meshes lay their depth first; they still do, by Moonglow's shader, and the game's programs draw their color over it (their see-through part a little towards the eye). Under test (`a_brush_s_tiles_are_drawn_by_the_game_s_shaders`: the brush's tiles among the models the game's programs draw, none before); seen in `look_tile_brush_with_game_shaders` (water laid beside the brush's, from above; a brush of trees at a slant, its trunks behind its canopy).
* **Update**: GFF paths are one type, the second of the large entries after 3.0.0 ([the deferred list](deferred.md)'s "GFF paths as strings"): `GffPath` and its `Step` are mg-gff's (mg-edit's re-exported, so its callers' imports are as they were), with one text form, written and read in one place (`/Creature List[3]/ScriptSpawn`, a label's `~`, `/`, `[` and `]` escaped as `mg set` and `mg apply` read them), and `Struct::walk_fields` hands each field its path as one. A reference, a usage and what Advanced Search and Find and Replace find carry the path, not its text; where a place is no GFF field it is one of its own kind (`mg_module::refs::Location`: a script's `line N`, a 2DA's `row R, COLUMN`, a sound set's `entry N`, a script's `string`). The parsers of a path's text are gone (`Hit::instance`, `Usage::instance`, `rename::describe`, Verify's category, the References window's conversation row, Advanced Search's objects and their places, `found.rs`' `path_of`, the window's grouping of what is ticked) and the walkers beside `walk_fields` with them (the index's tags and StrRefs, Find and Replace's, `text::struct_at`). What `mg refs`, `mg search`, `mg replace`, `mg rename` and `mg verify` print is as it was, byte for byte (held by `apps/mg/tests/places.rs` on a module the test builds, and compared over the eight modules the game installs); the References window's places, its paths and the Delete window's order too (`the_references_window_says_where_things_are`). Only a label with a path's characters is said otherwise: `/a~1b[0]/OnSpawn`, where it was `/a/b[0]/OnSpawn`, which read back as another path. [The deferred sprint](deferred-sprint.md)'s list after 3.0.0 has it done.
* **Feature**: `mg haks --usage` and What the Module Uses follow what scripts name by a number, the first of the large entries after 3.0.0 ([the deferred list](deferred.md)'s "What scripts reach by a number"): a visual effect (`EffectVisualEffect`, `EffectBeam`: visualeffects.2da's models and sounds and the progfx.2da rows it names), a spell (`ActionCastSpell*`, `ActionCastFakeSpell*`: spells.2da's icon, impact script, visuals and sounds), an item property's spell (`ItemPropertyCastSpell`, iprp_spells.2da and its spell) or weapon glow (`ItemPropertyVisualEffect`, on every item class) and an appearance (`SetCreatureAppearanceType`: the creature's look). Read from the compiled script (`mg_script::ncs`, new: the game VM's instructions, a call's constant arguments told by going back over what was pushed after them), where the compiler has put every constant's value in, so a hak's script without its source counts too, and its strings are read as a source's are. A number worked out as the script runs is counted and named (`by_number` in the JSON, a line in the report), not followed. Held to neverwinter.nim's `nwn_asm` over the game's compiled scripts (`--test scripts ncs`: the same instructions at the same offsets and the same function at every call); on The Domains of Dread's module, 3,385 calls followed and 139 not, the walk reaching 864 more resources. [Modules](manual/03-modules.md) says what is followed; [the deferred sprint](deferred-sprint.md)'s list after 3.0.0 has it done.
* **Fix**: An edit undone, or a field set back by hand, leaves its file as it was, byte for byte, where Moonglow wrote its own layout of the same document (a module folder kept in git showed a file saved by Aurora as changed after an edit and its Undo). `mg_edit::Workspace`'s write-back gives a document that is again as the file was opened or last saved that file's bytes. From James Reeves's GitHub pull request 36, whose other half (only the documents edited are written back) 3.0.0 had already; with his tests (`an_edit_undone_gives_the_bytes_back` and two more in mg-edit, and the app's `a_module_folder_saved_with_nothing_changed_is_as_it_was` on BioWare's Neverwinter Chess as a folder). [Modules](manual/03-modules.md) says so.
* **Fix**: A window's foot no longer goes up and down (GitHub issue 38: at some sizes a properties window's OK and Cancel jumped and its right edge flickered every frame, until it was resized). At a display scale of 125%, the scroll area egui_dock puts round a tab rounded its content to pixels a sliver past itself, and its scroll bars came and went each frame. The windows with OK and Cancel at their foot that did it now fit their pane, as the script editor and the Options do (`TabViewer::scroll_bars`): Module, Area (and several areas'), blueprint, placed object and GFF Properties, whose page scrolls both ways over the foot, and the journal, conversation and talk table editors, whose fields and lists scroll both ways (the talk table's Find row wraps, as the rows under it do). The faction, hak, 2DA and tileset editors did not move and keep the pane's scroll bars. Under test (`a_properties_window_s_buttons_stay_put`: eleven windows at scales 100% to 150%, at sizes where seven of them moved; a sweep of 504 sizes found them all at 125% alone); two frames in a row at 125%, before and after, in `screens.rs`'s `properties_window_at_125_percent`, and the three editors in a narrow window (`talk-table-long-narrow`, `journal-narrow`, `conversation-narrow`).
* **Fix**: A body part whose own material names no `texture0` (normal and specular maps alone, as a hak's parts often have) is drawn in the human's PLT of its name, as the game draws it, where it was drawn untextured (GitHub issue 37: `pfa0_bicepl001`, whose mesh names `pfa0_bicepl001.mtr`, in `pfh0_bicepl001.plt`). Such a material is no texture of its name to the part fallbacks (`mg_preview`'s `has_texture`, which reads that material alone for its `texture0`); in the area view, the creature and item previews alike. Under test with an authored material and model (`a_part_s_material_without_texture0_takes_the_human_s_plt`), and seen before and after in `creatures_look` (an elf's bicep 1 with such a material in the scratch override: untextured, then its bare arm).
* **Feature**: Shadows quality, Fast or High (Options › Area, kept in the settings, and the area view's Shadows menu), the owner's ask: Fast, the shadow map as before (the default); High, the game's own stencil shadow volumes (`mg_render::volume`, `Renderer::shadow_volumes`): each casting trimesh extruded from the sun or a creature's light on the GPU as `vs_shadowvol` does (the lit side moved 0.1 m, the rest to a tile's box's bottom or the light's radius, never above the camera), counted z-fail in a depth and stencil target of the view's samples, then darkened as the map's shadows are; volumes closed whatever the mesh, so an edge of three faces casts no spike. The owner's settled entry "The shadow map stands in for the game's stencil volumes" is rewritten to say both exist (a settled entry changed, at the owner's ask), and what is left is folded into the open "Shadows" entry of [the deferred list](deferred.md). Beside the client at its highest shadow setting (`high_shadows_beside_the_client`: a rural fence and gallows at three sun heights, up close and over a 16×16 area, an ogre, tcn01's house, and the wiki's "finhead", which the client draws welded as unwelded, no spike) Fast and High mark nearly the same pixels and the client's as well as the cameras allow; over the large area Fast's edges are soft and stepped, High's sharp. Costs (`frame_perf` with `FRAME_SHADOW_QUALITY=high`, new, one test at a time, the machine at a load of 2 to 3.4, no client running): every view within the budget with either; drawn apart at 3000×1250 with 4× MSAA a frame takes 0.1 to 1 ms more GPU time with High (area026 seen close 3.3 to 6.7 ms, of 6.9) and 0 to 0.15 ms more encoding; the app's area084 with everything selected 2.2 to 4.0 ms of GPU; High's first frame in an area makes the volumes (area084's opening's longest frame 22 to 50 ms). Fast is as before. Tests: `volume::tests` (closed volumes and their silhouettes: a cube, an open sheet, three faces on one edge, a point light), `high_shadows_darken_exactly_the_volume_s_footprint` (every pixel of the shadow's footprint darkened by the opacity, none else, the caster's lit top not; smooth edges with four samples), the sun's and the lights' shadow tests run with High too, `the_shadows_quality_is_chosen_in_the_shadows_menu`, the settings and Options tests. [Options](manual/10-options.md#area), [Areas](manual/04-areas.md), [the notes](research/notes_shaders.md) §G.2.
* **Update**: F6 against a builder's own binding settled in [the deferred list](deferred.md) by the owner's verdict of 2026-10-30 (proposals accepted as recommended): Options › Keyboard says the conflict and the pane's key wins until one is changed.
* **Update**: The [deferred sprint](deferred-sprint.md)'s count after wave 6, Advanced Search's OR and NOT and the hak names' bytes: 71 open entries (150 items), from 440 at the sprint's start; 287 fixed, 63 verified, 55 dropped and 98 settled in the sprint (fixed and verified counted by the log's lines). What is left waits on Windows or macOS, builders, client readings, an Aurora capture, the owner, or is large (after 3.0.0).
* **Fix**: A module's custom talk table's name (`Mod_CustomTlk`) follows its haks' rule, and a hak named in another case than its file is said with the file. Settled in the engine (`engine_opens_the_talk_table_file_named_by_the_name_s_bytes`, `--test engine engine_hak_names`): the server opens the talk table in the user's `tlk/` whose file name has the name's bytes, 0xF1 and UTF-8's C3 B1 each only its own (with only the other there the module doesn't load), and `MG_PLAIN` doesn't open `mg_plain.tlk`, as with haks (`MG_PLAIN` doesn't open `mg_plain.hak` either: the hak test's new cases). The one rule is `mg_resman`'s `file_name_text`, `file_name_bytes`, `named_file` and `name_of_file` (the hak functions of the entry below, made the module's file names'), and `listed` and `differs_in_case` for case: `Module::custom_tlk`, `talk::find` and a new table's file, Module Properties' Custom TLK (its files by `GameInstall::tlk_names`, exact names), `attach::placements`, `mg attach` and `mg serve` go through them, where they read the module's codepage or UTF-8. On Linux a hak whose file differs from the module's name in case alone is not found by the game: Module Properties marks it "not found: the file is mg_plain.hak" (the window found it, matching without case) and Add hak… offers the file; Verify, `mg haks` (`not_found` in its JSON, a line under the hak in its text), the log, `mg serve` and the command line's other warnings say "hak MG_PLAIN not found: the game opens a hak only by its exact name, and …/mg_plain.hak has its name in another case" (`GameInstall::hak_not_found`). On Windows and macOS, whose file systems take one case for another (`CASE_IGNORED`), nothing is said: [Modules](manual/03-modules.md) says so (not tested on Windows or macOS). Tests: `file_name::tests` (`a_name_in_another_case`, `a_name_listed_in_another_case`), `a_hak_named_in_another_case_is_not_found_on_linux` (`--test app resources`), `a_hak_named_in_another_case_is_said_with_its_file` (`--test cli attach`: the talk table attached by its UTF-8 bytes too).
* **Fix**: A module's hak names are read and written by one rule, the game's (the inconsistency fix package 05 found on 2026-10-29: Module Properties read `Mod_Hak` in the module's codepage, the layering, `mg` and NWSync as UTF-8). Settled in the engine (`engine_opens_the_hak_file_named_by_the_name_s_bytes`, `--test engine engine_hak_names`): the server opens the file whose name has the name's bytes and converts nothing; `ñ` as Windows-1252's 0xF1 opens `mg_\xF1hak.hak`, `ñ` in UTF-8 `mg_ñhak.hak`, each only its own (with only the other there the module doesn't load), the older single `Mod_Hak` alike. `mg_resman::hak_name` holds a name's bytes as Windows-1252 text (every byte a character and back) and `hak_file_name` makes the file's name of it (on Linux and macOS its bytes; on Windows the text, for the system's codepage: not tested, the server runs on Linux here); `haks_of`, `find_hak`, `GameInstall::hak_names` (Add hak…'s list, the file's own name, no longer lower case), Module Properties' list and Add hak…, `attach::hak_list` and `placements` (`mg attach`, Add Haks and Talk Table…, Custom Light), `mg serve`, a plugin's test folder and the NUI pictures' hak go through them. A hak whose file was named `ñ` on Linux was offered by Add hak… as `ñ` and written as 0xF1, which the game doesn't open; one named 0xF1 in a module was layered by no file. The engine is case-sensitive too on Linux (`MG_PLAIN` doesn't open `mg_plain.hak`), which Module Properties' "not found" doesn't follow (it matches without case): not changed here. Tests: `hak_name::tests` (mg-resman), `a_hak_s_name_is_its_file_s_bytes` (`--test app resources`), `a_hak_is_named_by_its_file_s_bytes` (`--test cli attach`). [Modules](manual/03-modules.md).

* **Fix**: Advanced Search finds what meets any of its conditions, and leaves out what meets one ticked Not (the deferred list's "Advanced Search, what it doesn't do", its OR and NOT; the owner chose to build them): **Find objects** chooses all or any once there are two conditions (the rows read And or Or), and each condition but the first has a **Not**, which leaves out exactly what an And of it would keep (the same object, one holding it, one held by it); a session keeps both. `mg_module::search::Query` has `any` and `not`; `mg search` takes `--any`, and `--not` before the condition it leaves out (`--class fighter --not --feat alertness`). Aurora's Find Instance has neither (its form in the [UI inventory](parity/aurora-ui-inventory.md)): Moonglow's own design. What the AND searches find is unchanged (their tests as they were; Chapter 1's fighters of 4 to 10 levels with Alertness still 54). Tests `any_of_the_conditions_and_those_not_met` (a NOT and its AND add up to what the first finds), `conditions_not_met_and_any_of_them_are_asked_and_kept`, `advanced_search_leaves_out_a_condition_and_finds_any_of_them`, `search_for_any_condition_and_leave_one_out`; pictures before and after (`screens.rs`'s `advanced_search`, `advanced-search-and` and the new `advanced-search-or-not`). ([Modules](manual/03-modules.md), [Command-line tools](manual/11-command-line.md))
* **Fix**: Grass sways in the area's wind with either shader (the deferred list's "A grass tuft's sway"): a tile's grass is a skin of two bones, its root holding the tufts' feet and a sway node carrying their tops (`mg_area::grass::SWAY_NODE`), posed by `grass::sway` as the client's grass moved in `reading_grass_sway_by_clock`: all the tufts together, north and south, at `WindPower` 2 between 0.055 m south and 0.098 m north of their feet, a swing of 4 s; at 1 between 0.027 and 0.045 m, a swing of 7 s (the client's fell for more than 3.4 s); at 0 still (not read in the client). Moonglow's shader and the game's `vsgrass` both skin it as they skin a creature (the game's `inc_transform` reads `skinmesh`): no change to the renderer. Grass put together in chunks far off (past 180 m) stands still. The swing taken as a sine's and the grass at no wind are in [the differences](manual/12-differences.md); [Areas](manual/04-areas.md) says it sways. `frame_perf`'s grass field is in a strong wind: its views within the budget as before (two runs each way in turn, the machine at a load of 10 to 14). Tests: `grass_sways_in_the_wind_with_either_shader` (mg-ui: still before), `a_tuft_s_top_is_carried_by_the_sway_and_its_feet_held`, `grass_sways_as_far_and_as_fast_as_the_client_s`.

Test: `a_material_that_samples_the_framebuffer_is_drawn_after_the_shadows` (mg-render).

* **Update**: Animations bound by part number (the deferred list's entry): the 70 game models where binding by number and by name differ (152 nodes, `binding_by_part_number_and_by_name` run again) sorted into their two kinds (a node of the supermodel's name numbered −1 or afresh: `c_blade_m`'s `head_g`; old models whose numbers fall on a later supermodel's new nodes: `c_mohrg`'s dangles under `a_ba`'s cloak bones), and the client reading that would settle them named (`c_mohrg` and `c_blade_m` walking).
* **Fix**: The rule by which the game's server refuses a tileset (the deferred list's "A tileset with holes", its second item), read in the engine (`a_tileset_whose_lines_end_both_ways`, fifteen files, side by side): a line of more than 255 characters, its CR and LF not counted, stops a module loading wherever it is and however it ends (255 loads, 256 doesn't, with CRLF too; 300 in the middle doesn't); and more than 256 bytes after the file's last CRLF do (256 bytes of LF lines load, 260 don't; ttr01's last 27 lines, 251 bytes, load, its last 28, 264, don't). Other LF lines load and read as CRLF ones, 600 bytes of them before a last CRLF line too. (The 389-byte line of the earlier reading failed by its length, not its LF.) Verify's `set-line-ends` says each refusal as an error, the line too long by its number, and keeps a warning for a mix the server reads. The entry keeps its first item, waiting on the builder's hak.
* **Verification**: A walkmesh's own node position (the deferred list's entry, Tyrants of the Moonsea's `ptm_candle02.pwk`, its mesh 72 m from the candle): the engine honors it, as Moonglow draws it. `engine_placeable_walkmesh.rs` (kept this time, in the server through `run_server`) walks a creature with no scripts straight across five lanes: past a wagon of the game's 0.9 m aside, past a 4 m square of ours replacing a placeable's walkmesh 2 to 6 m aside (a module's copy and an override's both read), past a square whose node is 15 m from its placeable 2.3 m aside at the square, and straight over that placeable's own spot. Making a creature on such a place had not moved it (the probe of 2026-10-29): what a creature is made on is not how it walks.

* **Fix**: An appearance with no model, what the warning left out (the deferred list's entry, dansen9191's report): the names of an item's and a body's models moved down into `mg_rules::models` (the previews, the usage report and the rule share them), and `AppearanceRow::parts` judges past the row the models an object's parts name: an item's pieces (a weapon's three, a helmet's, a ring's, a cloak's as a man or a woman wears it) and an armor's parts, a body of parts' skeleton (its phenotype's or the default's: none is as an appearance with no model) and its head and parts. Each missing one is a line under the field in the Properties (`an_item_s_and_a_body_s_parts_without_models_are_said`, pictures before and after) and a warning in Verify, placed or not (the rest is drawn). An item none of whose own models are there is drawn as its base item's `DefaultModel`, as the game draws its potions: said only when that is missing too (the first try warned of 3,930 potions in Contest of Champions alone). Verify also reads each model of the module's or a hak's that an object names, once (kept between runs as the tile models' faces are), and says one that is there and can't be read, with why (`an_object_s_parts_and_unreadable_models`). Over the whole install two modules' findings came: Tyrants of the Moonsea's three armors of robes 12 and 16, which no body has; TDoD's module, two weapons' missing pieces. The objects' check takes 0.58 s on Tyrants of the Moonsea and 0.02 s on TDoD's module (`mg verify --timings`).

* **Fix**: An area's view with everything selected and the walkmesh shown is back within the 6.94 ms budget (`frame_perf`'s `sound_ranges_frames_at_144`, Tyrants of the Moonsea's area084 at 3440×1400, 549 objects selected, the camera turning at 120 m): 5.8 to 6.2 ms a frame with Sound Ranges on and 5.8 off (load average 6 to 7 on 32 threads), from 12.1 to 13.8 and 8.3 to 9.8 at a load of 2 to 8. Stack samples (`eu-stack`) and the view timed without each overlay showed where it went: Sound Ranges' 135,000 dashes made, converted and sent to the GPU every frame (~3.5 ms), the walkmesh's 67,000 faces each cut at the near plane and put on screen with two allocations and the camera worked out again (~2.5 ms), the renderer's choice of the lights reaching each of ~4,000 meshes (~1.2 ms) and the selection's boxes (~1 ms). The picture is the same to the pixel but for the log's clock (`FRAME_SHOTS=1`, which now shoots a view as its frames have it). * **Fix**: NWSync's data files are compressed at zstd's level 3 by default, as `nwn_nwsync_write` compresses them, and at any level from 1 to 22 with `mg nwsync --level` (the deferred list's "Compression", the owner approving the dependency): the `zstd` crate, the reference library's C built from the sources zstd-sys ships (BSD-3-Clause, no system library at run time, built for the Windows target by `cargo clippy --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`; credited in `packaging/third_party_licenses.py`), where ruzstd's encoder had only its fastest level; ruzstd still reads. On the game's `potsc_resources.hak` (110 MB; the machine's load 2 to 3 on 32 CPUs): level 1, 52.1 MB in 0.4 s; 3, 47.3 MB in 0.5 s (`nwn_nwsync_write` 47.4 MB in 0.6 s); 6, 46.1 MB in 0.8 s; 9, 45.5 MB in 1.0 s; 12, 45.4 MB in 1.9 s; 15, 44.5 MB in 3.6 s; 19, 42.2 MB in 10 s; 22, 42.2 MB in 18 s (`levels_measured_on_a_hak`, run by hand). `every_level_is_read_by_neverwinter_nim`: levels 1, 3, 9, 19 and 22 of `sg_resources.hak`, read file for file by `nwn_compressedbuf` (the reference library as neverwinter.nim builds it in), each no bigger than the level below. * **Fix**: The UI tests (`--test app`) pass on a loaded machine, as CI's runners are. Most of the 1 to 37 failures a run seen when two full runs shared this machine were the two runs themselves: both wrote the same `target/test-output/` folders, each run's `scratch_dir` emptying them under the other's tests (files gone, an NWSync upload's parts sent twice, a project folder holding the other's claims table). `mg_testkit::test_output` now honors `MOONGLOW_TEST_OUTPUT` for a run beside another (CLAUDE.md says so); with it, pairs on the whole machine, or on 4 or 2 CPUs with a test thread a CPU, failed only on a test that spelled the folder out (now through `test_output`). Under CI's kind of load (both runs on 4 or 2 CPUs, 32 test threads each) 6 of 12 runs failed: the tile search in Tile Properties' All tiles 5 times and the talk table test once, `Harness::run exceeded max_steps (4)`, and the test of a game Moonglow did not start once. Work finished on a thread or timed by the clock asked for frames at once in the middle of a test's run (kittest takes a frame asked for sooner than its 250 ms step as one at once): the look at the module's files polled every 50 ms while it went on, a watch's change, a finished look's or the game's programs' wake each added two or three frames, the script editor's live check spun out its half-second pause, and a gallery's pictures, a few milliseconds' worth a frame, met the area view's animation step. The window now asks for those frames at once only where it keeps going (`background_jobs`, the desktop app: `jobs::wake`, `Moonglow::frame_after`), and in the tests at the next frame they draw; the look's thread asks for its frame when it is done instead of the 50 ms poll. `Moonglow::under_way` says what of the window's own work is going on (a job, a look, the scripts it read to compile, a watch hearing a burst of changes, `Watch::hearing`, pictures to make or being read, an area's reading, the lit check, the references, an update check), and the tests' `settle` waits for it and for the frames to stop, with a 30-second deadline instead of 400 tries; the helpers that type into a filter and choose a palette's type settle, and the talk table test settles after its save. The test of a game Moonglow did not start names its module by the process (another run's stand-in game was found on `mgtest`), and the armor part colors test reads its saved module through `test_output`. After: 24 of 24 full runs, each with another beside it, passed: 18 under that load (12 on 4 CPUs, 6 on 2) and 6 on the whole machine. No assertion weakened, none ignored; `frame_perf`, `world_perf` and the world tests, run by hand, keep their own fixed folders
* **Fix**: The NUI preview does three things as the second client batch read them in the game (`nui_readings_in_the_client`, the deferred list's "Where the preview is known to differ from the game"): a row's last button without a width stretches to a control with a width of its own after the row in its column, until the row is as wide as it less 2, never to one before it (one button under an image 200 wide is 196, two under 400 are 150 and 242: `a_row_s_last_button_stretches_to_a_wider_control_below_it`); at a UI scale that isn't whole each margin, and the gap of two margins between controls, is whole pixels rounded down as a control's size is (ten buttons 30 high are 37 and 43 apart at 111% with margins 2 and 5: `margins_are_whole_pixels_at_a_scale_that_isn_t_whole`); a number in text is the bind's value as a 32-bit float, to as many places as asked (no cap at 16), ties to even (1/3 at 17 places 0.33333334326744080, 2.5 at none 2: `numbers_in_text_are_the_client_s`), where the contributor's reading of 2026-10-08 had ties away from zero (42.125 at 2 places as 42.13): the two readings disagree, and [the deferred list](deferred.md) asks the client for that one again. Pictures before and after of each; the [manual](manual/18-nui-creator.md) says so

No `cutter` in `nwtoolset.exe`, `nwserver-linux` or `nwmain-linux` (their strings, ASCII and UTF-16), nor in the game's `nwscript.nss` (whose object types are creature, item, trigger, door, area of effect, waypoint, placeable, store, encounter and tile) or its talk table; the server's `CNWSTrigger` loads and saves one kind of trigger, its `Type` generic (0), area transition (1) or trap (2), the three Moonglow draws and places.
