* **Fix**: NWSync publishing's "No upload" (the owner approved it on 2026-10-29 and left the way to the sprint): Build › Publish to NWSync's **Upload** sends the repository to the web server by the builder's own command, set in Options › Folders or the project's `[nwsync] upload` (`moonglow.toml`, or `.moonglow/user.toml`, which wins; asked about before it first runs and allowed by its text, as `[commands]` are), never by a way in or a credential of Moonglow's: rsync, scp, WinSCP, `aws s3 sync`, rclone, a share, each with its own login. It runs in the repository's folder once for each part (`{part}`, `{folder}`: `mg_module::nwsync::upload_command`), the data, then the manifests, then `latest`, each after the one before succeeded, since one command over the folder sends `latest` before `manifests/` (rsync goes by name) and nwserver and players' games read the server meanwhile; `latest` naming a missing manifest sends nothing (`upload_parts`). After Remove Unused Data the manifests go before the data (a command with `--delete` takes a manifest away before its data). **Upload after publishing and after removing unused data** chains it; it is a job with its output as a project command's (`project_commands::run_steps`, the runner both share now), Cancel, Show Output. `mg nwsync --upload [COMMAND]` and `mg nwsync-prune --upload COMMAND` for scripts. Tests: `an_upload_s_parts_and_commands`, `the_nwsync_upload_command_is_read_from_either_file` (mg-module), `the_nwsync_repository_is_uploaded_part_by_part`, `a_project_s_nwsync_upload_is_asked_about_first`, `an_nwsync_upload_canceled_sends_nothing_more`, `published_to_nwsync_from_the_build_menu` (`--test app`), `every_command_answers_in_json` and `a_pruned_repository_is_mirrored_by_rsync` (rsync to a folder of the test's), all stand-ins sending nowhere but scratch folders; pictures before and after (`nwsync_publish_and_prune`, `options_window` in `screens.rs`: `nwsync-uploading`, `nwsync-uploaded`). The [manual](manual/09-build-and-test.md#uploading-to-the-web-server) says why so, and how for each tool. Closes the deferred entry.

Pictures before and after, the same pixel for pixel in the view: the area view with the Domains of Dread's ash zombie and badgers, one across the view's edge, both shaders (`area_creatures_game_shaders`). What stays: the area's objects are still posed each frame wherever they are (`mg-area`), as the shadows they cast into the view need. A renderer change, through CI on a branch.
* **Fix**: What the GPU refuses of the renderer's drawing no longer ends Moonglow (the deferred list's "A model that fails while it is drawn"): a texture it won't take (larger than it holds: Moonglow reads up to 16384 pixels a side, many cards take 8192; data it refuses) is uploaded under the device's error scopes and drawn as a missing one, and one read in the frame that breaks what reads it is none, as on the threads that read them apart; the application's device notes every other error of its drawing instead of wgpu's panic (`mg_render::guard::note_gpu_errors`, `take_gpu_errors`; tests' devices keep the panic). The log says "The GPU refused part of what is drawn and it is left out", once each ([Troubleshooting](manual/13-troubleshooting.md)). Tests: `a_texture_the_gpu_refuses_is_left_out_and_said` and `the_application_s_device_notes_what_the_gpu_refuses` (mg-render), `a_texture_the_gpu_refuses_is_left_out_and_told` (`--test app`: a ground texture 16384 wide in an area, the area drawn without it), `what_the_gpu_refuses_is_said_once_on_a_line`. Pictures looked at: the three cards (`texture_refused.png`) and the area (`refused.png`); before, there was none: the program ended. A panic in the renderer's own frame code is still a crash, as Moonglow's own mistake. A renderer change, through CI on a branch.

* **Update**: CI made faster again, after the morning's measurement (below). Where its time went: develop had no cache left (GitHub keeps 10 GB a repository; the seven caches there, 9.5 GB, were all renderer-ci's, each of its pushes that changed a manifest saving a new 3.8 GB set), so develop's runs started cold (40872200532's macOS 23.8 minutes, 40798056556's Windows 41); and warm, every Test job was its build (Windows 10m44 of an 11.4-minute Test step in 40645701826, the tests 40 s; Linux 5m00, macOS 5m09), mg-ui the long pole, after fmt and clippy (2 minutes on Windows) and, on Linux, the disk's clean-up (1.8) and a second build of the 26 libraries for the doc tests (1m50). Changed: caches saved by develop alone (ci.yml and release.yml; other branches restore develop's); fmt and clippy in a Lint job per system beside the Test job; Linux's clean-up in the background; the tests built without debug information (`CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0`: the doc tests' libraries are then the tests' own, as the unit graphs show, and the build at -j4 here took 121 and 117 s against 147 and 136, the machine loaded 7 to 13 by other builds); and each Test job's `--timings` report kept as an artifact. The same checks on the same three systems. [The plan](PLAN.md)'s Testing strategy says how CI runs. Measured on GitHub (run 40971587639 on tmp/ci-speed, cold, as no cache was left): the run took 25.7 minutes against the cold 40798056556's 41.5 (Windows' Test job 25.5 against 41.3, Linux's 14.8 against 26.1, macOS' 17.0 against 16.8; the Lint jobs 3.2 to 13.2 beside them), Free disk space 0 s; its `timings-*` reports show Windows building each unit, compile and link alike, about 1.8 times as long as Linux (mg-ui's tests 401 s against 226), so Windows' `rust-lld`, also tried, was taken out again: from `Compiling mg` to the end of the build, where the large links are, it took 163 s against link.exe's 156 (warm, 40645701826) and 177 (cold). Linux's doc tests were skipped there (a timing test of the projects page failed, its author's to fix); without debug information they rebuilt nothing here.

* **Fix**: The outside-changes watch no longer reads every file again on Windows after a single file changes: Windows' watcher also says the folder a file is written in was modified, which the watch took as a folder made and read all of. A folder's own entry modified (not renamed) is now nothing of its own, its files being said themselves; a folder made, removed or moved is still all (`a_folder_modified_is_said_by_its_files`). Found by CI's Windows job (`the_watch_says_which_files_changed_and_only_then`).
* **Fix**: Add Haks and Talk Table (and `mg attach`) take content downloaded as a `.7z` or a `.rar` (RAR 4 or 5) as they take a `.zip`: its haks and talk table are listed and copied from the archive (`mg_module::attach`'s `archive`: sevenz-rust2 and rars, both pure Rust and Apache-2.0, the owner's choice of 2026-10-29; rars is written from the format's description, not from UnRAR's source, whose license the GPL can't take). An archive is read in one pass for what is copied and one for what is compared (a solid one decoded once, not once a file), its files compared with those there by their bytes; a copy that fails leaves none in place. An archive with a password, or one volume of a set, is refused, said why; two files of one name chosen (in an archive and beside it) are refused too. rar-codec, the other pure-Rust reader under a license the GPL takes, was looked at and left: over 143 archives UnRAR extracts (rars' reference set, 54 RAR 5 downloads on this machine and ours) rars gave UnRAR's bytes for every one but volumes of sets and links, rar-codec failed 35 of those (RAR 4 with a comment, a recovery record or a service block, solid RAR 4, PPMd). `a_7z_s_and_a_rar_s_haks_and_talk_table_go_to_the_user_folder` (fixtures of our own text, made by 7-Zip and rars and tested by UnRAR), `locked_and_split_archives_are_refused_and_said_why`, `a_cut_or_damaged_archive_is_an_error_never_a_panic` (zip, 7z, RAR 4 and 5: cut at every length, every byte changed), `content_downloaded_as_7z_or_rar_is_attached_from_the_archive` (`--test app`), `haks_and_a_talk_table_attach_from_a_rar_or_a_7z` (`mg attach`). The manual's Custom Content and `mg attach`. Closes the deferred entry.

* **Fix**: Files changed outside Moonglow, six of the entry's seven items (The Domains of Dread's builder proposal, C12). The watches (a module folder's or a nasher project's files, and the haks, `override`, `development` and portrait folders and the custom talk table) are told by the system which files changed (the `notify` crate: inotify, FSEvents, ReadDirectoryChangesW; a file by its folder, so one written whole and moved into place is heard), and say so once a burst is quiet for 300 ms, asking the window for a frame: it looks then, not at its next 3 s, so a change is in a moment after it settles, not up to 7 s. The look takes the watch's list (`Module::outside_scan_of`): those files alone are snapshotted and read, whatever their time (a change within the clock's grain is found), no folder walked, and only their areas' GITs taken for their locks; a folder made, moved or removed, or the system losing count, is a look at all. Where the system can't watch, the walk every 3 s stays; told, the files are still walked every 30 s, for a change the system didn't tell (a network share's). A `.mod` changed outside is read again (`mg_module::archive_file`: its time, size and resources noted as read or written, the file read again on the look's thread when they change and compared by resource), taken or asked about as a folder's file, and Save doesn't write over changes found and not yet answered. Scripts read again compile for 4 ms a frame (`compile_outside_step`), the window taking input, however many a checkout changed (more than 24 went to a job that held it). Measured (`frame_perf` `reload_frames_at_144`, the persistent world as a nasher project, 21,000 files; load 5 to 7 on 32 threads): a pull of 970 files all in 2.1 s from its start (4.6 s before), the longest frame 3.1 ms (3.5), none over the budget; one of 2,870 in 4.5 to 5.8 s (6.2), the longest 6.7 to 9.2 ms over three runs (6.5 before), the look's start 1.6 ms and its take 4.5 ms of the window's thread, both of the files changed, not of the project's. [Modules](manual/03-modules.md), [Options](manual/10-options.md), [Building and testing](manual/09-build-and-test.md). Tests: `the_watch_says_which_files_changed_and_only_then`, `the_content_watch_hears_its_files_and_folders`, `a_path_said_under_a_real_place_is_the_watched_one`, `a_look_at_the_files_named_looks_at_them_alone`, `a_folder_s_look_at_the_files_named_looks_at_them_alone`, `a_mod_changed_outside_is_found_by_resource`, `a_mod_saved_by_another_program_is_read_again`, `many_scripts_saved_outside_are_compiled_a_few_a_frame`. * **Fix**: A Verify of a module with many haks reads each hak's models once: what it finds of each model of an archive (its text's findings, `mdl-text`; a tile model's faces, `tile-faces` and `mdl-read`) is kept in the cache folder beside the shader programs that compiled (`verify/`, a file an archive named by its label, time and size, of this release: `mg_module::doctor::Cache`), and a hak that is as it was is not read again; a hak changed is, and its earlier file goes. Folders (`override`, `development`, the module's) are always read. Measured on The Domains of Dread kept as a nasher project with its 145 haks (28 GB; `--user-dir` a scratch folder linking `~/Projects/tdod-module/build/hak`), `mg --json verify --timings` under a 16 GB cap, the machine shared (load 18 to 37 on 32 threads): before, 1.7 to 2.9 s wall and 27 to 30 s of the workers' time (lint 13 s for 1.9 GB of text models, the text tiles' face bound 5.4 s for 1.2 GB, the compiled tiles' 1.3 s for 2.6 GB); now 2.3 s and 23.5 s the first time (the cache written in 0.24 s), then 0.87 to 1.25 s and 8.1 to 8.5 s over seven rounds (with `var-script`, below, 21 ms of it), at most 0.9 GB held rather than 1.3 to 1.6; the JSON byte for byte the same in every round. What a first Verify still does as before: lint every text model and read every tile model (a text tile model read twice, by the linter and for its faces), and on every run the 2DAs (671, 3 to 5 s of the workers' time, `appearance.2da` 0.43 s: the longest part of a Verify whose models are known). [Building and testing](manual/09-build-and-test.md). Tests: `an_archive_s_models_are_read_once_while_it_is_as_it_was`, `facts_read_back_as_written`. Closes the deferred entry.

And found in doing it: a command canceled left the module's haks closed and its project files unwatched until the module was opened again (a canceled job hands nothing over, and the reopening was in its hand-over); they are taken back when it ends so too (`a_project_s_command_canceled_reads_the_project_s_files_again`). Going to a line (a compiler message, Definition, References) stays in Moonglow's editor. Manual: the command-line chapter.
* **Fix**: a module's haks are layered into the game data again (a builder's report on 2.13.1, Windows: every module opened said its haks "could not be added to the game data (it is in use)", closed and opened again or not). The 3D views kept the game data their textures are read apart from (`Viewport3d::textures_from`, since 2.10.0) for good, in the viewport's cache, the renderer's texture reader and its threads; since 2.13.1 the lit check filled that cache at startup, so the first module failed, and before it every module opened after an area had been drawn did. Whatever needs the game data to itself had silently done nothing meanwhile: Close left the old module's haks layered, edits weren't layered into the game data (`refresh_module_layer`, `update_module_layer`), nor Module Properties' hak list, the custom talk table, Reload Resources and its watch, a tileset's minimap pictures. Now each of them first has the views let go of it (`Moonglow::release_game_data`: the viewport's cache and the renderer's readers, taken again when an area next draws; and, ten seconds at most, what still reads it on a thread, such as an area of a module just closed; never a job) before `exclusive`; the content watch asks whether anything else holds it (`game_data_held`) and has the views let go only when something changed. The lit check reads the game's 92 programs (`.shd`) out of the game data first (0.3 ms) and holds none of it while it runs, so a module opened in the first frame (`moonglow path/to/module.mod`) layers its haks too. Tests in `--test app resources`: `a_module_s_haks_are_layered_with_the_lit_check`, `…_after_an_area_was_drawn` (Reload Resources with textures still being read, which are asked for again and drawn, then Close) and `…_after_one_closed_while_its_area_was_read`, failing before (the first with the builder's message; the other two also without the wait).
* **Update**: The lit check's notice says what it found: where the game's shaders draw its red test mesh in the wrong colors (Heed's Vulkan on a Radeon RX 580, 2.13.1: [212, 133, 133], washed-out pink), it says so, that Moonglow's own draw it right and that Moonglow draws with its own for the rest of the run, not that they "draw nothing right" (the area was drawn); where they draw nothing of it, it says that; Moonglow's own shader's notice likewise. The pink is exactly the stock `fslit` with `fNdotV` zero (the surface lit as if seen edge on: the environment specularity's Fresnel term at a grazing angle, 0.29 for 0.04, the diffuse unchanged); no uniform, texture, buffer, vertex input or uninitialized value of Moonglow's differs by driver (each written or zeroed, checked by filling them with other values and by forcing the program's terms here). What does change the program is the load order the check read it through: `override/`, `development/`, Workshop items and the module's haks, where a builder's `inc_lighting` draws so. The check now draws the game's own copies (`Assets::game_shader`, the keys'; `shader_origin` says where the load order's copy is), its debug-log line names any copy the load order puts over them and the color each shader drew, and `probe::Lit` keeps the two pictures. Tests: `a_shader_s_game_copy_and_where_the_load_order_s_comes_from` (mg-render), the lit-check render test's colors, `a_builder_s_include_leaves_the_lit_check_to_the_game_s_own` (corpus: the pink drawn by an overriding include, red by the check), `the_lit_check_turns_the_game_s_shaders_off_where_they_draw_wrong` (mg-ui: Heed's colors, the notice's words). [Findings](findings.md) (The lit check's pink on Heed's Vulkan), [Troubleshooting](manual/13-troubleshooting.md), [the deferred list](deferred.md): Heed's interiors' lighting entry says what the next release's log line will tell.
* **Update**: A model whose textures are read apart (the area view where jobs run in the background, as in the desktop app) asks for every mesh's textures in its first frame: the renderer stopped at the first mesh still waiting, so the next mesh's were asked for only once that one's were read, a round of reads a mesh, and a tile of several textured meshes stayed out of the view (black) that many rounds. The rural tileset's tile with a rock took six (`ttr01_stone06` … `ttr01_dirt04`, about 110 ms here), and the lit check's picture (`renderer_check::the_lit_check_turns_the_game_s_shaders_off_where_they_draw_nothing`) was taken in the middle of them: one tile black. Nothing of the game's shaders: the tile was left out before the switch to Moonglow's own as after it (118 meshes drawn on both sides, 142 once read), and the picture was black from the test's first commit (3680a48f), drawn or not as the lit check and the reads raced. A new render test, `a_model_s_meshes_ask_for_their_textures_together`, holds a three-mesh model to the frame after one round; the lit check's test waits for the textures and the game's programs, then asserts every mesh still drawn after the switch and each of the 16 tiles lit at its middle in the picture.

## 2026-10-28
* **Update**: Direct3D 12 compiles shaders with DXC (the owner's decision on the FXC entry): the Windows installer and zip put Microsoft's DirectX Shader Compiler `dxcompiler.dll` (x64, release v1.9.2609 pinned by its SHA-256, downloaded as the package is built: `packaging/windows/dxc.ps1`) beside `moonglow.exe` and `mg.exe`, and every wgpu instance Moonglow makes (the window's, the headless device's, the tests') names that file (`mg_render::dx12`: by its whole path, loaded first; FXC where it is missing or won't load; `WGPU_DX12_COMPILER` still decides). The debug log's `graphics:` line ends with the compiler taken. `dxil.dll` isn't needed (`dxcompiler.dll` alone signs what it compiles: checked) and isn't shipped; DXC is NCSA- and MIT-licensed, and its texts and notices are in `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt`. Checked under Wine (`tools/dx12/dxc.sh`, the arguments wgpu gives DXC): the install's 38 distinct stages of the game's programs all compile at shader models 6.0, 6.6 and 6.8, `fslit_nm` and `fslit_sm_nm` among them, which FXC still can't (X3511). A new render test, `a_texture_read_in_a_loop_of_a_varying_count_compiles_and_draws`, draws an authored shader with the same construct (a texture read with derivatives in a loop whose count varies by pixel; FXC compiles one whose count is a uniform alone) and says which compiler; CI's Windows job puts the pinned DLL beside the test binaries and requires DXC there (`MOONGLOW_REQUIRE_DXC=1`). With DXC, wgpu offers no Direct3D 12 adapter whose driver lacks shader model 6. [Troubleshooting](manual/13-troubleshooting.md) (Direct3D 12's shader compiler), [the deferred list](deferred.md): **FXC can't compile the normal-mapped lit programs** closed; what DXC on Heed's own driver shows added to his waiting entry.
* **Update**: The area view's Alt + middle click puts the camera's focus on the ground clicked (El Grillo's ask, Blender's Alt + middle click): Alt + middle click alone (a plain middle click does nothing, so a short middle drag never jumps the view). The focus goes at once to the point on the walkmesh, else on the floor of the tile there at its height; the distance, turn and tilt stay; the sky and the ground past the area's edge do nothing, and Ctrl or Shift with it leave it to the middle drags. Mouse gestures stay fixed (not in Options › Keyboard, as settled). The model viewer has no point to pick on (no ground, no ray against the model), so it has none. [Areas › The camera](manual/04-areas.md)
* **Update**: A tile's textures (Leoendethas' request): Tile Properties, a tile's view and the tileset editor's tile list the textures the tile's model draws, each with its picture, its file (DDS, TGA or PLT, size, format, bytes), where in the load order it comes from (the game, a hak by name, override, module), what draws it (the mesh nodes, the slot, the material it is drawn through, the environment map a TXI names, emitters and flares) and the missing ones marked; one listing (`mg_preview::replaceable::uses` and `texture_file`) that the Visuals page's texture replacements now come from too. [Areas](manual/04-areas.md), "A tile's textures".
* **Update**: Return types declared one way and defined another compile as in Aurora (El Grillo's report: scripts that compile in Aurora fail in Moonglow; the base game's `x2_inc_cutscene` fails every includer). The built-in compiler (neverwinter.nim 0972fc1f, as nwn_script_comp 2.3.1) refuses a function declared with one return type and defined with another; Aurora (8193.37) compiles it, the type met first kept at the calls. Watched in Aurora with a probe module (`tools/aurora/capture_scripts.py`, captures `script-compile`): `x2_inc_cutscene`'s includers, the mismatch both ways, include files, comments of every form. A marked patch of the vendored compiler (its [README](../crates/mg-script/nwscript/README.md)) gives Aurora's bytes, all 19 of the probe's; 338 scripts of the base game and the shipped modules compile now (all four mismatches met there are definitions that return nothing). The compile warns instead, naming the function and both lines, with what the game does (`engine_return_types`: the declared type's empty value; a value where `void` was declared overwrites the caller's last variable; another type stops the script where it is used): in the Compiler messages and the log, once per warning in Compile All, `mg compile` and `mg watch` (`"warnings"` in their JSON), and in `mg lsp`. Also: an `#include` commented out includes nothing (Verify reported one in a block comment missing; the includers compiled with an include, and Rename, read it), `#include` is read one way (`mg_script::lex::includes`), and a script whose `main` follows broken code (a "nested" block comment) is reported, as Aurora reports it, not passed over as an include. [Scripts](manual/07-scripts.md), [the deferred list](deferred.md) (`#include` read three ways, closed; the include files' entry seen again).
* **Update**: Heed's armourer (`hss_armourer`, the area he sent as still lit unlike the game): drawn in the client and in the area view from four cameras, it matches within 0.1 to 1.6 of 255 over the picture and 3.1 in any region, the Shaders switch's two pictures the same (`heed_armourer_look`, a new client comparison that builds his area of stock content: `tni01`'s smithy in its black filler, his tiles' lights, 60/170, fog of 5, the innkeeper; `a_builders_area_in_the_view_draws_as_the_comparison` holds the window's picture of his own file to it). **A tile's emitters run ahead** (fixed: a forge's fire and a chimney's smoke were dark for their first seconds after the area opened or changed, an object's were not; `a_tile_s_emitters_burn_from_the_first_frame`). [Findings](findings.md): a tile's main lights take the row's color over the node's own, black or not, and a tile without light nodes lights none of its settings; Lighting Scheme is Aurora's preset only. [Deferred](deferred.md): "Heed's tile lights" and "Heed's interior washed out with the game's shaders" made one entry, waiting on Heed's description, a picture and his haks (2 closed, 1 added).
* **Update**: Heed's Radeon RX 580 still drew nothing of an area through Direct3D 12 with 2.13.0, and neither check said so. What could get past them, found in the code and closed: **the watch** (`mg_render::watch`) now judges frames that stay not ready with nothing of what they wait for finished for 20 s (`PATIENCE`: a texture never read left every tile out, and no look counted), expects tiles whose models were read and failed (`AreaScene::failed_tiles`), gives up a look the GPU doesn't give back, reads the picture's color as well as its depth, and writes what it sees to the debug log (`graphics watch:` lines). The game's pipelines catch internal and out-of-memory errors as well as validation ones (Direct3D 12's FXC failing is internal: it reached the device's default handler, a panic and a crash report), and their failures go to the log, not stderr. **The lit check** (`probe::probe_lit`): once the game's data is read, a lit, BC1-textured mesh drawn by Moonglow's own shader and by the game's `vslit`/`fslit`, apart from the window's thread (25 and 40 ms here); where only the game's draw nothing, Moonglow's own draws for the session. **HLSL as Direct3D 12 writes it** (`mg_testkit::hlsl`, `tools/dx12/`): Moonglow's own shaders (29 stages, on every platform's tests) and the game's programs as the worker gives them to wgpu (the install's 38 distinct stages), compiled by Microsoft's FXC under Wine: all of Moonglow's compile; of the game's, `fslit_nm` and `fslit_sm_nm` don't (X3511, their height-map loop), so on Direct3D 12 those meshes fall back to Moonglow's own shader. The watch's warm-up test made deterministic. [Troubleshooting](manual/13-troubleshooting.md) (the lit check, what to send), [the deferred list](deferred.md): Heed's entry rewritten (what is closed, what waits on him), El Grillo's report on Direct3D 12 noted, the FXC failure filed, **Renderer changes not yet on Direct3D 12 and Metal** closed (2.13.0's CI drew them on both).
* **Update**: Unused scripts (Jasperre's report). **A script is one line**, with the files the module has of it (`Unused: x.nss (source and compiled)`, `compiled only (no source)`, `source only (not compiled)`), in Build Module and `mg verify --unused` (whose JSON `unused` is now objects: `resource`, `names`, `files`). **What counts as used**, beyond the fields and `#include`s it read before: a string in a script that spells a name (`ExecuteScript("x")`, `CreateObject`, what an `ExecuteScriptChunk` quotes; not a script's own name, nor comments); the scripts the game runs from its 2DAs as the module sees them (`spells.2da` ImpactScript, `vfx_persistent.2da` ONENTER/ONEXIT/HEARTBEAT, `statescripts.2da` SCRIPTNAME, `traps.2da` TrapScript, `disease.2da` End_Incu_Script/24_Hour_Script, `poison.2da` Script_1/Script_2; each checked against nwn.wiki and the game's tables, `areaeffects.2da` left out as the engine doesn't read it), a new column kind `script` (`mg.twoda.kinds`, the 2DA editor's tips) that also goes into `mg haks --usage`; what the module reaches in its haks and the game names (Kingmaker's 1,220 unused scripts are 205: its conversations and blueprints are in its hak); and a module table's column described `kind = "script"`. **Marks**: the project file's `[used] scripts`, `conversations`, `blueprints` (names and globs; beside a `.mod`, `NAME.moonglow.toml`, made where there is none), written by Build Module's **Mark as Used** (a button and the line's menu) and **Counted as Used** (listed, Remove, Add), and by `mg used`. Find References and `mg refs` say which table runs a script and which mark counts it. [Build, verify and test](manual/09-build-and-test.md#what-counts-as-used), [Modules](manual/03-modules.md#the-project-file-moonglowtoml), [the command line](manual/11-command-line.md), [the plugin API](manual/17-plugin-api.md). No entry of [the deferred list](deferred.md) added or closed.
* **Update**: The renderer checks what it draws. Heed's Radeon RX 580 drew nothing of an area through Direct3D 12 (Automatic's choice for AMD on Windows since 2.11.0) and drew right through Vulkan; El Grillo's Radeon PRO lost its tiles through Vulkan: no fixed rule serves both. **The startup check** (`mg_render::probe`): before the window opens, a small scene drawn offscreen through Moonglow's own pipelines (solid, see-through, see-through over solid, skinned) and compared; where it draws nothing on Automatic, the same GPU's other backend is taken (once), the failure recorded in the settings by GPU, driver and backend, and passed over by Automatic until the driver changes (88 ms on the development machine's Vulkan). **The area view's watch** (`mg_render::watch`): once a second the depth drawn at a 64 by 36 grid against the ground of the tiles the camera sees, judged only with the pipelines ready and warm, above a floor and for five seconds; a notice names the adapter and backend and offers **Restart with …** through the close flow, with the module. Automatic's order is kept. Neither builder's case was reproduced; both are imitated with `guard::blank_draws`. ## 2026-10-27
* **Update**: [Blueprints](manual/05-blueprints.md) (Variables…) and [Troubleshooting](manual/13-troubleshooting.md#where-moonglow-keeps-its-files): variable sets are renamed and deleted (Add Set › Manage Sets…, the Variable Sets window: Rename… refuses a name another set has in any case, or one that can't name a file; Delete with Undo Delete, as the prefab palette's), saved to a file of one's choosing (Save to File…) and added from one (Add from File…, merged as Add Set merges), and their folder opened (Open Sets Folder); the manual says where the files are on each system and that they can be edited by hand (Troubletcat's and ShadowM's requests, October 2026). Rename, delete and put back are `saved::Shelf`'s, which prefabs and variable sets share. Add Set keeps its name: it merges. [The deferred list](deferred.md): what is left.
* **Update**: Options › General › **Graphics backend** ([Options](manual/10-options.md), [Troubleshooting](manual/13-troubleshooting.md#an-area-draws-nothing-or-loses-its-tiles-on-an-amd-gpu-under-windows)), from El Grillo's report (October 2026): on an AMD Radeon PRO under Windows (AMD's Vulkan driver 25.10.37.03) an area's tiles were drawn when it opened and then lost one by one, and `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` drew them right. Automatic, the default, is wgpu's choice except that an AMD GPU on Windows is taken through Direct3D 12 rather than Vulkan; Vulkan and Direct3D 12 can be chosen on Windows, Vulkan on Linux, Metal on macOS (not OpenGL, which Moonglow draws wrong: wgpu falls back to it only where nothing else draws), from the next start (read from eframe's settings file before the window opens); a backend with no adapter falls back to Automatic and the log says so; `WGPU_BACKEND` still decides over it. The choice is one function, `mg_render::backend::pick_adapter`, over the adapters' backend, vendor, device and kind (wgpu's order by power preference kept), used by the window and by the headless renderers (`mg`, the previews), which now follow `WGPU_BACKEND` too; the debug log's `graphics:` line says why the adapter was taken. What is left is in [the deferred list](deferred.md) (The install, starting and crashes).
* **Update**: [The framebuffer proposal](framebuffer-proposal.md): its spike named by its commit, `039c999b`, the branch `framebuffer-assessment` deleted with the others merged or done.
* **Update**: The review's list worked through ([Scripts](manual/07-scripts.md) and [Options](manual/10-options.md): the external compiler's limits). **Hostile files:** what GFF, TLK and binary-model readers copy from offsets that point at one stretch is capped (64 times the input and 64 MiB), a 2DA's short rows are padded to a bound (8 cells a byte and a million), a TGA's run-length path makes room by the data there, a TLK in JSON with an entry far past the rest is refused (where `nwn_tlk` builds it); truncation tests for PLT, ASCII models and walkmeshes, 2DA and SET. **Writers** refuse a model past 4 GiB, a render order or bone past its field, and a GFF value past 4 GiB before writing it. **External programs** stop after a time (the compiler two minutes, git 30 s), the compiler is given the scripts asked for and what they include (not every script), and a hak path with a comma is said where `{haks}` can't carry it. **Writes:** locks, the builder's project file and `moonglow.toml` through a temporary file; the locks file named by SHA-1 (an old one taken over), and one that can't be read is said and kept as `.unreadable`; a folder save reads each file once; a `.mod` is written straight to disk and its `.bak` linked, not copied. The hak editor finds resources by name and keeps only each step's change (20,000 resources); script stamps walk each include once (the first Compile after this recompiles every script); undo and redo keep a command that fails; a missing 2DA is looked for once. **Frames** (`frame_perf`'s new views, before and after): the log of 10,000 lines 12.5 to 0.40 ms, the Preview window of a 1,000-item store 9.36 to 0.34, the Export window of 25,000 resources 3.56 to 0.35, an area with everything selected and its walkmesh 5.4 to 4.4, typing in `nwscript.nss` 28.8 to 13.2, 12,480 particles 1.07 to 0.87; Find References and Speaker Tag's list made once. **Defects:** a placed sound took over the one deleted before it, the brush's ghost kept a blueprint's old look, a conversation whose lines own one another twice grew as 2^depth, plugin trust looked up the project folder on disk every frame. One ray-triangle test, one lightcolor.2da conversion, one `map_file`. [The deferred list](deferred.md): what is left.
* **Update**: A review of the code for defects and cost ([Modules](manual/03-modules.md): Save As into a folder) (six readers over the workspace, clippy's pedantic lints as a finder, `frame_perf` as the measure: every view within 144 fps). **Fixed, each with a test:** `mg unpack`, Export and a folder or nasher save wrote a resource named `../x` (as a crafted hak may name one) outside the folder chosen (`ResRef::is_file_name`, `ResKey::path_in`); a plugin's code could be loaded as Luau bytecode, which runs unverified (now text only); Save As into a folder of other resources deleted them (now refused, nothing deleted); a hak's compressed resource made room for the size its header claimed and read a frame without end (now bounded by the header and the frame); a model whose keys have more than 15 values was compiled to a byte that read back as a Bézier key of none (now an error); Undo of a removed field put it back at the struct's end and dropped any other of its label, and of an item that made its list left the list (now exact, so an undone file saves as it was); closing a module kept its 2DA editors, whose Save then wrote the table into the next module; a recovery copy being written as the module was saved was offered at the next start; the script editor's completion accepted after the cursor left its word panicked; the script editor's functions and error markers followed an include edited in another tab, and another install's `nwscript.nss`, only after a restart; the claims table rewritten turned a Windows-1252 name to U+FFFD and was written in place; nasher.cfg's line added turned a CRLF file to LF; a Delete of tiles that was refused never showed which cells; a spawn point held while Undo took an object before it away edited another (or panicked); a store's script named a tag of `é` wrongly; the Standard palette's tags searched another module's; the external compiler waited on Moonglow's input. **Faster:** the includers of a changed script found in one pass (a scan of every script for each found), uncompressed hak resources read without a second copy, 2DA column names looked up without an allocation per cell, blueprint and area pages share the game data's choice lists instead of copying them every frame, drop-onto-objects looks up the selection in a set. `frame_perf`'s reload test waits for every file of the pull, not the last of each kind (it failed now and then; "all in" is 3.6 s, not the 1.5 s it printed). [The deferred list](deferred.md): what the review found and left.

The command line's five tests that start the server by another program take turns three at once (`engine::timed_turn`, where one at a time made 15 s), and the corpus test that waits for a tileset with LF line ends not to load waits three times the CRLF run, not a fixed minute (the `engine` group 66 s to 25 s). The everyday suite 69 s to 27 s; the three semaphores of `mg-testkit` are one `Places`. **A defect found by it:** the window took the failures of models that broke as they were built (`mg_render::guard`, kept for the whole process) in every frame, and a test's window with no GPU took another test's; a window takes them only when it draws (in the program there is one window), and a test that makes a model fail on purpose takes the GPU alone (`gpu::alone`). The UI tests ask for a GPU adapter once, not with a second device in each test that draws. **One of each:** the day-to-date arithmetic (five copies, and ERF build dates by a loop) is `mg_core::time`; the struct a `GffPath` leads to, to change, is `GffPath::get_mut` (two hand copies gone); a ray against a box is `mg_preview::compose::ray_box` (the area view's picking and the previews'); a plugin's log level and a script's text hash once each in mg-ui; the Aurora comparisons' seven `fn lines` one `aurora_common::lines`; the command line's tests read `mg --json` with `json_out` and `quiet_json_out`; and eight tests that another nearly covered or that shared its set-up and changed nothing are part of it (each assertion kept). **Scratch folders named twice** (eight tests' pictures in one `render` folder, two script tests' modules in one, a test emptying its own `before.png`): each call of `scratch_dir` empties the folder, under any test using it beside; pictures go to `output_dir`, and `every_scratch_dir_is_named_once` holds each name to one call. * **Update**: [Plugins](manual/15-plugins.md), [Writing plugins](manual/16-writing-plugins.md), [the plugin API reference](manual/17-plugin-api.md), [the command line](manual/11-command-line.md), [the plugin API changes](plugins/CHANGES.md), [the plugins' guide](plugins/README.md), [the plugin proposal](plugin-proposal.md) and [the deferred list](deferred.md): The Domains of Dread's builder proposal (A4, A6), the last of plugin API 0.4. **A4, a resource's own events:** `resource-saving` calls a plugin's handler for each resource a save would write, with `ctx.event.old` and `new` (plain values, or text) and `changed` (a GFF's differences as lines); it warns (`ctx.event:warn`) or refuses (`ctx.event:refuse`), each with a fix made with `ctx.fix`, and the new Before saving window shows them before anything is written (Save Anyway or Cancel; a refusal stops the save; a fix is made as a step of Undo and the save asked again). `resource-saved` reads each resource written, after. `object-placed` and `object-pasted` give the objects placed or pasted. **A6, the after-create hook:** `resource-created` for each resource the Area Wizard, the creature and blueprint wizards, Add to Palette, Setup Store or a copy makes. **The decision,** recorded in the reference and the proposal's Safety: a plugin edits only on the user's word, so the handlers of a placing, a paste or a making may edit, their edits joining the user's own command (one Undo takes both back; Moonglow's own work, the builder code and the project's store rules, first), while around a save a plugin only reads, warns, refuses and offers fixes. The events that run within what the user does have 5 seconds a plugin and nobody to ask; one that fails is left out and said, and before a save is a warning, never a refusal. `mg set` and `mg apply` take `--plugins` (and the project's allowed plugins) and run a save's events (a refusal is an error); `mg plugin run --event` takes `--was`, `--select` and `--by`; a plugin's tests take `was`, `by`, `warned` and `refused`. New example: `house-rules`. The deferred list's entry on one event a save and none per resource is closed, with what A4 and A6 left undone.

Quick fixes: a check gives a finding a fix with `ctx.fix(label)` (`ctx.edit`'s methods, recording edits on a copy of the module as the check reads it); Verify Module shows a button beside the finding and makes the edits only when it is clicked, as one step of Undo, and only while what they change is as Verify read it (`mg_edit::fix::Guard`). Moonglow's own `tag-unique` (the others retagged) and `area-variables` (moved to the area's GIT) have fixes; `pc-faction` has none, the faction being the builder's choice. `mg verify --json` gives each finding's fix as an edit file, and `mg verify --fix CHECK` makes a check's fixes (`--dry-run`). A plugin's own tests: `tests/*.toml` in its folder name a fixture module (a folder, a .mod or a nasher project) and the checks, commands and events to run on it with what is to come of each (findings and their fixes, fixes made and findings left, fields, edits, the log, an error); `mg plugin test` runs them with a line a test, a summary and a failing exit for a build pipeline, and `mg plugin pack` leaves `tests/` out. * **Update**: [Modules](manual/03-modules.md) and [the deferred list](deferred.md): The Domains of Dread's builder proposal (C12), large checkouts reload without stalling. A `git pull` on a large nasher project (the persistent world kept as one, 21,000 files; 970 rewritten, added or deleted) held the window for 1.6 s in one frame: every file's time looked at and the changed ones read and converted, on the window's thread. Now the watch waits for a burst of changes to settle, a thread of its own reads what changed (`mg_module::outside`: what is known of the files taken, looked at anywhere, what still stands taken back; changes to files Moonglow saved or took meanwhile, and files found deleted that are back, are left for the next look; a file is taken with the time it had when it was read, so a write after that is found), areas' locks are found there too, and the window takes it all at once; the game data's module layer is changed in place, its tables forgotten only for a 2DA, and a project's files' times are noted at open. Conflicts are asked about as before. Longest frame 1,630 ms before, 3.5 ms after (`frame_perf` `reload_frames_at_144`, new), all in 4.6 s from the pull's start; a pull of 2,870 files (every area, 2,000 blueprints): 6.5 ms, all in 6.2 s; the status bar says *Reading files changed outside Moonglow…* meanwhile. Tests: `a_pull_s_burst_of_changes_is_read_off_the_window_s_thread` (UI), `a_look_apart_hands_back_only_what_still_stands` (mg-module). What is left is on the deferred list.

The name is cut to keep the code within 16 characters, and a name that has the builder's code already doesn't get it twice. **C2, described variables:** a project's `variables.toml` (beside `moonglow.toml`, in the manner of `name.2da.toml`) gives each local variable (by name or glob) its type, values (written, a script's constants or a table's rows), range, the objects it goes on and a line of help; `undescribed` names the project's own, for typos. The Variables window offers the described names as one is typed, sets the type of the one chosen, offers its values, shows its help, and says what is wrong under the list without keeping OK from writing. Verify's new checks `var-type` (an error), `var-value`, `var-object` and `var-name`; `mg vars` lists the descriptions and `mg areas --var` takes a described type. * **Update**: [Modules](manual/03-modules.md), [the command line](manual/11-command-line.md) and [the deferred list](deferred.md): The Domains of Dread's builder proposal (C9), a three-way GFF merge usable as git's merge driver. **`mg merge-gff BASE OURS THEIRS`** (git's `%O %A %B`, with `--path %P`) merges two copies of a GFF resource made from a third, as binary GFF or nasher's JSON (told by content: git hands a driver files without their names), and writes the merge over OURS in OURS's form. A value one side changed is taken; two different changes are a conflict named by its path (`/Placeable List[plc_chest "CHEST" at 10, 4.5]/Tag`): exit 1 and nothing written, unless `--prefer ours` or `theirs`. Lists merge by item, by a rule per list (`mg_schema::merge::list_rule`; the engine is `mg_gff::merge`): an area's placed objects by object (the same in every field, then `ObjectId`, then blueprint, tag and position, then the only one left of its blueprint and tag, or of its blueprint and position; both sides' additions kept), `Mod_Area_list` as a union (the base's order, ours' additions, theirs'), `VarTable` by name and type, feats, classes, spells, haks, journal entries and faction pairs by what they are, equipped items by slot, anything else by place. A merge equal to OURS leaves its bytes, one equal to THEIRS is THEIRS's bytes, any other JSON is written as nasher writes it (the project's float places and codepage). The manual's new **Merging in git** has the `.gitattributes` and `.git/config` lines. A test sets up a scratch repository and merges two builders' branches, each adding an object to one area and an area to `module.ifo`, which git alone calls a conflict (the hand-back's measurement). What's left (inventories and conversations merged by place, reordering, strings per language, a conflict file, NWNT) is in the deferred list.

On The Domains of Dread (3 areas, 143 haks, 29.5 GB) 4–5 s and 417 MB: 1,957 of 236,209 hak resources used (427 MB), nothing reaching 125 haks (23 of them holding what is not judged). **Export stamps its base**: `mg export` and File › Export write the module's git commit (and whether files were uncommitted), Moonglow's version and the module's name after the ERF's description (an extra resource would be imported into the module); `mg import` and File › Import show it and warn when the module's checkout is at another commit (older work, other work, a commit it doesn't have). **`MG_Locked` kept out of a nasher project's files**: the window keeps a project's locks in Moonglow's data folder (`locks/`), each found again by list place, blueprint, tag and position, and puts them back on opening and on reading an area changed outside (the files still stand for the area: no false conflict); a file that has the byte keeps it while the object stays locked. Module folders and `.mod` files keep the byte. Held by `a_module_reaches_into_its_haks`, `usage_says_what_the_module_reaches_in_each_hak`, `the_commit_is_stamped_and_compared`, `the_stamp_is_in_the_description`, `a_project_keeps_its_locks_apart` and `a_project_s_locks_stay_out_of_its_files`.

The engine settled that a static placeable is still an object to scripts (found by its tag, its variables read, made Plot), which the client does not show changing (`engine_static_placeables`). **Duplicate tags**: a paste or an area's Copy… that puts a tag on a second object says so and offers **Retag**; by default (`paste_warning = "custom"`, the owner's decision) only of tags a builder set (not the object's blueprint's own) and those that must be unique, never of a static placeable's, so copies of scenery ask nothing (the tag with a number, unique in the module, one undo); `[tags] unique` names tags Verify holds to one object (`tag-unique`). **Setup Store** follows `[store]`: the project's open script (no `openstoreNNN`), the store's tag pattern made unique, the blueprint chosen at first, and the shopkeeper's variable with the store's tag; without it, as Aurora's.

From the Plugins menu or a key it gets the area view's selection, else the palette's. 0.1 to 0.3 plugins run unchanged; `for` under an earlier `api` is refused with the reason. `mg plugin run` takes `--select` and `--open`. ## 2026-10-21
* **Update**: [Scripts](manual/07-scripts.md), [the main window](manual/02-main-window.md), [options](manual/10-options.md) and [the deferred list](deferred.md): El Grillo's three script-editor requests. **Ctrl+S saves the script, not the module** ("When I try to save when editing a script I would expect the script to save, rather than the entire module"): the Save key, while a script editor's text has the keyboard (the rule its Undo and Redo go by), is that script's toolbar Save (its text into the module, compiled with Automatically Compile Scripts on Save, the Compiler tab's note when not), through the keymap, so a Save key chosen in Options › Keyboard does the same; elsewhere, and File › Save always, it saves the module. As in Aurora, whose script editor has its own Save on Ctrl+S (`TdlgScriptEditor`'s `actSave`, the [inventory](parity/aurora-ui-inventory.md)). The manual says what a script's Save writes: no file; File › Save writes the `.mod`, or the script's own file in a module folder or nasher project. **Open Script selects several and opens them together** ("single-click should not open, but just select them"): a click selects, Ctrl+click adds or takes away, Shift+click selects a range, the arrows move the selection (Shift widens it), Open or Enter opens every one selected, each in its tab, and a double click opens that one (`widgets::select_in_list`, the hak editor's rule). Seen in a picture (`open_script_several` in `screens.rs`). **To Scratch for a script that doesn't compile** ("e.g. include scripts"): the source is copied whatever the compiler says, its compiled script only when it compiled just now (not the module's older one), and the Compiler tab says what was copied, that it wasn't compiled (an include file, or the compiler's error) and whether the folder holds an earlier compiled script of the name. Held by `the_save_key_in_a_script_editor_saves_the_script_not_the_module`, `open_script_opens_the_scripts_selected_together` and `a_script_goes_to_the_scratch_folder_compiled`.

Every other item keeps its order and what it does. * **Update**: [Scripts](manual/07-scripts.md), [options](manual/10-options.md) and [the deferred list](deferred.md): Jasperre's report on the script editor, with the owner's decisions. The error found as you type has a line of its own under the toolbar, there with no error too (one line, the whole message on hover), so the text no longer jumps down as an error comes and goes; **Options › Script Editor › Check for errors as you type** turns the check off; the error's own line alone is underlined (tokens of one color are one section over several lines, and the lines around it were underlined too: seen in a picture). Tab puts in four spaces by default, to the next multiple of the width (egui's own tab no longer gets in), or a tab: **Indent with** Spaces or Tabs and **Indent width**; Shift+Tab outdents a step, Tab on several lines indents them (empty lines stay empty). **Background** joins the editor's colors. Help shows a function's documentation as the source has it (`//`, spaces and columns, in the editor's colors and font, then the declaration), from `doc_source` kept beside `doc` in mg-script's spec, outline and analysis. The Compiler tab's messages start with the local time they were said, and a Save that doesn't compile says so there (jiff, a new dependency, reads the time zone). A CRLF script's `\r` was in the editor's text at every line's end, where the cursor stopped and a copy took it ("trailing spaces" on every line): the editor and the read-only view work with plain line ends, and a script is written back with its own (untouched byte for byte; new lines in the file's kind; a file with both kinds keeps the ends around the change), pasted CRLF text included; Rename Symbol and every view of a script's text count positions in the same form. Seen in pictures before and after (`script_error_line`, `script_help`, `options_window` in `screens.rs`) and held by `a_crlf_script_has_no_carriage_returns_in_its_editor`, `a_save_that_does_not_compile_says_so`, `help_shows_documentation_as_the_source_has_it`, `tab_indents_selected_lines_in_the_script_editor` and `script_navigation_definition_references_rename_and_live_errors` (CRLF files, the editor's top before and after an error).
* **Update**: [Blueprints](manual/05-blueprints.md), [journal and factions](manual/08-journal-and-factions.md), [build and test](manual/09-build-and-test.md), [differences from Aurora](manual/12-differences.md), [findings](findings.md), [the GFF notes](research/notes_gff_changelog.md), [the doctor's notes](research/notes_doctor.md) and [the deferred list](deferred.md): Jasperre's two reports. **A placeable's illumination**: the game keeps it in `LightState` (a byte Aurora neither shows nor writes), settled in the engine (`engine_light_state.rs`): read from a placed placeable's GIT entry and from a blueprint created by script, 0 off, any other value on, without the field on; a placeable whose appearance has no light is never lit. A placeable's Advanced page has **Illuminated**, written only when changed (an untouched placeable keeps no field), grayed for an appearance without a light (`mg_rules::placeables`). **No PC faction for objects**: settled in the engine (`engine_factions.rs`), a creature of faction 0, placed or created, is put in Hostile as it loads; a placeable, door or trigger keeps 0 and creatures regard it as they regard players. The faction lists (creatures, placeables, doors, triggers, encounters) and the Store Wizard's leave it out; a file that has it keeps it, shown as "PC (not for objects)" until another is picked; Verify warns of it (`pc-faction`, in the objects group; none in the shipped modules or the game's blueprints). Seen in pictures (`illumination_and_pc_faction` in `screens.rs`); held by `a_placeable_s_illumination_is_written_only_when_changed`, `an_object_s_factions_leave_out_the_pc_faction`, `objects_of_the_pc_faction_are_warned_of` and `verify_warns_of_an_object_of_the_pc_faction`. Drawing the light off, and what is left of faction 0, are in the deferred list. Verify leaves triggers out of `pc-faction` (the owner's decision): Aurora writes faction 0 for a trigger whose blueprint has none.
* **Update**: [Options](manual/10-options.md), [differences from Aurora](manual/12-differences.md) and [the deferred list](deferred.md): El Grillo's question ("is there a way to have Moonglow load userpatch content?"), the owner's decision: **Read userpatch.ini's haks** (Options › General), off by default as in Aurora (Jasperre's ask: a subscribed item or a userpatch hak a builder doesn't want in the module makes a mess); **Read Steam Workshop content**, which was on by default, is off by default too (the setting is now `read_workshop`, read anew: off for everyone until turned on). The haks the user's `userpatch.ini` names (`[Patch]`, `PatchFile000=…`, the highest number winning) are read from the folder `nwn.ini` aliases as `PATCH` (else `patch/` in the user folder), at the game's priority for them: under the module and its haks, over `override/` (`GameInstall::userpatch`, `userpatch_haks`; layers `userpatch:NAME`). Aurora doesn't read them. Verify reports a reference only they satisfy as a warning (`Missing::only_userpatch`: "only in userpatch.ini's haks (players without them won't have it)"; `mg verify --json` has it as `only_userpatch`), and no longer checks their files as the module's custom content. `mg` doesn't read them, as it doesn't read the Workshop. Held by `userpatch_haks_are_read_when_asked_for` and `a_reference_only_a_userpatch_hak_has_is_a_warning`.
* **Update**: [Scripts](manual/07-scripts.md): Sacha's report ("in the script editor, the keys for page up or down do not work"). Page Down and Page Up move the cursor by the lines in sight, in the same column (or at a shorter line's end; past the first line the text's start, past the last its end), and scroll the text as far, so the cursor keeps its place on the screen; with Shift they select. egui's text field has no page keys of its own. Seen in pictures (`script_page_down` in `screens.rs`) and held by `page_keys_move_through_the_script_editor` and `script_tools::line_moved`'s test.
* **Update**: [The shaders proposal](shaders-proposal.md) ("After M5: the lights") and [the deferred list](deferred.md): M5's light-dense water view brought back within the budget with the Shaders switch on, 7.5 to 6.5 ms a frame (off 5.6; area092 zoomed out 5.7–6.1 to 5.2, off 4.0), so M3's rule holds again and the default stays on. The time was the CPU's, writing the game draws' values: a draw's lights built and hashed per draw and its 1,040-byte lights block written an element at a time, 1,524 such blocks a frame. The game's programs now read `lightPosition[i]` and `lightColor[i]` by the draw's places in the frame's lights (`mg_shader`'s `index_lights`, a SPIR-V pass: 144-byte blocks, the same values, zeros past a draw's lights as before); a draw's lights are written as indices, a vector at a time; its model-view matrix worked out once; the light sets hashed eight bytes at a time; the regions indexed by number. `MAX_NUM_LIGHTS` stays the client's 32 (the loops are bounded by `numLights`). The lit oracle and the water area's views are unchanged; area092's at a fixed clock too. Every stock program that reads the lights reads them by index (7 of 65; TDoD's 26 of 102). What is left (0.9 ms of encoding, the places not yet run on Direct3D 12 or Metal) is in the deferred list.
* **Update**: [The shaders proposal](shaders-proposal.md) (M5 built), [the shader notes](research/notes_shaders.md) (§A.3, §A.4 and §J: the special surfaces read in the client), [areas](manual/04-areas.md) and [the deferred list](deferred.md): water, grass, the skybox, additive meshes, decals with an envmap and particles marked in the client (`surfaces_in_the_client`). The skybox (`vsvt`/`fst`, at the far plane), the area's grass (`vsgrass`/`fsgrass`), additive meshes and particles (`vsparticle`/`fsparticle`, by blend) draw with the game's programs; shiny water stays Moonglow's, as `fswater` without the framebuffer draws it opaque and pale (TDoD's fountain 16.4 of 255 from the client against 11.7, a rural lake 19.4 against 12.6). On is as close as off for every surface's region, closer on the grass. See-through game draws are batched (a water-and-fires area 7.9 to 7.5 ms, still over the budget as at M4; area092 6.2 to 5.8). M4's macOS failure fixed: the cube map's level worked out in the shader, not read with gradients.
* **Update**: [The shaders proposal](shaders-proposal.md) (M4 built), [the shader notes](research/notes_shaders.md) (§A.4 settled in the client, §B, §C, §M.10 and §M.12 answered), [areas](manual/04-areas.md), [differences from Aurora](manual/12-differences.md) and [the deferred list](deferred.md): every mesh drawn by the game's shaders with the program the engine chooses and its material's NO_DISCARD, read from the client by marking every stock program in a scratch override (`program_choice_in_the_client`: Moonglow chooses as the client for each of 34 kinds of mesh read). What the engine ignores, Moonglow's own shader now ignores too: `bumpyshinytexture`, maps without a render hint, a DXT1's alpha; every lit mesh reflects the area's map; a tile's `rotatetexture` turns its texture. Moonglow's shader samples the environment map as the game does (`_sm` 0.73 to 0.00 of 255 from the stock programs). A hak's `inc_lighting` changes the area view through the load order (TDoD: 259,475 of 330,000 pixels). Against the client's reference scenes, the switch on is as close as off on the stock scenes and closer on TDoD's room; TDoD's woods seen whole 52 ms on (56 at M3), 28 off.
* **Update**: [The shaders proposal](shaders-proposal.md) (M3 built), [areas](manual/04-areas.md) and [the deferred list](deferred.md): the **🎨 Shaders** switch within the frame budget and **on by default** (`GAME_SHADERS_BY_DEFAULT`; a builder's choice is kept). A program's uniforms are split in IR into a draw's, its lights', the frame's (written once a frame) and the bones'; the game's draws are instances of storage arrays their places pick, as Moonglow's own draws are; the programs are compiled and their pipelines made on a worker thread (an area draws with Moonglow's shader until they are ready) and kept compiled in Moonglow's cache folder. On the campaign's largest area zoomed out, 5.97 ms a frame on (12.37 before M3), 3.97 off; every view within 144 fps off stays within it on. The Domains of Dread's synthetic 24 by 24 area seen whole is over the budget either way (54 ms on, 29 off): in the deferred list. CI's platforms run an authored pair (`an_authored_glsl_pair_draws_on_this_platform_s_gpu`) and print the adapter. With the default on, `frames_at_144` (the campaign's views) has nothing over the budget; the Gallery's first pictures wait for the pipelines (deferred).
* **Update**: [The shaders proposal](shaders-proposal.md) (M2 built), [areas](manual/04-areas.md), [the main window](manual/02-main-window.md), [the shader notes](research/notes_shaders.md) §A.4 and §B.4, and [the deferred list](deferred.md): tier A of the game's shaders. A **🎨 Shaders** switch on the area view's toolbar and in the model viewer (one setting for every 3D view, off by default until M3 meets the frame budget: `GAME_SHADERS_BY_DEFAULT`) draws a mesh whose material names `customshaderVS` and `customshaderFS` with that pair, compiled from the module's load order, and the rest with the stock lit pair; see-through meshes in Moonglow's two parts (the fragment program discards by its alpha in IR), the MTR's parameters filled by name, the clock, and the area's `Flags` and `WindPower` as `areaFlags` and `areaGlobalWind`; tangents made where a model has none (the stock normal-mapped programs drew such a mesh black). A material naming one program alone draws with the stock pair, as the game does (250 of The Domains of Dread's name `fslit_nm` alone as `customshaderVS`); Verify's new `shader-pair` warns of them, and `shader-compile` no longer calls them magenta. A program that fails is drawn with Moonglow's shader and said once in the log. TDoD's grass sways, its fountain's water slides and its roof shader shows a roof by the camera's height, with the switch on only; beside the client, the floor of the reference room under TDoD's `inc_lighting` is 73.4 against the client's 73.5 with the switch on (87.9 off), the fountain differs from the client by 11.7 of 255 on average with the switch on (13.8 off; its shiny water is Moonglow's). What it leaves is in the deferred list.
* **Update**: [The shaders proposal](shaders-proposal.md) (M1 built), [the shader notes](research/notes_shaders.md) §B.4 and [the deferred list](deferred.md): the game's own lit shaders drawn. `Renderer::game_shaders` (off by default, nothing in the UI yet) draws a solid lit mesh with the stock pair the engine would choose (`vslit`/`fslit`, `_nm`, `_sm`, `_sm_nm`; skinned ones too), compiled from the install by `mg-shader`, and the rest, or a pair that fails (reported once), with Moonglow's WGSL shader. The engine's OpenGL matrices are uploaded as they are and `mg-shader` takes the position's depth to wgpu's range in IR (no y flip); vertex inputs are bound by the engine's names from the reflected locations (`vIndex` read from u32 in IR), varyings matched by name, the fragment program's resources in bind group 1, the uniform blocks filled by name from the renderer's values and an MTR's parameters. The WGSL port's first oracle: on plain lit meshes (a textured sphere and ground with an area light, a point light and fog, a tile, a placeable, the skinned wolf) the stock shaders and Moonglow's agree within 1 in 255; where an environment map shows (`_sm`, `_nm`) they differ by up to 15 at the 99th percentile, because the game samples it with the roughness as a bias over the derivatives' level and Moonglow's shader at that level (in the deferred list). The time uniforms read back from the client: `worldtimerTimeOfDay` counts real milliseconds and `sceneCurrentFrame` frames.
* **Update**: [The shaders proposal](shaders-proposal.md) (M0 built), [the architecture](PLAN.md), [build and test](manual/09-build-and-test.md) and [the deferred list](deferred.md): the compiler for the game's own shaders, `mg-shader` (after `mg-image`, so that Verify can use it). A program is assembled as the engine does it (the preamble as a struct of its defines, `#include`s spliced through the load order, each line keeping its file and line), compiled by glslang (glslang-rs: its C++ vendored and built with `cc`, no CMake or network, so the Flatpak builds offline), its combined image samplers split and its inputs and outputs given locations by a pass of Moonglow's on the SPIR-V words (SPIRV-Tools' pass is in `spirv-tools-sys` but not reachable, and a patched copy would be a git dependency the Flatpak refuses; `shaderc` has no relaxed rules), read by naga 30, bound in group 0 and validated, with the uniform block's members, the textures and their samplers, and the varyings by name. Errors name the `.shd` and line glslang's message is at. Unit tests on authored shaders (and bad input as errors, not panics); a corpus test over every stock program and every program in the installed haks (`MOONGLOW_HAKS` adds a builder's): 65 of 65, and 102 of 102 with The Domains of Dread's haks (its 37 and the stock ones over its `inc_lighting`), in 0.7 s. Verify's `shader-compile` check reports a module's programs that don't compile, a stock program broken by a hak's include among them, at the custom file and line. What it leaves out is in the deferred list. The third-party notices carry glslang's own license. CI is green on ubuntu, windows and macos, the Release workflow built the AppImage, the Windows installer and the macOS disk image, and the Flatpak built offline.
* **Update**: [The shaders proposal](shaders-proposal.md) accepted by the owner: the game's shaders for every mesh in 2.0 (tier B, tier A on the way), native glslang and SPIRV-Tools, on by default once the frame budget is met, a program that doesn't compile drawn with Moonglow's own shader and reported by Verify (not magenta), and the `shaders` branch deleted, its note kept in `develop`. [The architecture](PLAN.md) §5.5 says so.
* **Creation**: [The shaders proposal](shaders-proposal.md): the game's own shaders in the area view as Moonglow 2.0's centerpiece. The tabled `shaders` branch's note is brought into develop as [deprecated](research/notes_custom_shaders.md), superseded by the proposal. A spike (`tools/shaders/spike.py`) took all 102 programs on this machine (65 stock, and The Domains of Dread's 37 custom shaders over its own `inc_lighting`) through glslang (`-V -R --amb --aml`), `spirv-opt --split-combined-image-sampler` and naga 30 (bindings renumbered in its IR) to valid shader modules; nothing is drawn yet. Two tiers (custom shaders, then the stock programs throughout), the uniform contract by name, costs (5–9 KB uniform blocks per draw), milestones M0–M6 and five decisions for the owner. The deferred list's two custom-shader entries point to it.
* **Update**: [The deferred list](deferred.md): the Conversation Editor saves a script parameter in the game's codepage, the one it shows it in: a value typed with "é" was saved as UTF-8 (two bytes, shown back as "Ã©"), now as the byte 0xE9, shown back as "é". Parameters are read and written in one place (`dialog::params_in` and `params_value_in`, with a codepage), which the editor and the Ink and Twine exports share.
* **Update**: [Conversations](manual/06-conversations.md) and [the deferred list](deferred.md): dansen9191's report ("script parameters in a conversation are lost on export of a dialogue to Ink"). Condition and action parameters go out to Ink and Twine and are read back with the conversation: after the script's name, `name=value` separated by spaces, quoted where a space is (`# do:a_give item="gold coins"`); a condition's in Ink as a tag naming it (`# if:c_has item=gold`, on the choice, or on its own line before a conditional divert), an NPC line's action in a Twine passage's tags as a query (`do:a_give?item=gold%20coins`); `%`, quotes and what Ink or Twine reads as syntax percent-escaped, so the story stays valid Ink and Twine. Names and values, and the speaker, quest and comment, are read and written in the game's codepage (they were taken as UTF-8). The round trip of every shipped conversation compares the parameters too. Not checked with inklecate (not on this machine). Seen on the way: the Conversation Editor saves the parameters it shows in the game's codepage as UTF-8 (in the deferred list).
* **Update**: [Modules](manual/03-modules.md), [the main window](manual/02-main-window.md) and [the deferred list](deferred.md): dansen9191's reports on the 2DA editor. A column's width is set by dragging the edge at the right of its name, and a double click there fits it to its widest cell; a drag on the rest of the name still moves the column. Widths are kept for the table's name in the settings (between runs), and the resource browser's read-only view of the table shows them too. That view (a game's table, not editable) had no vertical scroll bar in sight: its rows' scroll area was as wide as the table, its bar off at the far right, and the rows' numbers scrolled away sideways. It is now laid out as the editor's grid is: one scroll area for the rows with both bars, the column names and the rows' numbers following it. Each seen in pictures before and after (`table_read_only_and_column_widths` in `screens.rs`: spells.2da read-only, appearance.2da widened and fitted), and held by `a_table_s_column_is_widened_by_the_edge_of_its_name` and `a_game_table_read_only_scrolls` (which finds the scroll bar in the rendered picture, and fails on the old view).
* **Update**: [Blueprints](manual/05-blueprints.md) and [the deferred list](deferred.md): dansen9191's report. An appearance with no model to draw is said where the builder looks: a line in red under a placeable's Appearance Type, a door's appearance, a creature's Appearance and an item's Base Type Name, and in the model's place in the page ("No model: plc_x99 (placeables.2da row 451, ModelName) isn't in the module, its haks or the game"; a row the table lacks, one that names no model, one reserved as `USER`). The page's model kept showing the appearance before when one with no model was chosen (seen in a picture before and after: the chest stayed). The Appearance Gallery frames such rows in red. One rule for it, `mg_rules::appearance`, which the previews, Verify's `object-row` check and the warnings go by; they had differed: the previews had no `USER` rule (they said "no model user"), Verify called a row that names no model one that isn't there, and checked no model for a door without an `Appearance` field or a creature whose row has no `MODELTYPE` (the previews' reading kept: a generic door, a single model). Held by `an_appearance_s_row_must_name_a_model_that_is_there`, `doors_creatures_and_items_by_their_own_tables` and `a_placeable_s_appearance_without_a_model_is_said`; what the rule leaves out is in the deferred list.
* **Update**: [Areas](manual/04-areas.md): builders' asks. Area Properties › Visual lists the lighting schemes in as many columns as the page is wide, every one in sight (Heed's ask: one column, scrolled, left the page's width unused; seen in a picture before and after). Under them, **Copy From Area** gives this area another's Visual settings (lighting, fog, shadows, sky and weather), and **Saved Lighting** keeps them under a name, to give to any area of any module (dansen9191's ask), as files in Moonglow's data folder (`lighting`). Variable sets, prefabs and lighting are kept by one piece of code (`saved.rs`), which the first two had each written.
* **Update**: [Main window](manual/02-main-window.md), [modules](manual/03-modules.md), [areas](manual/04-areas.md) and [the deferred list](deferred.md): the side editors (a hak's, a 2DA's, a tileset's) share one path for their unsaved work, their closing and their Undo, where each had its own (the deferred list's "The side editors' unsaved work, close and undo"). One question for a tab closed with unsaved changes, as the module's asks it (**Save**, **Don't Save**, **Cancel**: they said Discard), with the tabs waiting asked of in turn: Close All with two changed haks asked only of the last. Undo and Redo go through the keymap to the editor under the pointer (the talk table's too) or the 2DA grid that has the keys: Ctrl+Z over a hak's or a tileset's editor undid the module's last change, and the 2DA grid read Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y by hand, so a key set in Options › Keyboard and Ctrl+Shift+Z did not reach it. With the pointer over one of these editors and nothing of its own to undo, nothing is undone (the talk table's fell through to the module's). `side_doc.rs`: the `SideDoc` trait, the one closing window and `Moonglow::local_undo`; held by `closing_two_changed_haks_asks_of_both`, `undo_over_a_hak_editor_is_the_hak_s` and `a_rebound_undo_key_reaches_a_table_s_grid`.
* **Update**: [Differences from Aurora](manual/12-differences.md), [the main window](manual/02-main-window.md), [areas](manual/04-areas.md), [blueprints](manual/05-blueprints.md), [options](manual/10-options.md), [the plugin examples](plugins/README.md) and [the deferred list](deferred.md): the owner's decision. Stores are called Stores everywhere, on purpose unlike Aurora, which says Merchants in some places: the area view's toolbar and its tips, the module tree's group (now in its alphabetical place, after Sounds), Find Instance's kinds, the palettes' **New Store…**, the Script Wizard's **Open a Store** (Aurora's form names it so; its label said Start a Merchant), **Options › Area › Show stores as $ signs**, the manual, and the example plugin (now `store-markup`). One name is left in the code (`ObjectKind::label`; `plural` is gone). * **Update**: [The architecture](PLAN.md) and [the deferred list](deferred.md): the deferred list's "GIT's lists, spelled out about ten times" made one. `mg_rules::ObjectKind` is the nine types of placed object: blueprint type, GIT list and struct id (the generated schema's `git::*_LIST`, not a copy), names, and the fields that name a blueprint, its category and its name; `mg_area::ObjectKind` and `mg_module::palette::BlueprintKind` are that one type, and `verify::Category` takes its nine from it. Through it now: `instances::git_list` and Update Instances (`GIT_LISTS` is gone), references and what satisfies a blueprint's, Rename's kinds, family and a blueprint's own name field, Verify's categories, the content doctor's walk, `mg find`, Advanced Search's places, `mg update-instances`, the 2DA rows' kinds (mg-rules now builds on mg-schema), the area's objects, Find Instance and the Preview window, and Update Instances' window; the eight `if UTM { "ResRef" } else { "TemplateResRef" }` (and five in the corpus tests) are `resref_field`. Nothing shown changed: the one copy that was wrong, Update Instances' window calling an object of a list it doesn't know a "waypoint" where the others say "object", never met one. The window's own tables, and "Stores" against "Merchants", are in the deferred list.
* **Update**: [Blueprints](manual/05-blueprints.md) and [the deferred list](deferred.md): the first of the review's structural unifications. Every list that chooses a row of a table is one widget (`widgets::row_choice`), the blueprint fields' list as its source: a list of more than 12 rows by name (parts, costs and the palette's categories keep their order), a Filter field past 30 that narrows by name or to a row's number, opened at the row chosen, the arrow keys as in Aurora. The "name, else `(n)`" text is `mg_rules::choice_text`, in the level-up wizard, the special abilities and the store's restrictions too.
